concepts.title: Online scheduling as a game
concepts.description:
In an online problem the instance is revealed over time, and a schedule must
be fixed as time passes. A revelation of a problem says, for every time
$t \ge 0$, which instances look the same to the scheduler at time $t$, and
which schedules of two instances have made the same decisions up to time
$t$.

The competitive-ratio game is played by the scheduler and an adversary. The
scheduler chooses an algorithm, a schedule for every instance, which must be
non-anticipative: on two instances that look the same at time $t$ it makes
the same decisions up to time $t$. The adversary then chooses an instance.
For a ratio $\rho$ and an additive constant $\alpha$, the scheduler wins if
its schedule is feasible and costs at most $\rho$ times the cost of every
feasible schedule of the instance, plus $\alpha$; otherwise the adversary
wins. An algorithm with which the scheduler always wins is
$(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive.

A randomized algorithm is a finite probability distribution over
non-anticipative algorithms; it is $(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive if all its
algorithms schedule every instance feasibly and its expected cost is at most
$\rho$ times the cost of every feasible schedule, plus $\alpha$. A
distribution over instances, each with a feasible schedule as witness,
defeats the ratio if every non-anticipative algorithm schedules some instance
of it infeasibly or has positive expected excess, the cost minus $\rho$
times the witness's cost minus $\alpha$.

An embedding of one problem into another is causal for two revelations if
instances that look the same at time $t$ are mapped to instances that look
the same at time $t$, and schedules that made the same decisions up to time
$t$ are translated back to schedules that made the same decisions up to
time $t$.

**Theorem.**

1. The game is determined: the adversary wins against every non-anticipative
   algorithm exactly if the scheduler has no winning algorithm.
2. A deterministic competitive algorithm is a randomized one.
3. (Yao's principle, the direction used for lower bounds.) If a distribution
   over instances defeats a ratio, no randomized algorithm has that ratio.
4. Along a sound causal embedding of $A$ into $B$ and for $\rho \ge 0$, a
   $(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive algorithm for $B$ yields one for $A$, so
   that lower bounds pass from $A$ to $B$.

import Lax434175.Problems

/-!
---
title: Online scheduling as a game
type: theorem
---
In an online problem the instance is revealed over time, and a schedule must
be fixed as time passes. A revelation of a problem says, for every time
$t \ge 0$, which instances look the same to the scheduler at time $t$, and
which schedules of two instances have made the same decisions up to time
$t$.

The competitive-ratio game is played by the scheduler and an adversary. The
scheduler chooses an algorithm, a schedule for every instance, which must be
non-anticipative: on two instances that look the same at time $t$ it makes
the same decisions up to time $t$. The adversary then chooses an instance.
For a ratio $\rho$ and an additive constant $\alpha$, the scheduler wins if
its schedule is feasible and costs at most $\rho$ times the cost of every
feasible schedule of the instance, plus $\alpha$; otherwise the adversary
wins. An algorithm with which the scheduler always wins is
$(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive.

A randomized algorithm is a finite probability distribution over
non-anticipative algorithms; it is $(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive if all its
algorithms schedule every instance feasibly and its expected cost is at most
$\rho$ times the cost of every feasible schedule, plus $\alpha$. A
distribution over instances, each with a feasible schedule as witness,
defeats the ratio if every non-anticipative algorithm schedules some instance
of it infeasibly or has positive expected excess, the cost minus $\rho$
times the witness's cost minus $\alpha$.

An embedding of one problem into another is causal for two revelations if
instances that look the same at time $t$ are mapped to instances that look
the same at time $t$, and schedules that made the same decisions up to time
$t$ are translated back to schedules that made the same decisions up to
time $t$.

**Theorem.**

1. The game is determined: the adversary wins against every non-anticipative
   algorithm exactly if the scheduler has no winning algorithm.
2. A deterministic competitive algorithm is a randomized one.
3. (Yao's principle, the direction used for lower bounds.) If a distribution
   over instances defeats a ratio, no randomized algorithm has that ratio.
4. Along a sound causal embedding of $A$ into $B$ and for $\rho \ge 0$, a
   $(\rho, \alpha)$-competitive algorithm for $B$ yields one for $A$, so
   that lower bounds pass from $A$ to $B$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Online
open Lax434175.Problems

/-- How the instances of a problem are revealed over time. -/
structure Revelation (P : Problem) where
  /-- The two instances look the same to the scheduler at time `t`. -/
  same : P.Inst → P.Inst → NNRat → Prop
  /-- Two schedules of two instances made the same decisions up to time `t`. -/
  agree : (x y : P.Inst) → P.Sched x → P.Sched y → NNRat → Prop

variable {P : Problem}

/-- A deterministic algorithm: a schedule for every instance. -/
abbrev Algorithm (P : Problem) := (x : P.Inst) → P.Sched x

/-- The algorithm decides up to time `t` only from what is revealed at `t`. -/
def NonAnticipative (R : Revelation P) (A : Algorithm P) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y t, R.same x y t → R.agree x y (A x) (A y) t

/-- The scheduler wins on every instance: a feasible schedule costing at most
`ρ` times every feasible schedule, plus `α`. -/
def Competitive (A : Algorithm P) (ρ α : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, P.feasible x (A x) ∧ ∀ σ, P.feasible x σ → P.cost x (A x) ≤ ρ * P.cost x σ + α

/-- The scheduler has a winning strategy. -/
def SchedulerWins (R : Revelation P) (ρ α : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, NonAnticipative R A ∧ Competitive A ρ α

/-- The adversary beats every non-anticipative algorithm. -/
def AdversaryWins (R : Revelation P) (ρ α : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A, NonAnticipative R A → ∃ x, ¬ P.feasible x (A x) ∨
    ∃ σ, P.feasible x σ ∧ ρ * P.cost x σ + α < P.cost x (A x)

/-- A finite probability distribution over non-anticipative algorithms. -/
structure Randomized (R : Revelation P) where
  algorithms : List (ℚ × Algorithm P)
  nonneg : ∀ a ∈ algorithms, 0 ≤ a.1
  total : (algorithms.map Prod.fst).sum = 1
  nonAnticipative : ∀ a ∈ algorithms, NonAnticipative R a.2

/-- The expected cost of a randomized algorithm on an instance. -/
def Randomized.cost {R : Revelation P} (μ : Randomized R) (x : P.Inst) : ℚ :=
  (μ.algorithms.map fun a => a.1 * P.cost x (a.2 x)).sum

def Randomized.Competitive {R : Revelation P} (μ : Randomized R) (ρ α : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, (∀ a ∈ μ.algorithms, P.feasible x (a.2 x)) ∧
    ∀ σ, P.feasible x σ → μ.cost x ≤ ρ * P.cost x σ + α

/-- A finite distribution over instances, each with a feasible witness
schedule. -/
structure Hard (P : Problem) where
  instances : List (ℚ × (x : P.Inst) × P.Sched x)
  nonneg : ∀ a ∈ instances, 0 ≤ a.1
  feasible : ∀ a ∈ instances, P.feasible a.2.1 a.2.2

/-- The expected excess of an algorithm over `ρ` times the witnesses plus `α`. -/
def Hard.excess (H : Hard P) (A : Algorithm P) (ρ α : ℚ) : ℚ :=
  (H.instances.map fun a => a.1 * (P.cost a.2.1 (A a.2.1) - ρ * P.cost a.2.1 a.2.2 - α)).sum

/-- The distribution defeats the ratio: every non-anticipative algorithm
schedules one of its instances infeasibly or has positive expected excess. -/
def Hard.Defeats (H : Hard P) (R : Revelation P) (ρ α : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A, NonAnticipative R A → (∃ a ∈ H.instances, ¬ P.feasible a.2.1 (A a.2.1)) ∨
    0 < H.excess A ρ α

/-- The embedding respects what is revealed and what is decided. -/
structure Causal {A B : Problem} (RA : Revelation A) (RB : Revelation B)
    (e : Embedding A B) : Prop where
  same : ∀ x y t, RA.same x y t → RB.same (e.map x) (e.map y) t
  agree : ∀ x y τ τ' t, RB.agree (e.map x) (e.map y) τ τ' t →
    RA.agree x y (e.back x τ) (e.back y τ') t

axiom adversaryWins_iff (R : Revelation P) (ρ α : ℚ) :
    AdversaryWins R ρ α ↔ ¬ SchedulerWins R ρ α

axiom randomized_of_competitive (R : Revelation P) {A : Algorithm P} {ρ α : ℚ}
    (hA : NonAnticipative R A) (hc : Competitive A ρ α) :
    ∃ μ : Randomized R, μ.Competitive ρ α

axiom yao (R : Revelation P) (H : Hard P) {ρ α : ℚ} (hH : H.Defeats R ρ α) :
    ¬ ∃ μ : Randomized R, μ.Competitive ρ α

axiom schedulerWins_of_embedding {A B : Problem} {RA : Revelation A} {RB : Revelation B}
    {e : Embedding A B} (he : e.Sound) (hc : Causal RA RB e) {ρ α : ℚ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    SchedulerWins RB ρ α → SchedulerWins RA ρ α

axiom adversaryWins_of_embedding {A B : Problem} {RA : Revelation A} {RB : Revelation B}
    {e : Embedding A B} (he : e.Sound) (hc : Causal RA RB e) {ρ α : ℚ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    AdversaryWins RA ρ α → AdversaryWins RB ρ α

end Lax434175.Online

statements.signature:
adversaryWins_iff : ∀ {P : Lax434175.Problems.Problem} (R : Lax434175.Online.Revelation P) (ρ α : Rat),
  Iff (Lax434175.Online.AdversaryWins R ρ α) (Not (Lax434175.Online.SchedulerWins R ρ α))

adversaryWins_of_embedding : ∀ {A B : Lax434175.Problems.Problem} {RA : Lax434175.Online.Revelation A} {RB : Lax434175.Online.Revelation B}
  {e : Lax434175.Problems.Embedding A B},
  e.Sound →
    Lax434175.Online.Causal RA RB e →
      ∀ {ρ α : Rat}, Rat.instLE.le 0 ρ → Lax434175.Online.AdversaryWins RA ρ α → Lax434175.Online.AdversaryWins RB ρ α

randomized_of_competitive : ∀ {P : Lax434175.Problems.Problem} (R : Lax434175.Online.Revelation P) {A : Lax434175.Online.Algorithm P} {ρ α : Rat},
  Lax434175.Online.NonAnticipative R A → Lax434175.Online.Competitive A ρ α → Exists fun μ => μ.Competitive ρ α

  {e : Lax434175.Problems.Embedding A B},
  e.Sound →
    Lax434175.Online.Causal RA RB e →
      ∀ {ρ α : Rat}, Rat.instLE.le 0 ρ → Lax434175.Online.SchedulerWins RB ρ α → Lax434175.Online.SchedulerWins RA ρ α

  H.Defeats R ρ α → Not (Exists fun μ => μ.Competitive ρ α)

concepts.title: Scheduling with operations
concepts.description:
An instance has $n$ jobs and $m$ machines. Every job consists of a sequence
of operations, and an operation $o$ needs time $p_{oi}$ on machine $i$; when
it occupies a set of machines, it needs the largest of these times. Every job
has a release date. Parallel machines are the case of one operation per job,
and shops the case in which the time of an operation does not depend on the
machine.

A schedule is a finite list of pieces. A piece processes one operation on a
nonempty set of machines during an interval given by a start time and a
length, both nonnegative rational numbers. A schedule is feasible for the
kernel if two different pieces that belong to the same job or share a
machine are disjoint in time. An operation starts when its first piece
starts and completes when its last piece ends; a job starts when its first
piece starts and completes when its last piece ends.

The fields are those of parallel machines and of shops, read per operation:

- interruption, per operation: none (one full piece starting at an integral
  time), restarts, preemption (the fractions of its pieces sum to $1$, or a
  piece is on machines on which it needs time $0$), or preemption without
  migration (preemption, and all its pieces occupy the same set of
  machines);
- job structure: one operation per job, or the open, flow, job and two-stage
  flexible flow shop;
- machine environment and processing times, over the times $p_{oi}$;
- machines: the values of the machine-set field of parallel machines, which
  restrict every operation of a job alike, and those of the machine field of
  shops, which restrict every operation separately; a value of the first kind
  is a special case of the second kind where the second kind can express it;
- numbers of machines and of jobs, release dates, deadlines, precedence
  constraints, communication delays, forbidden times and the input encoding,
  as for parallel machines;
- server, no-wait, transportation delays, no-idle and batch setups, as for
  shops.

**Theorem.** The fields are sound, and every job starts no later than it
completes.

import Lax434175.ParallelMachines
import Lax434175.Interruption
import Lax434175.MachineSets
import Lax434175.ShopFamily

/-!
---
title: Scheduling with operations
type: theorem
---
An instance has $n$ jobs and $m$ machines. Every job consists of a sequence
of operations, and an operation $o$ needs time $p_{oi}$ on machine $i$; when
it occupies a set of machines, it needs the largest of these times. Every job
has a release date. Parallel machines are the case of one operation per job,
and shops the case in which the time of an operation does not depend on the
machine.

A schedule is a finite list of pieces. A piece processes one operation on a
nonempty set of machines during an interval given by a start time and a
length, both nonnegative rational numbers. A schedule is feasible for the
kernel if two different pieces that belong to the same job or share a
machine are disjoint in time. An operation starts when its first piece
starts and completes when its last piece ends; a job starts when its first
piece starts and completes when its last piece ends.

The fields are those of parallel machines and of shops, read per operation:

- interruption, per operation: none (one full piece starting at an integral
  time), restarts, preemption (the fractions of its pieces sum to $1$, or a
  piece is on machines on which it needs time $0$), or preemption without
  migration (preemption, and all its pieces occupy the same set of
  machines);
- job structure: one operation per job, or the open, flow, job and two-stage
  flexible flow shop;
- machine environment and processing times, over the times $p_{oi}$;
- machines: the values of the machine-set field of parallel machines, which
  restrict every operation of a job alike, and those of the machine field of
  shops, which restrict every operation separately; a value of the first kind
  is a special case of the second kind where the second kind can express it;
- numbers of machines and of jobs, release dates, deadlines, precedence
  constraints, communication delays, forbidden times and the input encoding,
  as for parallel machines;
- server, no-wait, transportation delays, no-idle and batch setups, as for
  shops.

**Theorem.** The fields are sound, and every job starts no later than it
completes.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Operations
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175

structure Inst where
  jobs : ℕ
  machines : ℕ
  /-- The number of operations of a job. -/
  ops : Fin jobs → ℕ
  /-- The time an operation needs on a machine. -/
  p : (j : Fin jobs) → Fin (ops j) → Fin machines → ℕ
  /-- The release date of a job. -/
  r : Fin jobs → ℕ

/-- An operation: a job and a position in its sequence. -/
abbrev Op (x : Inst) := (j : Fin x.jobs) × Fin (x.ops j)

/-- The time an operation needs when it occupies a set of machines. -/
def duration (x : Inst) (o : Op x) (S : Finset (Fin x.machines)) : ℕ :=
  S.sup (x.p o.1 o.2)

/-- The shop instance with the jobs, machines and operations of an instance. -/
abbrev Inst.toShop (x : Inst) : Shops.Inst := ⟨x.jobs, x.machines, x.ops, fun _ _ => 0, x.r⟩

/-- The parallel-machine instance with the jobs and machines of an instance. -/
abbrev Inst.toPar (x : Inst) : ParallelMachines.Inst := ⟨x.jobs, x.machines, fun _ _ => 0, x.r⟩

/-- An operation is processed on a set of machines from `start` for `length`
time units. -/
structure Piece (x : Inst) where
  op : Op x
  machines : Finset (Fin x.machines)
  start : NNRat
  length : NNRat

/-- The time at which a piece ends. -/
def Piece.finish {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : NNRat := q.start + q.length

structure Sched (x : Inst) where
  pieces : List (Piece x)

/-- The pieces of an operation. -/
def piecesOf {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : List (Piece x) :=
  σ.pieces.filter (fun q => decide (q.op = o))

/-- The pieces of a job. -/
def piecesOfJob {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : List (Piece x) :=
  σ.pieces.filter (fun q => decide (q.op.1 = j))

/-- Two pieces do not overlap in time. -/
def Apart {x : Inst} (a b : Piece x) : Prop :=
  a.finish ≤ b.start ∨ b.finish ≤ a.start

/-- The start of the first piece of an operation. -/
def opStart {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0

/-- The end of the last piece of an operation. -/
def opFinish {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The fraction of an operation that a schedule completes. -/
def fraction (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : NNRat :=
  ((piecesOf σ o).map (fun q => q.length / (duration x o q.machines : NNRat))).sum

/-- Every piece occupies some machine, and two different pieces that belong to
the same job or share a machine do not overlap. -/
def feasible {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, q.machines.Nonempty) ∧
  σ.pieces.Pairwise (fun a b => (a.op.1 = b.op.1 ∨ ¬ Disjoint a.machines b.machines) → Apart a b)

/-- The kernel of scheduling with operations. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := Sched
  feasible _ σ := feasible σ
  start _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0
  completion _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The number of machines, a parameter of the kernel. -/
def machines : kernel.Inst → ℕ := Inst.machines

-- Interruption

/-- A piece processes its operation entirely. -/
def Complete {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : Prop :=
  q.length = (duration x q.op q.machines : NNRat)

/-- The schedules that respect a way of interruption. -/
def holds : Interruption.Mode → (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  | .none, x, σ => ∀ o : Op x, ∃ q, piecesOf σ o = [q] ∧
      q.length = (duration x o q.machines : NNRat) ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, q.start = (n : NNRat)
  | .restarts, _, σ => ∀ o, ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, Complete q ∧
      ∀ q' ∈ piecesOf σ o, q'.finish ≤ q.finish ∧ (Complete q' → q'.finish = q.finish)
  | .pmtn, x, σ => ∀ o, fraction x σ o = 1 ∨ ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, duration x o q.machines = 0
  | .pmtnNoMigration, x, σ => ∀ o,
      (fraction x σ o = 1 ∨ ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, duration x o q.machines = 0) ∧
        ∀ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, ∀ q' ∈ piecesOf σ o, q.machines = q'.machines

/-- The interruption field. -/
def interruption : Module kernel where
  Value := Interruption.Mode
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := holds v x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

-- Job structure

inductive Structure
  | single
  | open
  | flow
  | job
  | flexibleFlow
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The instances of a job structure. -/
def Structure.holds : Structure → Inst → Prop
  | .single, x => ∀ j, x.ops j = 1
  | .open, x => ∀ j, x.ops j = x.machines
  | .flow, x => ∀ j, x.ops j = x.machines
  | .job, _ => True
  | .flexibleFlow, x => ∀ j, x.ops j = 2

/-- The operations of every job are processed in their given order. -/
def InOrder (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k k' : Fin (x.ops j)), k < k' → opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, k'⟩

/-- The order a job structure imposes on the operations of a job. -/
def Structure.ordered : Structure → (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  | .single, _, _ => True
  | .open, _, _ => True
  | .flow, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .job, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .flexibleFlow, x, σ => InOrder x σ

def Structure.le : Structure → Structure → Bool
  | .single, .job | .flow, .job | .flexibleFlow, .job => true
  | v, w => decide (v = w)

/-- The job-structure field. -/
def jobStructure : Module kernel where
  Value := Structure
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits v x _ := v.holds x
  constraint v x _ σ := v.ordered x σ
  le := Structure.le
  embed _ _ _ := ()

-- Machine environment and processing times

/-- The instances of a machine environment. -/
def environmentHolds : ParallelMachines.Environment → Inst → Prop
  | .identical, x => ∀ (o : Op x) i i', x.p o.1 o.2 i = x.p o.1 o.2 i'
  | .uniform, x => ∃ (q : Op x → ℕ) (s : Fin x.machines → ℕ),
      ∀ (o : Op x) i, 0 < s i ∧ x.p o.1 o.2 i * s i = q o
  | .unrelated, _ => True

/-- The machine-environment field. -/
def environment : Module kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ParallelMachines.Environment (fun v x => environmentHolds v x)
    (fun v w => decide (v.rank ≤ w.rank))

/-- The instances of a processing-time restriction. -/
def processingTimesHolds : ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes → Inst → Prop
  | .unit, x => ∀ (o : Op x) i, x.p o.1 o.2 i = 1
  | .equal, x => ∃ p, ∀ (o : Op x) i, x.p o.1 o.2 i = p
  | .oneOrTwo, x => ∀ (o : Op x) i, x.p o.1 o.2 i = 1 ∨ x.p o.1 o.2 i = 2
  | .arbitrary, _ => True

/-- The processing-time field. -/
def processingTimes : Module kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes (fun v x => processingTimesHolds v x)
    ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes.le

-- Machines

/-- A value of the machine field: a machine-set value of parallel machines,
which restricts every operation of a job alike, or a machine value of shops. -/
inductive Machines
  | par (v : MachineSets.Value)
  | shop (v : Shops.Machines)

/-- The data of a value. -/
def Machines.Data : Machines → Inst → Type
  | .par v, x => MachineSets.Data v x.toPar
  | .shop v, x => Shops.Machines.Data v x.toShop

/-- Whether an operation may occupy a set of machines. -/
def Machines.view {x : Inst} : (v : Machines) → v.Data x → Op x → Finset (Fin x.machines) → Prop
  | .par v, d => fun o S => MachineSets.view (x := x.toPar) v d o.1 S
  | .shop v, d => fun o S => Shops.Machines.view (x := x.toShop) v d o.1 o.2 S

/-- The condition on the data. -/
def Machines.admits {x : Inst} : (v : Machines) → v.Data x → Prop
  | .par _, _ => True
  | .shop v, d => Shops.Machines.admits (x := x.toShop) v d

/-- Which machine-set values of parallel machines are special cases of which
machine values of shops. -/
def crossLe : MachineSets.Value → Shops.Machines → Bool
  | .none, .sets | .sets, .sets | .fix, .fix => true
  | _, .general => true
  | _, _ => false

def Machines.le : Machines → Machines → Bool
  | .par v, .par w => MachineSets.le v w
  | .shop v, .shop w => Shops.Machines.le v w
  | .par v, .shop w => crossLe v w
  | .shop _, .par _ => false

/-- Machine-set data of parallel machines read as machine data of shops. -/
def crossEmbed : (v : MachineSets.Value) → (w : Shops.Machines) → crossLe v w = true →
    (x : Inst) → MachineSets.Data v x.toPar → Shops.Machines.Data w x.toShop
  | .none, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .none, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .none, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .none, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .none, .sets, _, _, _ => fun _ _ _ => True
  | .none, .fix, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .none, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .none M j S
  | .sets, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sets, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sets, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sets, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sets, .sets, _, _, M => fun j _ i => M j i
  | .sets, .fix, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sets, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .sets M j S
  | .fix, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .fix, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .fix, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .fix, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .fix, .sets, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .fix, .fix, _, _, M => fun j _ => M j
  | .fix, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .fix M j S
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .sets, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .fix, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .sizeOneOrAll, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .sizeOneOrAll M j S
  | .size, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .sets, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .fix, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .size, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .size M j S
  | .general, .byPosition, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .dedicated, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .recirculation, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .stages, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .sets, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .fix, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true
  | .general, .general, _, _, M => fun j _ S => MachineSets.view .general M j S

def Machines.embed : {v w : Machines} → Machines.le v w = true → (x : Inst) →
    v.Data x → w.Data x
  | .par _, .par _, h, x, d => MachineSets.embed h x.toPar d
  | .shop _, .shop _, h, x, d => Shops.Machines.embed h x.toShop d
  | .par v, .shop w, h, x, d => crossEmbed v w h x d
  | .shop _, .par _, h, _, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true

/-- The machine field. -/
def machineSets : Module kernel where
  Value := Machines
  Data := Machines.Data
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v _ d σ := ∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, v.view d q.op q.machines
  le := Machines.le
  embed := Machines.embed

-- Fields of parallel machines read per job

/-- Scheduling with operations as a machine model on parallel machines: a job
occupies a set of machines if one of its pieces does. -/
def model : ParallelMachines.Model where
  kernel := kernel
  inst x := x.toPar
  jobs_eq _ := rfl
  uses _ σ j S := ∃ q ∈ piecesOfJob σ j, q.machines = S

-- Fields of shops

/-- A piece of one operation and a piece of another share a machine. -/
def Shares {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (a b : Op x) : Prop :=
  ∃ qa ∈ piecesOf σ a, ∃ qb ∈ piecesOf σ b, ¬ Disjoint qa.machines qb.machines

/-- The server field: every operation needs a setup. -/
def server : Module kernel where
  Value := Servers.Value
  Data v x := Servers.Data (Op x) v
  admits v _ d := Servers.Admits v d
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ s, Servers.view v d = some s →
    Servers.Served (fun o : Op x => (opStart σ o : ℚ)) (fun o => (opFinish σ o : ℚ))
      (Servers.setupRelease (fun o : Op x => (opStart σ o : ℚ))
        (fun o => (kernel.start x σ o.1 : ℚ)) (fun o => (x.r o.1 : ℚ)))
      (Shares σ) s
  le := Servers.le
  embed h _ d := Servers.embed h d

/-- The time an operation needs on the first machine; for shops, where the
time does not depend on the machine, its processing time. Without machines no
operation can be processed, and the time is taken to be `1`. -/
def opTime (x : Inst) (o : Op x) : ℕ :=
  if h : 0 < x.machines then x.p o.1 o.2 ⟨0, h⟩ else 1

/-- The no-wait field. -/
def noWait : Module kernel where
  Value := Shops.NoWait
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v = .noWait →
    ∀ j, kernel.completion x σ j = kernel.start x σ j + ∑ k, (opTime x ⟨j, k⟩ : NNRat)
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- Of two operations of a job, the later one waits for the delay, unless both
delays between them are `0`. -/
def Delayed (x : Inst) (t : Transportation.Delays x.toShop) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), k ≠ l → (t j k l = 0 ∧ t j l k = 0) ∨
    opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ + (t j k l : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, l⟩ ∨
    opFinish σ ⟨j, l⟩ + (t j l k : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, k⟩

/-- The machines that the pieces of an operation occupy. -/
def opMachines {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : Finset (Fin x.machines) :=
  ((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.machines).foldr (· ∪ ·) ∅

/-- A single robot carries every job from each operation to the next, and
between two transports it travels empty from the machines where it delivers
the one to the machines where it picks up the other. -/
def Carried (x : Inst) (t : Transportation.Delays x.toShop)
    (e : Transportation.EmptyMoves x.toShop) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∃ depart : (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ,
    (∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ (depart j k : NNRat) ∧
        ((depart j k + t j k l : ℕ) : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, l⟩) ∧
    ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)) j' (k' l' : Fin (x.ops j')), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      l'.val = k'.val + 1 → (⟨j, k⟩ : Op x) ≠ ⟨j', k'⟩ →
      depart j k + t j k l +
          Transportation.emptyTime e (opMachines σ ⟨j, l⟩) (opMachines σ ⟨j', k'⟩) ≤
        depart j' k' ∨
      depart j' k' + t j' k' l' +
          Transportation.emptyTime e (opMachines σ ⟨j', l'⟩) (opMachines σ ⟨j, k⟩) ≤
        depart j k

/-- The field of transportation delays. -/
def transportation : Module kernel where
  Value := Transportation.Value
  Data _ x := Transportation.Data x.toShop
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v x d σ := Delayed x d.1 σ ∧ (v.robot = true → Carried x d.1 d.2 σ)
  le := Transportation.Value.le
  embed _ _ d := d

/-- A piece of an operation occupies a machine. -/
def Occupies {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) (i : Fin x.machines) : Prop :=
  ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, i ∈ q.machines

/-- Every operation on a machine is immediately followed by another one on
that machine, unless none completes later. -/
def Contiguous (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ i (a : Op x), Occupies σ a i →
    (∃ b : Op x, b ≠ a ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧ opStart σ b = opFinish σ a) ∨
    ∀ b : Op x, Occupies σ b i → opFinish σ b ≤ opFinish σ a

/-- The no-idle field. -/
def noIdle : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopExtras.NoIdle
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v = .noIdle → Contiguous x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- On some machine, operation `b` follows operation `a`: `b` starts after `a`
completes, and no other operation on that machine lies in between. -/
def Follows {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (a b : Op x) : Prop :=
  opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ b ∧ ∃ i, Occupies σ a i ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧
    ∀ c : Op x, c ≠ a → c ≠ b → Occupies σ c i →
      ¬ (opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ c ∧ opFinish σ c ≤ opStart σ b)

/-- The batch-setup field. -/
def batchSetups : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopExtras.BatchSetups
  Data v x := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.Data v x.toShop
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ a b : Op x,
    v.batch (x := x.toShop) d a.1 ≠ v.batch (x := x.toShop) d b.1 →
    (Shares σ a b → opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ b ∨ opFinish σ b ≤ opStart σ a) ∧
    (Follows σ a b → opFinish σ a + (v.setup (x := x.toShop) d (v.batch (x := x.toShop) d a.1)
        (v.batch (x := x.toShop) d b.1) : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ b)
  le := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.le
  embed h x d := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.embed h x.toShop d

axiom interruption_sound : interruption.Sound
axiom jobStructure_sound : jobStructure.Sound
axiom environment_sound : environment.Sound
axiom processingTimes_sound : processingTimes.Sound
axiom machineSets_sound : machineSets.Sound
axiom server_sound : server.Sound
axiom noWait_sound : noWait.Sound
axiom transportation_sound : transportation.Sound
axiom noIdle_sound : noIdle.Sound
axiom batchSetups_sound : batchSetups.Sound

concepts.title: One family for parallel machines and shops
concepts.description:
The problems on parallel machines and the shop problems form one family over
scheduling with operations, with the fields of scheduling with operations and
the completion-time objectives.

A problem of the family of parallel machines determines the problem of this
family with one operation per job, the same values in the fields of parallel
machines, its machine-set value as a value of the machine field, and the
value none in the fields of shops. A shop problem determines the problem with
its shop type as job structure, identical machines, its machine value, its
processing-time value, the same values in the fields of shops, and the value
none in the fields of parallel machines.

**Theorem.** In both cases the two problems are special cases of each other.
In the family, a specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another, directly or through flow time, describes a problem
whose decision version reduces to that of the other.

import Lax434175.Operations
import Lax434175.ParallelFamily

/-!
---
title: One family for parallel machines and shops
type: theorem
---
The problems on parallel machines and the shop problems form one family over
scheduling with operations, with the fields of scheduling with operations and
the completion-time objectives.

A problem of the family of parallel machines determines the problem of this
family with one operation per job, the same values in the fields of parallel
machines, its machine-set value as a value of the machine field, and the
value none in the fields of shops. A shop problem determines the problem with
its shop type as job structure, identical machines, its machine value, its
processing-time value, the same values in the fields of shops, and the value
none in the fields of parallel machines.

**Theorem.** In both cases the two problems are special cases of each other.
In the family, a specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another, directly or through flow time, describes a problem
whose decision version reduces to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.OperationsFamily
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Operations

/-- The fields of the family. -/
inductive FieldName
  | interruption
  | jobStructure
  | environment
  | machineCount
  | jobCount
  | processingTimes
  | machineSets
  | releaseDates
  | deadlines
  | precedence
  | communicationDelays
  | server
  | forbiddenTimes
  | encoding
  | noWait
  | transportation
  | noIdle
  | batchSetups
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.interruption, .jobStructure, .environment, .machineCount, .jobCount,
    .processingTimes, .machineSets, .releaseDates, .deadlines, .precedence,
    .communicationDelays, .server, .forbiddenTimes, .encoding, .noWait, .transportation,
    .noIdle, .batchSetups}
  complete x := by cases x <;> decide

/-- The problems on parallel machines and in shops. -/
abbrev family : Family Operations.kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .interruption => Operations.interruption
    | .jobStructure => Operations.jobStructure
    | .environment => Operations.environment
    | .machineCount => Counts.module _ Operations.machines 1
    | .jobCount => Counts.module _ Operations.kernel.jobs
    | .processingTimes => Operations.processingTimes
    | .machineSets => Operations.machineSets
    | .releaseDates => ReleaseDates.module _
    | .deadlines => Deadlines.module _
    | .precedence => Precedence.module _ Operations.machines
    | .communicationDelays => CommunicationDelays.module Operations.model
    | .server => Operations.server
    | .forbiddenTimes => ForbiddenTimes.module _
    | .encoding => ForbiddenTimes.encoding _
    | .noWait => Operations.noWait
    | .transportation => Operations.transportation
    | .noIdle => Operations.noIdle
    | .batchSetups => Operations.batchSetups

instance : Fintype family.ModuleName :=
  inferInstanceAs (Fintype FieldName)

/-- The specification `α | β | γ`. -/
def spec (interruption : Interruption.Mode := .none)
    (shopType : Structure := .single)
    (environment : ParallelMachines.Environment := .identical)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (processingTimes : ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (machineSets : Machines := .par .none)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (communicationDelays : CommunicationDelays.Value := .none)
    (server : Servers.Value := .none)
    (forbiddenTimes : ForbiddenTimes.Value := .none)
    (encoding : ForbiddenTimes.Encoding := .standard)
    (waiting : Shops.NoWait := .none)
    (transportation : Transportation.Value := .none)
    (idling : ShopExtras.NoIdle := .none)
    (setups : ShopExtras.BatchSetups := .none)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => interruption
    | .jobStructure => shopType
    | .environment => environment
    | .machineCount => machineCount
    | .jobCount => jobCount
    | .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .machineSets => machineSets
    | .releaseDates => release
    | .deadlines => deadline
    | .precedence => precedence
    | .communicationDelays => communicationDelays
    | .server => server
    | .forbiddenTimes => forbiddenTimes
    | .encoding => encoding
    | .noWait => waiting
    | .transportation => transportation
    | .noIdle => idling
    | .batchSetups => setups
  objective := objective

/-- The job structure of a shop type. -/
def ofShopType : Shops.ShopType → Structure
  | .open => .open
  | .flow => .flow
  | .job => .job
  | .flexibleFlow => .flexibleFlow

/-- The processing-time value of a shop value. -/
def ofShopTimes : Shops.ProcessingTimes → ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes
  | .unit => .unit
  | .equal => .equal
  | .arbitrary => .arbitrary

/-- The specification of the family with the values of a problem on parallel
machines. -/
def ofParallel (s : Spec ParallelFamily.family) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => s.module .interruption
    | .jobStructure => Structure.single
    | .environment => s.module (.field .environment)
    | .machineCount => s.module (.field .machineCount)
    | .jobCount => s.module (.field .jobCount)
    | .processingTimes => s.module (.field .processingTimes)
    | .machineSets => Machines.par (s.module (.field .machineSets))
    | .releaseDates => s.module (.field .releaseDates)
    | .deadlines => s.module (.field .deadlines)
    | .precedence => s.module (.field .precedence)
    | .communicationDelays => s.module (.field .communicationDelays)
    | .server => s.module (.field .server)
    | .forbiddenTimes => s.module (.field .forbiddenTimes)
    | .encoding => s.module (.field .encoding)
    | .noWait => Shops.NoWait.none
    | .transportation => Transportation.Value.none
    | .noIdle => ShopExtras.NoIdle.none
    | .batchSetups => ShopExtras.BatchSetups.none
  objective := s.objective

/-- The specification of the family with the values of a shop problem. -/
def ofShop (s : Spec ShopFamily.family) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => s.module .interruption
    | .jobStructure => ofShopType (s.module (.field .shopType))
    | .environment => ParallelMachines.Environment.identical
    | .machineCount => s.module (.field .machineCount)
    | .jobCount => s.module (.field .jobCount)
    | .processingTimes => ofShopTimes (s.module (.field .processingTimes))
    | .machineSets => Machines.shop (s.module (.field .machineSets))
    | .releaseDates => s.module (.field .releaseDates)
    | .deadlines => s.module (.field .deadlines)
    | .precedence => s.module (.field .precedence)
    | .communicationDelays => CommunicationDelays.Value.none
    | .server => s.module (.field .server)
    | .forbiddenTimes => ForbiddenTimes.Value.none
    | .encoding => ForbiddenTimes.Encoding.standard
    | .noWait => s.module (.field .noWait)
    | .transportation => s.module (.field .transportation)
    | .noIdle => s.module (.field .noIdle)
    | .batchSetups => s.module (.field .batchSetups)
  objective := s.objective

axiom parallel_faithful (s : Spec ParallelFamily.family) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofParallel s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofParallel s)) (problem _ s)

axiom shop_faithful (s : Spec ShopFamily.family) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofShop s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofShop s)) (problem _ s)

axiom family_sound : family.Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le {s t : Spec family} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reducesThroughFlow {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.ReducesThroughFlow s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.OperationsFamily

parallel_faithful : ∀ (s : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec Lax434175.ParallelFamily.family),
  And
    (Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ParallelFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family (Lax434175.OperationsFamily.ofParallel s)))
    (Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family (Lax434175.OperationsFamily.ofParallel s))
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ParallelFamily.family s))

reducible_of_reduces : ∀ {s t : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family},
  Lax434175.Thresholds.Reduces s t →
    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family t)

reducible_of_reducesThroughFlow : ∀ {s t : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family},
  Lax434175.Thresholds.ReducesThroughFlow s t →
    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family t)

shop_faithful : ∀ (s : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec Lax434175.ShopFamily.family),
  And
    (Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family (Lax434175.OperationsFamily.ofShop s)))
    (Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family (Lax434175.OperationsFamily.ofShop s))
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopFamily.family s))

specialCase_of_le : ∀ {s t : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family},
  s.le t →
    Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family t)

concepts.title: One family for parallel machines with and without preemption
concepts.description:
The problems on parallel machines form one family over the machine model with
pieces: its fields are the interruption field and the fields of parallel
machines (machine environment, number of machines, number of jobs,
processing times, machine sets, release dates, deadlines, precedence
constraints with time lags, communication delays, a server, forbidden times
and the input encoding), and its objectives are the completion-time
objectives. The entry $\mathrm{pmtn}$ of the three-field notation is the value
preemption of the interruption field, the entry restarts the value restarts,
and no entry the value none. The value preemption without migration has no
machine model of its own.

A problem of the non-preemptive, the preemptive, or the restarts machine model
determines the problem of this family with the same values in the common
fields and the corresponding value of the interruption field.

**Theorem.** The two problems are special cases of each other, so that the
family describes the problems of the three machine models faithfully. In
the family, a specification that is field by field a special case of another
describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification that
reduces to another, directly or through flow time, describes a problem whose
decision version reduces to that of the other.

import Lax434175.ParallelProblems
import Lax434175.Interruption

/-!
---
title: One family for parallel machines with and without preemption
type: theorem
---
The problems on parallel machines form one family over the machine model with
pieces: its fields are the interruption field and the fields of parallel
machines (machine environment, number of machines, number of jobs,
processing times, machine sets, release dates, deadlines, precedence
constraints with time lags, communication delays, a server, forbidden times
and the input encoding), and its objectives are the completion-time
objectives. The entry $\mathrm{pmtn}$ of the three-field notation is the value
preemption of the interruption field, the entry restarts the value restarts,
and no entry the value none. The value preemption without migration has no
machine model of its own.

A problem of the non-preemptive, the preemptive, or the restarts machine model
determines the problem of this family with the same values in the common
fields and the corresponding value of the interruption field.

**Theorem.** The two problems are special cases of each other, so that the
family describes the problems of the three machine models faithfully. In
the family, a specification that is field by field a special case of another
describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification that
reduces to another, directly or through flow time, describes a problem whose
decision version reduces to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ParallelFamily
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175

/-- The fields of the family: interruption and the fields of parallel
machines. -/
inductive FieldName
  | interruption
  | field (i : ParallelProblems.FieldName)
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.interruption, .field .environment, .field .machineCount, .field .jobCount,
    .field .processingTimes, .field .machineSets, .field .releaseDates, .field .deadlines,
    .field .precedence, .field .communicationDelays, .field .server, .field .forbiddenTimes,
    .field .encoding}
  complete x := by
    cases x with
    | interruption => decide
    | field i => cases i <;> decide

/-- The problems on parallel machines. -/
abbrev family : Family Interruption.kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .interruption => Interruption.module
    | .field i => (ParallelProblems.family Interruption.model).module i

instance : Fintype family.ModuleName :=
  inferInstanceAs (Fintype FieldName)

/-- The specification `α | β | γ`. -/
def spec (interruption : Interruption.Mode := .none)
    (environment : ParallelMachines.Environment)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (machineSets : MachineSets.Value := .none)
    (processingTimes : ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (communicationDelays : CommunicationDelays.Value := .none)
    (server : Servers.Value := .none)
    (forbiddenTimes : ForbiddenTimes.Value := .none)
    (encoding : ForbiddenTimes.Encoding := .standard)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => interruption
    | .field .environment => environment
    | .field .machineCount => machineCount
    | .field .jobCount => jobCount
    | .field .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .field .machineSets => machineSets
    | .field .releaseDates => release
    | .field .deadlines => deadline
    | .field .precedence => precedence
    | .field .communicationDelays => communicationDelays
    | .field .server => server
    | .field .forbiddenTimes => forbiddenTimes
    | .field .encoding => encoding
  objective := objective

/-- A specification of one machine model on parallel machines read in another:
the values of the fields are the same. -/
def transSpec {M M' : ParallelMachines.Model} (s : Spec (ParallelProblems.family M)) :
    Spec (ParallelProblems.family M') where
  module
    | .environment => s.module .environment
    | .machineCount => s.module .machineCount
    | .jobCount => s.module .jobCount
    | .processingTimes => s.module .processingTimes
    | .machineSets => s.module .machineSets
    | .releaseDates => s.module .releaseDates
    | .deadlines => s.module .deadlines
    | .precedence => s.module .precedence
    | .communicationDelays => s.module .communicationDelays
    | .server => s.module .server
    | .forbiddenTimes => s.module .forbiddenTimes
    | .encoding => s.module .encoding
  objective := s.objective

/-- The specification of the family with the values of a specification of a
machine model on parallel machines and a way of interruption. -/
def ofSpec {M : ParallelMachines.Model} (interruption : Interruption.Mode)
    (s : Spec (ParallelProblems.family M)) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => interruption
    | .field i => (transSpec (M' := Interruption.model) s).module i
  objective := s.objective

axiom nonpreemptive_faithful (s : Spec ParallelProblems.nonpreemptive) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofSpec .none s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofSpec .none s)) (problem _ s)

axiom preemptive_faithful (s : Spec ParallelProblems.preemptive) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofSpec .pmtn s)) ∧

axiom restarts_faithful (s : Spec ParallelProblems.restarts) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofSpec .restarts s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofSpec .restarts s)) (problem _ s)

axiom family_sound : family.Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le {s t : Spec family} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reducesThroughFlow {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.ReducesThroughFlow s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.ParallelFamily

concepts.title: Parallel machines
concepts.description:
An instance on parallel machines has $n$ jobs, $m$ machines, and a
processing time $p_{ij}$ of job $j$ on machine $i$. A machine model on
parallel machines is a kernel whose instances are of this form, together
with the relation "at some time of schedule $\sigma$, job $j$ occupies
exactly the set $S$ of machines". Non-preemptive and preemptive scheduling
are two such models. A job may occupy several machines at once; the time it
then needs is its largest processing time on these machines.

The following fields restrict the instances of every machine model.

The machine-environment field:

- identical machines: the processing time of a job is the same on every
  machine;
- uniform machines: there are a length $q_j$ for every job and a positive
  speed $s_i$ for every machine with $p_{ij} \cdot s_i = q_j$;
- unrelated machines: no restriction.

Processing times are integral, so uniform machines are represented with the
time unit chosen fine enough that every quotient $q_j / s_i$ is an integer.

The processing-time field:

- unit: $p_{ij} = 1$;
- equal: there is a number $p$ with $p_{ij} = p$;
- one or two: $p_{ij} \in \{1, 2\}$;
- arbitrary: no restriction.

In the environment field each value is a special case of the next. Unit
processing times are a special case of equal ones and of one or two, and
every value of arbitrary ones.

**Theorem.** Over every machine model, the machine-environment and
processing-time fields are sound.

import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Lattice.Fold
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic
import Lax434175.Modules

/-!
---
title: Parallel machines
type: theorem
---
An instance on parallel machines has $n$ jobs, $m$ machines, and a
processing time $p_{ij}$ of job $j$ on machine $i$. A machine model on
parallel machines is a kernel whose instances are of this form, together
with the relation "at some time of schedule $\sigma$, job $j$ occupies
exactly the set $S$ of machines". Non-preemptive and preemptive scheduling
are two such models. A job may occupy several machines at once; the time it
then needs is its largest processing time on these machines.

The following fields restrict the instances of every machine model.

The machine-environment field:

- identical machines: the processing time of a job is the same on every
  machine;
- uniform machines: there are a length $q_j$ for every job and a positive
  speed $s_i$ for every machine with $p_{ij} \cdot s_i = q_j$;
- unrelated machines: no restriction.

Processing times are integral, so uniform machines are represented with the
time unit chosen fine enough that every quotient $q_j / s_i$ is an integer.

The processing-time field:

- unit: $p_{ij} = 1$;
- equal: there is a number $p$ with $p_{ij} = p$;
- one or two: $p_{ij} \in \{1, 2\}$;
- arbitrary: no restriction.

In the environment field each value is a special case of the next. Unit
processing times are a special case of equal ones and of one or two, and
every value of arbitrary ones.

**Theorem.** Over every machine model, the machine-environment and
processing-time fields are sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ParallelMachines
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

structure Inst where
  jobs : ℕ
  machines : ℕ
  /-- The processing time of a job on a machine. -/
  p : Fin jobs → Fin machines → ℕ
  /-- The release date of a job. -/
  r : Fin jobs → ℕ

/-- The time a job needs when it occupies a set of machines. -/
def duration (x : Inst) (j : Fin x.jobs) (S : Finset (Fin x.machines)) : ℕ :=
  S.sup (x.p j)

/-- A kernel on parallel machines. -/
structure Model where
  kernel : Kernel
  /-- The parallel-machine instance underlying an instance of the kernel. -/
  inst : kernel.Inst → Inst
  /-- The jobs of the kernel are those of the underlying instance. -/
  jobs_eq : ∀ x, kernel.jobs x = (inst x).jobs
  /-- At some time of the schedule the job occupies exactly this set of
  machines. -/
  uses : (x : kernel.Inst) → kernel.Sched x → Fin (inst x).jobs →
    Finset (Fin (inst x).machines) → Prop

inductive Environment
  | identical
  | uniform
  | unrelated

/-- The instances of a machine environment. -/
def Environment.holds : Environment → Inst → Prop
  | .identical, x => ∀ j i i', x.p j i = x.p j i'
  | .uniform, x => ∃ (q : Fin x.jobs → ℕ) (s : Fin x.machines → ℕ),
      ∀ j i, 0 < s i ∧ x.p j i * s i = q j
  | .unrelated, _ => True

/-- The position of an environment in the chain identical, uniform, unrelated. -/
def Environment.rank : Environment → ℕ
  | .identical => 0
  | .uniform => 1
  | .unrelated => 2

/-- The machine-environment field. -/
def environment (M : Model) : Module M.kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction Environment (fun v x => v.holds (M.inst x))
    (fun v w => decide (v.rank ≤ w.rank))

inductive ProcessingTimes
  | unit
  | equal
  | oneOrTwo
  | arbitrary
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The instances of a processing-time restriction. -/
def ProcessingTimes.holds : ProcessingTimes → Inst → Prop
  | .unit, x => ∀ j i, x.p j i = 1
  | .equal, x => ∃ p, ∀ j i, x.p j i = p
  | .oneOrTwo, x => ∀ j i, x.p j i = 1 ∨ x.p j i = 2
  | .arbitrary, _ => True

def ProcessingTimes.le : ProcessingTimes → ProcessingTimes → Bool
  | _, .arbitrary => true
  | .unit, _ => true
  | v, w => decide (v = w)

/-- The processing-time field. -/
def processingTimes (M : Model) : Module M.kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ProcessingTimes (fun v x => v.holds (M.inst x)) ProcessingTimes.le

/-- The number of machines, a parameter of every machine model. -/
def machines (M : Model) : M.kernel.Inst → ℕ := fun x => (M.inst x).machines

axiom environment_sound (M : Model) : (environment M).Sound

axiom processingTimes_sound (M : Model) : (processingTimes M).Sound

end Lax434175.ParallelMachines

processingTimes_sound : ∀ (M : Lax434175.ParallelMachines.Model), (Lax434175.ParallelMachines.processingTimes M).Sound

concepts.title: Problems on parallel machines in three-field notation
concepts.description:
The family of problems of a machine model on parallel machines has the
constraint fields machine environment, number of machines, number of jobs,
processing times, machine sets, release dates, deadlines, precedence
constraints with time lags, communication delays, a server, forbidden times
and the input encoding, and the
completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ of the three-field notation is one
specification of this family: $\alpha$ is the machine environment and count,
$\beta$ lists the values of the constraint fields, and $\gamma$ is the
objective. The entry $\mathrm{pmtn}$ of $\beta$ selects the preemptive
machine model, and the entry restarts the model with restarts; the concept on
one family for parallel machines joins the three models into a single family
with an interruption field. For example $1 \mid\mid \sum C_j$, $1 \mid r_j \mid \sum C_j$,
$P \mid p_j = 1, \mathrm{chains} \mid C_{\max}$ and
$R \mid r_j, \mathrm{prec} \mid \sum w_j T_j$ are the specifications below.

**Theorem.** In every machine model, a specification that is field by field a
special case of another describes a special case of the other's problem, and
a specification that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision
version reduces to that of the other. The same holds for reductions through
flow time in every machine model in which jobs start no later than they
complete. In
particular $1 \mid\mid \sum C_j$ is a special case of
$R \mid r_j, \mathrm{prec} \mid \sum w_j T_j$.

import Lax434175.Assembly
import Lax434175.Counts
import Lax434175.ReleaseDates
import Lax434175.Deadlines
import Lax434175.Precedence
import Lax434175.Thresholds
import Lax434175.MachineSets
import Lax434175.CommunicationDelays
import Lax434175.Servers
import Lax434175.ForbiddenTimes
import Lax434175.Restarts
import Lax434175.Nonpreemptive
import Lax434175.Preemptive

/-!
---
title: Problems on parallel machines in three-field notation
type: theorem
---
The family of problems of a machine model on parallel machines has the
constraint fields machine environment, number of machines, number of jobs,
processing times, machine sets, release dates, deadlines, precedence
constraints with time lags, communication delays, a server, forbidden times
and the input encoding, and the
completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ of the three-field notation is one
specification of this family: $\alpha$ is the machine environment and count,
$\beta$ lists the values of the constraint fields, and $\gamma$ is the
objective. The entry $\mathrm{pmtn}$ of $\beta$ selects the preemptive
machine model, and the entry restarts the model with restarts; the concept on
one family for parallel machines joins the three models into a single family
with an interruption field. For example $1 \mid\mid \sum C_j$, $1 \mid r_j \mid \sum C_j$,
$P \mid p_j = 1, \mathrm{chains} \mid C_{\max}$ and
$R \mid r_j, \mathrm{prec} \mid \sum w_j T_j$ are the specifications below.

**Theorem.** In every machine model, a specification that is field by field a
special case of another describes a special case of the other's problem, and
a specification that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision
version reduces to that of the other. The same holds for reductions through
flow time in every machine model in which jobs start no later than they
complete. In
particular $1 \mid\mid \sum C_j$ is a special case of
$R \mid r_j, \mathrm{prec} \mid \sum w_j T_j$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ParallelProblems
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175

/-- The constraint fields of the family. -/
inductive FieldName
  | environment
  | machineCount
  | jobCount
  | processingTimes
  | machineSets
  | releaseDates
  | deadlines
  | precedence
  | communicationDelays
  | server
  | forbiddenTimes
  | encoding
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.environment, .machineCount, .jobCount, .processingTimes, .machineSets, .releaseDates,
    .deadlines, .precedence, .communicationDelays, .server,
    .forbiddenTimes, .encoding}
  complete x := by cases x <;> decide

/-- The problems of a machine model on parallel machines. -/
abbrev family (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : Family M.kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .environment => ParallelMachines.environment M
    | .machineCount => Counts.module _ (ParallelMachines.machines M) 1
    | .jobCount => Counts.module _ M.kernel.jobs
    | .processingTimes => ParallelMachines.processingTimes M
    | .machineSets => MachineSets.module M
    | .releaseDates => ReleaseDates.module _
    | .deadlines => Deadlines.module _
    | .precedence => Precedence.module _ (ParallelMachines.machines M)
    | .communicationDelays => CommunicationDelays.module M
    | .server => Servers.parallel M
    | .forbiddenTimes => ForbiddenTimes.module _
    | .encoding => ForbiddenTimes.encoding _

instance (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : Fintype (family M).ModuleName :=
  inferInstanceAs (Fintype FieldName)

/-- The specification `α | β | γ` in a machine model. -/
def spec (M : ParallelMachines.Model) (environment : ParallelMachines.Environment)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (machineSets : MachineSets.Value := .none)
    (processingTimes : ParallelMachines.ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (communicationDelays : CommunicationDelays.Value := .none)
    (server : Servers.Value := .none)
    (forbiddenTimes : ForbiddenTimes.Value := .none)
    (encoding : ForbiddenTimes.Encoding := .standard)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec (family M) where
  module
    | .environment => environment
    | .machineCount => machineCount
    | .jobCount => jobCount
    | .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .machineSets => machineSets
    | .releaseDates => release
    | .deadlines => deadline
    | .precedence => precedence
    | .communicationDelays => communicationDelays
    | .server => server
    | .forbiddenTimes => forbiddenTimes
    | .encoding => encoding
  objective := objective

/-- The non-preemptive problems. -/
abbrev nonpreemptive := family Nonpreemptive.model

/-- The preemptive problems. -/
abbrev preemptive := family Preemptive.model

/-- The problems with restarts. -/
abbrev restarts := family Restarts.model

/-- `1 || ΣC_j` -/
def single_sumC : Spec nonpreemptive :=
  spec _ (environment := .identical) (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `1 | r_j | ΣC_j` -/
def single_release_sumC : Spec nonpreemptive :=
  spec _ (environment := .identical) (machineCount := .atMost 1) (release := .releaseDates)
    (objective := .sumC)

/-- `P | p_j = 1, chains | C_max` -/
def identical_unit_chains_makespan : Spec nonpreemptive :=
  spec _ (environment := .identical) (processingTimes := .unit) (precedence := ⟨.chains, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .makespan)

/-- `R | r_j, prec | Σw_jT_j` -/
def unrelated_release_prec_sumWT : Spec nonpreemptive :=
  spec _ (environment := .unrelated) (release := .releaseDates) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `P | pmtn, r_j | L_max` -/
def identical_pmtn_release_lmax : Spec preemptive :=
  spec _ (environment := .identical) (release := .releaseDates) (objective := .lmax)

axiom family_sound (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : (family M).Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le (M : ParallelMachines.Model) {s t : Spec (family M)} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem (family M) s) (problem (family M) t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces (M : ParallelMachines.Model) {s t : Spec (family M)} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem (family M) s) (problem (family M) t)

axiom reducible_of_reducesThroughFlow (M : ParallelMachines.Model)
    (h : M.kernel.StartsBeforeCompletion) {s t : Spec (family M)} :
    Thresholds.ReducesThroughFlow s t → Reducible (problem (family M) s) (problem (family M) t)

axiom single_sumC_specialCase :
    SpecialCase (problem nonpreemptive single_sumC)
      (problem nonpreemptive unrelated_release_prec_sumWT)

end Lax434175.ParallelProblems

  Lax434175.Thresholds.Reduces s t →
    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem (Lax434175.ParallelProblems.family M) s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem (Lax434175.ParallelProblems.family M) t)

  M.kernel.StartsBeforeCompletion →
    ∀ {s t : Lax434175.Assembly.Spec (Lax434175.ParallelProblems.family M)},
      Lax434175.Thresholds.ReducesThroughFlow s t →
        Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem (Lax434175.ParallelProblems.family M) s)

  (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ParallelProblems.nonpreemptive
    Lax434175.ParallelProblems.unrelated_release_prec_sumWT)

    Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem (Lax434175.ParallelProblems.family M) s)

concepts.title: Parameters along embeddings
concepts.description:
A parameter of a problem assigns a natural number to every instance. An
embedding of $A$ into $B$ bounds a parameter $\kappa_B$ of $B$ by a function
$g$ of a parameter $\kappa_A$ of $A$ if $\kappa_B(f(x)) \le g(\kappa_A(x))$
for every instance $x$ of $A$, where $f$ is the instance map.

For problems assembled from fields there are two sources of parameters. A
kernel parameter depends on the kernel instance only, such as the number of
machines. A field parameter depends on the data of one constraint module,
such as the number of distinct release dates; it is invariant if reading data
with a more general value does not change it.

**Theorem.** The embedding induced by a field-wise comparison of
specifications preserves every kernel parameter and every invariant field
parameter exactly.

For reductions of decision versions, let $\kappa_A$ and $\kappa_B$ assign to
the instances of $A$ and $B$ values of any kind, for instance pairs of
numbers, and let $R$ relate such values. Problem $A$ reduces to $B$ with
$R$ if some reduction maps every instance $x$ to an instance $y$ with
$R(\kappa_A(x), \kappa_B(y))$. A reduction between two problems of one
family is in place if it does not change the kernel instance, and hence no
kernel parameter, and changes no invariant field parameter.

**Theorem.** A sound embedding that relates the parameters gives a reduction
with the same relation, and reductions with relations compose.

Reductions are arbitrary maps here: their running time is not modelled.

/-!
---
title: Parameters along embeddings
type: theorem
---

for every instance $x$ of $A$, where $f$ is the instance map.

For problems assembled from fields there are two sources of parameters. A
kernel parameter depends on the kernel instance only, such as the number of
machines. A field parameter depends on the data of one constraint module,
such as the number of distinct release dates; it is invariant if reading data
with a more general value does not change it.

**Theorem.** The embedding induced by a field-wise comparison of
specifications preserves every kernel parameter and every invariant field
parameter exactly.

For reductions of decision versions, let $\kappa_A$ and $\kappa_B$ assign to
the instances of $A$ and $B$ values of any kind, for instance pairs of
numbers, and let $R$ relate such values. Problem $A$ reduces to $B$ with
$R$ if some reduction maps every instance $x$ to an instance $y$ with
$R(\kappa_A(x), \kappa_B(y))$. A reduction between two problems of one
family is in place if it does not change the kernel instance, and hence no
kernel parameter, and changes no invariant field parameter.

**Theorem.** A sound embedding that relates the parameters gives a reduction
with the same relation, and reductions with relations compose.

Reductions are arbitrary maps here: their running time is not modelled.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Parameters
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly

/-- A parameter of a problem. -/
abbrev Parameter (P : Problem) := P.Inst → ℕ

/-- The embedding bounds `κB` by `g` of `κA`. -/
def Bounds {A B : Problem} (e : Embedding A B) (κA : Parameter A) (κB : Parameter B)
    (g : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, κB (e.map x) ≤ g (κA x)

/-- A parameter that depends on the kernel instance only. -/
def ofKernel {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) (κ : K.Inst → ℕ) (s : Spec F) :
    Parameter (problem F s) :=
  fun x => κ x.base

/-- A parameter that depends on the data of one constraint module. -/
abbrev FieldParameter {K : Kernel} (M : Module K) :=
  (v : M.Value) → (x : K.Inst) → M.Data v x → ℕ

/-- Reading data with a more general value does not change the parameter. -/
def FieldParameter.Invariant {K : Kernel} {M : Module K} (κ : FieldParameter M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (v w : M.Value) (h : M.le v w = true) (x : K.Inst) (d : M.Data v x),
    κ w x (M.embed h x d) = κ v x d

/-- A field parameter as a parameter of an assembled problem. -/
def ofField {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) (i : F.ModuleName) (κ : FieldParameter (F.module i))
    (s : Spec F) : Parameter (problem F s) :=
  fun x => κ (s.module i) x.base (x.data i)

/-- `A` reduces to `B` by a reduction that relates the parameter values of
an instance and of its image by `R`. -/
def ReducibleWith {A B : Problem} {α β : Type} (κA : A.Inst → α) (κB : B.Inst → β)
    (R : α → β → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : DecisionReduction A B, r.Sound ∧ ∀ x D, R (κA x) (κB (r.map x D))

/-- A reduction between two problems of a family that keeps the kernel
instance and every invariant field parameter. -/
structure InPlace {K : Kernel} {F : Family K} {s t : Spec F}
    (r : DecisionReduction (problem F s) (problem F t)) : Prop where
  base : ∀ (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ), (r.map x D).base = x.base
  field : ∀ (i : F.ModuleName) (κ : FieldParameter (F.module i)), κ.Invariant →
    ∀ (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ), ofField F i κ t (r.map x D) = ofField F i κ s x

/-- The decision version of the problem of `s` reduces in place to that of
`t`. -/
def ReducibleInPlace {K : Kernel} {F : Family K} (s t : Spec F) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : DecisionReduction (problem F s) (problem F t), r.Sound ∧ InPlace r

axiom reducibleWith_of_embedding {A B : Problem} {α β : Type} (e : Embedding A B)
    (κA : A.Inst → α) (κB : B.Inst → β) (R : α → β → Prop) :
    e.Sound → (∀ x, R (κA x) (κB (e.map x))) → ReducibleWith κA κB R

axiom reducibleWith_trans {A B C : Problem} {α β γ : Type} (κA : A.Inst → α)
    (κB : B.Inst → β) (κC : C.Inst → γ) (R : α → β → Prop) (S : β → γ → Prop) :
    ReducibleWith κA κB R → ReducibleWith κB κC S →
      ReducibleWith κA κC (fun a c => ∃ b, R a b ∧ S b c)

axiom reducible_of_reducibleWith {A B : Problem} {α β : Type} (κA : A.Inst → α)
    (κB : B.Inst → β) (R : α → β → Prop) : ReducibleWith κA κB R → Reducible A B

axiom lift_ofKernel {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) (hF : F.Sound) (κ : K.Inst → ℕ)
    {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t) :
    ∀ x, ofKernel F κ t ((lift F hF h).map x) = ofKernel F κ s x

axiom lift_ofField {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) (hF : F.Sound) (i : F.ModuleName)
    (κ : FieldParameter (F.module i)) (hκ : κ.Invariant) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t) :
    ∀ x, ofField F i κ t ((lift F hF h).map x) = ofField F i κ s x

end Lax434175.Parameters

concepts.title: Precedence constraints and time lags
concepts.description:
With precedence constraints an instance carries a relation on the jobs,
given by its arcs, and a time lag $l_{ij}$ for every pair of jobs. Whenever
$i$ precedes $j$, job $j$ may not start before the completion of job $i$
plus the lag: $C_i + l_{ij} \le S_j$. A lag may be negative.

A value of the field consists of a class of relations and a kind of lags.

The classes are, with $\prec$ the transitive closure of the arcs:

- none: no relation, read as the empty relation;
- chains: every job has at most one successor and at most one predecessor;
- intree: every job has at most one successor;
- outtree: every job has at most one predecessor;
- tree: the relation is an intree or an outtree;
- opposing forest: the jobs split into two parts without arcs between them,
  one an intree and the other an outtree;
- series-parallel: $\prec$ contains no four jobs $a, b, c, d$ whose only
  relations are $a \prec c$, $b \prec c$, $b \prec d$;
- divide-and-conquer graph: a single job is one; and for two further jobs
  $s$ and $t$ and at least one divide-and-conquer graph on disjoint sets of
  jobs, so is their union with $s$, $t$ and all arcs from $s$ to the jobs of
  the graphs and from these to $t$;
- interval order: $a \prec b$ and $c \prec d$ imply $a \prec d$ or
  $c \prec b$;
- over-interval order: no five different jobs $1, \dots, 5$ are related
  exactly by $1 \prec 2$, $3 \prec 4$, $3 \prec 5$, and none exactly by the
  reverse relations $2 \prec 1$, $4 \prec 3$, $5 \prec 3$ (the structures of type
  I and II of Chardon and Moukrim, 2005);
- quasi-interval order: an over-interval order in which, moreover, no five
  different jobs are related exactly by $1 \prec 2$, $1 \prec 4$,
  $3 \prec 5 \prec 4$ and hence $3 \prec 4$ (Moukrim 1999, Definition 2: the
  structures of type I, in either orientation, and of type II);
- $A_m$-order, for the number $m$ of machines of the instance: for any two
  sets $A$ and $B$ of at most $m$ pairwise unrelated jobs, at most $m$ jobs
  of $A \cup B$ have a predecessor in $A \cup B$, and at most $m$ have a
  successor in $A \cup B$ (the property $Q_m$ of Moukrim and Quilliot, 1997);
- level order: every job of level $l + 1$ precedes every job of level $l$,
  where the level of a job is the length of the longest path of arcs
  starting from it;
- bounded height: an arbitrary relation; the value records that the length
  of its longest path is regarded as a constant;
- dimension two: the jobs can be placed in the plane such that, for
  different jobs, $i \prec j$ exactly if both coordinates of $i$ are at most
  those of $j$;
- bounded dimension: the same in a space of some dimension;
- prec: an arbitrary relation.

The class none is a special case of every class except
divide-and-conquer graphs, which have a single first and a single last job; interval orders of quasi-interval orders,
of over-interval orders and of $A_m$-orders; quasi-interval orders of over-interval orders; chains of intree
and outtree; these of tree; tree of opposing forest; dimension two of
bounded dimension; chains, the trees and opposing forests of series-parallel
orders, since every job of an intree has its successors on a chain and every job
of an outtree its predecessors; series-parallel orders of dimension two and of bounded
dimension, by the classical theorem that an order without such four jobs has
dimension at most two; and every class of prec.

The kinds of lags are: zero; unit, $l_{ij} = 1$; constant, $l_{ij} = l$, also
restricted to $l \le 0$ or to $l > 0$; and arbitrary, also restricted to
$l_{ij} \le 0$ or to $l_{ij} > 0$. A kind is a special case of another if
its lags are among the other's.

On a single machine, as in batching, every order is an $A_1$-order, so the
value says nothing there. The field of one machine leaves it out: the value
$A_m$ admits no instance and is a special case of no other value.

**Theorem.** Over every kernel, the field of precedence constraints with
time lags is sound, and so is the field of one machine.
