namespace Lax434175.Precedence
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

inductive Order
  | none
  | chains
  | intree
  | outtree
  | tree
  | opposingForest
  | seriesParallel
  | divideAndConquer
  | intervalOrder
  | quasiInterval
  | overInterval
  | aOrder
  | levelOrder
  | boundedHeight
  | dimensionTwo
  | boundedDimension
  | prec
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- No data without precedence constraints; a relation on the jobs with them. -/
def Order.Data (n : ℕ) : Order → Type
  | .none => Unit
  | _ => Fin n → Fin n → Prop

/-- The precedence relation; empty when the class is none. -/
def Order.view {n : ℕ} : (v : Order) → v.Data n → Fin n → Fin n → Prop
  | .none, _ => fun _ _ => False
  | .chains, r | .intree, r | .outtree, r | .tree, r | .opposingForest, r
  | .seriesParallel, r | .divideAndConquer, r | .intervalOrder, r | .levelOrder, r | .boundedHeight, r
  | .quasiInterval, r | .overInterval, r | .aOrder, r
  | .dimensionTwo, r
  | .boundedDimension, r | .prec, r => r

/-- Every job has at most one successor. -/
def AtMostOneSuccessor {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j k, r i j → r i k → j = k

/-- Every job has at most one predecessor. -/
def AtMostOnePredecessor {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j k, r j i → r k i → j = k

/-- The jobs split into an intree part and an outtree part without arcs
between them. -/
def OpposingForest {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ inPart : Fin n → Prop, (∀ i j, r i j → (inPart i ↔ inPart j)) ∧
    (∀ i j k, inPart i → r i j → r i k → j = k) ∧
    (∀ i j k, ¬ inPart i → r j i → r k i → j = k)

/-- No four jobs are related exactly by `a ≺ c`, `b ≺ c`, `b ≺ d`. -/
def SeriesParallel {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d, Relation.TransGen r a c → Relation.TransGen r b c → Relation.TransGen r b d →
    Relation.TransGen r a d ∨ Relation.TransGen r a b ∨ Relation.TransGen r b a ∨
      Relation.TransGen r c d ∨ Relation.TransGen r d c

/-- The arcs among a set of jobs form a divide-and-conquer graph. -/
inductive DivideAndConquer {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Finset (Fin n) → Prop
  | single (v : Fin n) : ¬ r v v → DivideAndConquer r {v}
  | compose (s t : Fin n) (parts : List (Finset (Fin n))) :
      s ≠ t → parts ≠ [] → (∀ P ∈ parts, s ∉ P ∧ t ∉ P) → parts.Pairwise Disjoint →
      (∀ P ∈ parts, DivideAndConquer r P) →
      (∀ a b, (a = s ∨ a = t ∨ ∃ P ∈ parts, a ∈ P) → (b = s ∨ b = t ∨ ∃ P ∈ parts, b ∈ P) →
        (r a b ↔ (∃ P ∈ parts, a ∈ P ∧ b ∈ P ∧ r a b) ∨ (a = s ∧ ∃ P ∈ parts, b ∈ P) ∨
          (b = t ∧ ∃ P ∈ parts, a ∈ P))) →
      DivideAndConquer r (parts.foldr (· ∪ ·) {s, t})

/-- `a ≺ b` and `c ≺ d` imply `a ≺ d` or `c ≺ b`. -/
def IntervalOrder {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d, Relation.TransGen r a b → Relation.TransGen r c d →
    Relation.TransGen r a d ∨ Relation.TransGen r c b

/-- Five different jobs are related exactly by the pairs of a pattern. -/
def Contains {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) (pattern : List (Fin 5 × Fin 5)) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Fin 5 → Fin n, Function.Injective f ∧
    ∀ a b, Relation.TransGen r (f a) (f b) ↔ (a, b) ∈ pattern
/-- Two unrelated pairs, the first job of one having a further successor. -/
def patternOut : List (Fin 5 × Fin 5) := [(0, 1), (2, 3), (2, 4)]
/-- The reverse of `patternOut`. -/
def patternIn : List (Fin 5 × Fin 5) := [(1, 0), (3, 2), (4, 2)]
/-- The third pattern forbidden in a quasi-interval order. -/
def patternThird : List (Fin 5 × Fin 5) := [(0, 1), (0, 3), (2, 3), (2, 4), (4, 3)]
/-- Neither `patternOut` nor its reverse occurs. -/
def OverInterval {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ¬ Contains r patternOut ∧ ¬ Contains r patternIn
/-- An over-interval order in which `patternThird` does not occur. -/
def QuasiInterval {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  OverInterval r ∧ ¬ Contains r patternThird
/-- Moukrim and Quilliot's property `Q_m`: for two sets of at most `m` pairwise
unrelated jobs, at most `m` jobs of their union have a predecessor in the union,
and at most `m` have a successor in the union. -/
def AOrder {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ) (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ A, ¬ Relation.TransGen r x y) →
    (∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ¬ Relation.TransGen r x y) → A.card ≤ m → B.card ≤ m →
    ∀ U ⊆ A ∪ B,
      ((∀ x ∈ U, ∃ y ∈ A ∪ B, Relation.TransGen r y x) → U.card ≤ m) ∧
      ((∀ x ∈ U, ∃ y ∈ A ∪ B, Relation.TransGen r x y) → U.card ≤ m)
/-- A path of `l` arcs starts from the job. -/
def HasPath {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : ℕ → Fin n → Prop
  | 0, _ => True
  | l + 1, v => ∃ w, r v w ∧ HasPath r l w

/-- The longest path of arcs starting from the job has `l` arcs. -/
def HasLevel {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) (v : Fin n) (l : ℕ) : Prop :=
  HasPath r l v ∧ ¬ HasPath r (l + 1) v

/-- Every job of level `l + 1` precedes every job of level `l`. -/
def LevelOrder {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v l, HasLevel r u (l + 1) → HasLevel r v l → Relation.TransGen r u v

/-- The jobs can be placed in `k`-dimensional space such that, for different
jobs, `i ≺ j` exactly if every coordinate of `i` is at most that of `j`. -/
def HasDimension {n : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Fin n → Fin k → ℚ, ∀ i j, i ≠ j → (Relation.TransGen r i j ↔ ∀ c, f i c ≤ f j c)

/-- The relations of a class, for a number `m` of machines. -/
def Order.InClass {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ) : Order → (Fin n → Fin n → Prop) → Prop
  | .none, r => ∀ i j, ¬ r i j
  | .chains, r => AtMostOneSuccessor r ∧ AtMostOnePredecessor r
  | .intree, r => AtMostOneSuccessor r
  | .outtree, r => AtMostOnePredecessor r
  | .tree, r => AtMostOneSuccessor r ∨ AtMostOnePredecessor r
  | .opposingForest, r => OpposingForest r
  | .seriesParallel, r => SeriesParallel r
  | .divideAndConquer, r => DivideAndConquer r Finset.univ
  | .intervalOrder, r => IntervalOrder r
  | .quasiInterval, r => QuasiInterval r
  | .overInterval, r => OverInterval r
  | .aOrder, r => AOrder m r
  | .levelOrder, r => LevelOrder r
  | .boundedHeight, _ => True
  | .dimensionTwo, r => HasDimension 2 r
  | .boundedDimension, r => ∃ k, HasDimension k r
  | .prec, _ => True

def Order.le : Order → Order → Bool
  | _, .prec => true
  | .none, .divideAndConquer => false
  | .none, _ => true
  | .chains, .chains | .chains, .intree | .chains, .outtree | .chains, .tree
  | .chains, .opposingForest => true
  | .intree, .intree | .intree, .tree | .intree, .opposingForest => true
  | .outtree, .outtree | .outtree, .tree | .outtree, .opposingForest => true
  | .tree, .tree | .tree, .opposingForest => true
  | .chains, .seriesParallel | .intree, .seriesParallel | .outtree, .seriesParallel
  | .tree, .seriesParallel | .opposingForest, .seriesParallel => true
  | .chains, .dimensionTwo | .intree, .dimensionTwo | .outtree, .dimensionTwo
  | .tree, .dimensionTwo | .opposingForest, .dimensionTwo => true
  | .chains, .boundedDimension | .intree, .boundedDimension | .outtree, .boundedDimension
  | .tree, .boundedDimension | .opposingForest, .boundedDimension => true
  | .dimensionTwo, .boundedDimension => true
  | .intervalOrder, .quasiInterval | .intervalOrder, .overInterval | .intervalOrder, .aOrder
  | .quasiInterval, .overInterval => true
  | .seriesParallel, .dimensionTwo | .seriesParallel, .boundedDimension => true
  | v, w => decide (v = w)

def Order.embed {n : ℕ} : {v w : Order} → Order.le v w = true → v.Data n → w.Data n
  | _, .none, _, _ => ()
  | v, .chains, _, d | v, .intree, _, d | v, .outtree, _, d | v, .tree, _, d
  | v, .opposingForest, _, d | v, .seriesParallel, _, d | v, .divideAndConquer, _, d
  | v, .intervalOrder, _, d | v, .quasiInterval, _, d | v, .overInterval, _, d | v, .aOrder, _, d
  | v, .levelOrder, _, d
  | v, .boundedHeight, _, d | v, .dimensionTwo, _, d | v, .boundedDimension, _, d
  | v, .prec, _, d => v.view d

inductive Lags
  | zero
  | unit
  | constant
  | constantNonpositive
  | constantPositive
  | arbitrary
  | arbitraryNonpositive
  | arbitraryPositive
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The data of a kind of lags. -/
def Lags.Data (n : ℕ) : Lags → Type
  | .zero | .unit => Unit
  | .constant | .constantNonpositive | .constantPositive => ℤ
  | .arbitrary | .arbitraryNonpositive | .arbitraryPositive => Fin n → Fin n → ℤ

/-- The lag between two jobs. -/
def Lags.view {n : ℕ} : (v : Lags) → v.Data n → Fin n → Fin n → ℤ
  | .zero, _ => fun _ _ => 0
  | .unit, _ => fun _ _ => 1
  | .constant, l | .constantNonpositive, l | .constantPositive, l => fun _ _ => l
  | .arbitrary, l | .arbitraryNonpositive, l | .arbitraryPositive, l => l

/-- The sign condition of a kind of lags. -/
def Lags.Admits {n : ℕ} : Lags → (Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) → Prop
  | .constantNonpositive, l | .arbitraryNonpositive, l => ∀ i j, l i j ≤ 0
  | .constantPositive, l | .arbitraryPositive, l => ∀ i j, 0 < l i j
  | _, _ => True

def Lags.le : Lags → Lags → Bool
  | .zero, .zero | .zero, .constant | .zero, .constantNonpositive | .zero, .arbitrary
  | .zero, .arbitraryNonpositive => true
  | .unit, .unit | .unit, .constant | .unit, .constantPositive | .unit, .arbitrary
  | .unit, .arbitraryPositive => true
  | .constant, .constant | .constant, .arbitrary => true
  | .constantNonpositive, .constantNonpositive | .constantNonpositive, .constant
  | .constantNonpositive, .arbitraryNonpositive | .constantNonpositive, .arbitrary => true
  | .constantPositive, .constantPositive | .constantPositive, .constant
  | .constantPositive, .arbitraryPositive | .constantPositive, .arbitrary => true
  | .arbitrary, .arbitrary => true
  | .arbitraryNonpositive, .arbitraryNonpositive | .arbitraryNonpositive, .arbitrary => true
  | .arbitraryPositive, .arbitraryPositive | .arbitraryPositive, .arbitrary => true
  | _, _ => false

def Lags.embed {n : ℕ} : {v w : Lags} → Lags.le v w = true → v.Data n → w.Data n
  | _, .zero, _, _ | _, .unit, _, _ => ()
  | .constant, .constant, _, l | .constantNonpositive, .constant, _, l
  | .constantPositive, .constant, _, l
  | .constantNonpositive, .constantNonpositive, _, l
  | .constantPositive, .constantPositive, _, l => l
  | .zero, .constant, _, _ | .zero, .constantNonpositive, _, _ => (0 : ℤ)
  | .unit, .constant, _, _ | .unit, .constantPositive, _, _ => (1 : ℤ)
  | v, .arbitrary, _, d | v, .arbitraryNonpositive, _, d | v, .arbitraryPositive, _, d =>
      v.view d
  | .zero, .constantPositive, h, _ | .unit, .constantNonpositive, h, _
  | .constant, .constantNonpositive, h, _ | .constant, .constantPositive, h, _
  | .constantNonpositive, .constantPositive, h, _
  | .constantPositive, .constantNonpositive, h, _
  | .arbitrary, .constant, h, _ | .arbitrary, .constantNonpositive, h, _
  | .arbitrary, .constantPositive, h, _ | .arbitraryNonpositive, .constant, h, _
  | .arbitraryNonpositive, .constantNonpositive, h, _
  | .arbitraryNonpositive, .constantPositive, h, _ | .arbitraryPositive, .constant, h, _
  | .arbitraryPositive, .constantNonpositive, h, _
  | .arbitraryPositive, .constantPositive, h, _ => absurd h Bool.false_ne_true

/-- A value of the field: a class of relations and a kind of lags. -/
structure Value where
  order : Order
  lags : Lags := .zero

/-- No precedence constraints. -/
def Value.none : Value := ⟨.none, .zero⟩

/-- The field of precedence constraints with time lags over a kernel with a
number of machines. -/
def module (K : Kernel) (machines : K.Inst → ℕ) : Module K where
  Value := Value
  Data v x := v.order.Data (K.jobs x) × v.lags.Data (K.jobs x)
  admits v x d := v.order.InClass (machines x) (v.order.view d.1) ∧ v.lags.Admits (v.lags.view d.2)
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ i j, v.order.view d.1 i j →
    (K.completion x σ i : ℚ) + (v.lags.view d.2 i j : ℚ) ≤ (K.start x σ j : ℚ)
  le v w := Order.le v.order w.order && Lags.le v.lags w.lags
  embed {v w} h _ d :=
    (Order.embed (v := v.order) (w := w.order) (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1 d.1,
      Lags.embed (v := v.lags) (w := w.lags) (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).2 d.2)

axiom sound (K : Kernel) (machines : K.Inst → ℕ) : (module K machines).Sound

/-- The field of precedence constraints on one machine, without `A_m`-orders:
the value `A_m` admits no instance and lies below no other value. -/
def oneMachine (K : Kernel) : Module K where
  Value := Value
  Data := (module K fun _ => 1).Data
  admits v x d := v.order ≠ .aOrder ∧ (module K fun _ => 1).admits v x d
  constraint := (module K fun _ => 1).constraint
  le v w := (module K fun _ => 1).le v w && (w.order != .aOrder || v.order == .aOrder)
  embed {v w} h x d := (module K fun _ => 1).embed (v := v) (w := w)
    (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1 x d

axiom oneMachine_sound (K : Kernel) : (oneMachine K).Sound

end Lax434175.Precedence

concepts.title: Reversing precedence constraints
concepts.description:
Reversing a relation turns every arc $i \to j$ into $j \to i$. Reversal maps
intrees to outtrees and outtrees to intrees, and every other class of the
precedence field except quasi-interval orders, divide-and-conquer graphs and
level orders to itself; these three are called not reversible here.
Reversing the data of a value of the precedence field reverses the relation
and transposes arbitrary lags, $l'_{ij} = l_{ji}$; other lags are kept.

**Theorem.** For a reversible class, the reverse of a relation of the class
belongs to the reversed class; reversed lags satisfy the same sign
condition.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.Precedence

/-!
---
title: Reversing precedence constraints
type: theorem
---
Reversing a relation turns every arc $i \to j$ into $j \to i$. Reversal maps
intrees to outtrees and outtrees to intrees, and every other class of the
precedence field except quasi-interval orders, divide-and-conquer graphs and
level orders to itself; these three are called not reversible here.
Reversing the data of a value of the precedence field reverses the relation
and transposes arbitrary lags, $l'_{ij} = l_{ji}$; other lags are kept.

**Theorem.** For a reversible class, the reverse of a relation of the class
belongs to the reversed class; reversed lags satisfy the same sign
condition.
-/

namespace Lax434175.PrecedenceReversal
open Lax434175.Precedence

/-- The class of the reverses of the relations of a class. -/
def reverse : Order → Order
  | .intree => .outtree
  | .outtree => .intree
  | o => o

/-- The classes whose reverses are shown to stay in a class. -/
def reversible : Order → Bool
  | .quasiInterval | .divideAndConquer | .levelOrder => false
  | _ => true

/-- The reversed relation of a value. -/
def reverseData {n : ℕ} : (o : Order) → o.Data n → (reverse o).Data n
  | .none, _ => ()
  | .chains, r | .intree, r | .outtree, r | .tree, r | .opposingForest, r
  | .seriesParallel, r | .divideAndConquer, r | .intervalOrder, r | .quasiInterval, r
  | .overInterval, r | .aOrder, r | .levelOrder, r | .boundedHeight, r | .dimensionTwo, r
  | .boundedDimension, r | .prec, r => fun i j => r j i

/-- The transposed lags of a value. -/
def lagsReverseData {n : ℕ} : (l : Lags) → l.Data n → l.Data n
  | .arbitrary, d | .arbitraryNonpositive, d | .arbitraryPositive, d => fun i j => d j i
  | .zero, d | .unit, d | .constant, d | .constantNonpositive, d | .constantPositive, d => d

axiom view_reverse {n : ℕ} (o : Order) (d : o.Data n) (i j : Fin n) :
    (reverse o).view (reverseData o d) i j ↔ o.view d j i

axiom lags_view_reverse {n : ℕ} (l : Lags) (d : l.Data n) (i j : Fin n) :
    l.view (lagsReverseData l d) i j = l.view d j i

axiom inClass_reverse {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ) (o : Order) (h : reversible o = true)
    (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : o.InClass m r → (reverse o).InClass m (fun i j => r j i)

axiom lags_admits_reverse {n : ℕ} (l : Lags) (d : l.Data n) :
    l.Admits (l.view d) → l.Admits (l.view (lagsReverseData l d))

end Lax434175.PrecedenceReversal

concepts.title: Preemption does not help on a single machine
concepts.description:
On a single machine and without release dates, a preemptive schedule can be
turned into a non-preemptive one in which no job completes later: process the
jobs one after the other from time $0$, in the order of their completion
times (ties broken by start times and then by the numbering of the jobs). A
job then completes at the total processing time of the jobs before it and
itself, and the machine has processed these jobs entirely by the original
completion time of the job, so this total is at most that time.

Hence a problem and the same problem with preemption allowed have the same
decision versions when there is one operation per job, at most one machine,
no release dates, the precedence constraints have zero lags, the objective
depends monotonically on the completion times (every objective except the
number of jobs not completed just in time), and there are no server,
forbidden times, no-idle constraints or batch setups. Deadlines, machine sets,
communication delays, no-wait and transportation delays may be present; with
one operation per job on one machine the last three impose nothing more on
the new schedule.

A specification $s$ reduces to $t$ by dropping preemption if it is of this
kind, has no interruption or preemption, and the same specification with the
other of the two is field by field a special case of $t$.

**Theorem.** A specification that reduces to another by dropping preemption
describes a problem whose decision version reduces to that of the other.

import Lax434175.TimeReversal

/-!
---
title: Preemption does not help on a single machine
type: theorem
---
On a single machine and without release dates, a preemptive schedule can be
turned into a non-preemptive one in which no job completes later: process the
jobs one after the other from time $0$, in the order of their completion
times (ties broken by start times and then by the numbering of the jobs). A
job then completes at the total processing time of the jobs before it and
itself, and the machine has processed these jobs entirely by the original
completion time of the job, so this total is at most that time.

Hence a problem and the same problem with preemption allowed have the same
decision versions when there is one operation per job, at most one machine,
no release dates, the precedence constraints have zero lags, the objective
depends monotonically on the completion times (every objective except the
number of jobs not completed just in time), and there are no server,
forbidden times, no-idle constraints or batch setups. Deadlines, machine sets,
communication delays, no-wait and transportation delays may be present; with
one operation per job on one machine the last three impose nothing more on
the new schedule.

A specification $s$ reduces to $t$ by dropping preemption if it is of this
kind, has no interruption or preemption, and the same specification with the
other of the two is field by field a special case of $t$.

**Theorem.** A specification that reduces to another by dropping preemption
describes a problem whose decision version reduces to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.PreemptionUseless
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Operations Lax434175.OperationsFamily Lax434175.TimeReversal

def atMostOne : Counts.Bound → Bool
  | .atMost 0 | .atMost 1 => true
  | _ => false

def zeroLags (v : Precedence.Value) : Bool :=
  match v.lags with
  | .zero => true
  | _ => false

def regular : Objectives.Value → Bool
  | .sumZ | .sumWZ => false
  | _ => true

/-- The interruption swapped between none and preemption. -/
def swapped : Interruption.Mode → Option Interruption.Mode
  | .none => some .pmtn
  | .pmtn => some .none
  | .restarts | .pmtnNoMigration => none

/-- The specification is of the kind for which preemption does not help. -/
def Applies (s : Spec family) : Bool :=
  isSingle (s.module .jobStructure) && atMostOne (s.module .machineCount) &&
    releaseNone (s.module .releaseDates) && zeroLags (s.module .precedence) &&
    regular (Thresholds.objectiveOf s) && noServer (s.module .server) &&
    noForbidden (s.module .forbiddenTimes) && noIdling (s.module .noIdle) &&
    noSetups (s.module .batchSetups)

/-- The same specification with another way of interruption. -/
def withInterruption (s : Spec family) (m : Interruption.Mode) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => m
    | i => s.module i
  objective := s.objective

/-- `s` reduces to `t` by dropping or allowing preemption. -/
def ReducesByPreemption (s t : Spec family) : Prop :=
  Applies s = true ∧ ∃ m, swapped (s.module .interruption) = some m ∧ (withInterruption s m).le t

instance (s t : Spec family) : Decidable (ReducesByPreemption s t) := by
  unfold ReducesByPreemption
  cases h : swapped (s.module .interruption) with
  | none => exact isFalse fun ⟨_, m, hm, _⟩ => by simp at hm
  | some m =>
    exact decidable_of_iff (Applies s = true ∧ (withInterruption s m).le t)
      ⟨fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => ⟨h1, m, rfl, h2⟩, fun ⟨h1, m', hm, h2⟩ => by
        cases hm
        exact ⟨h1, h2⟩⟩

axiom reducible_of_reducesByPreemption {s t : Spec family} :
    ReducesByPreemption s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.PreemptionUseless

  Lax434175.PreemptionUseless.ReducesByPreemption s t →
    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family t)

concepts.title: Preemptive scheduling on parallel machines
concepts.description:
A preemptive schedule is a finite list of pieces. A piece processes one job
on a nonempty set of machines during an interval given by a start time and a
length, both nonnegative rational numbers.

A piece of length $\ell$ of job $j$ on a set of machines on which the job
needs time $p$ completes the fraction $\ell / p$ of the job. A schedule is
feasible for the kernel if

- two different pieces that share a machine or a job are disjoint in time,
  so a machine processes one job at a time and a job is processed in one
  place at a time, and
- every job is completed: its fractions sum to $1$, or one of its pieces is
  on machines on which it needs time $0$.

A job starts when its first piece starts and completes when its last piece
ends.

**Theorem.** Every job starts no later than it completes.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Rat
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Ring.Rat
import Lax434175.ParallelMachines

/-!
---
title: Preemptive scheduling on parallel machines
type: theorem
---
A preemptive schedule is a finite list of pieces. A piece processes one job
on a nonempty set of machines during an interval given by a start time and a
length, both nonnegative rational numbers.

A piece of length $\ell$ of job $j$ on a set of machines on which the job
needs time $p$ completes the fraction $\ell / p$ of the job. A schedule is
feasible for the kernel if

- two different pieces that share a machine or a job are disjoint in time,
  so a machine processes one job at a time and a job is processed in one
  place at a time, and
- every job is completed: its fractions sum to $1$, or one of its pieces is
  on machines on which it needs time $0$.

A job starts when its first piece starts and completes when its last piece
ends.

**Theorem.** Every job starts no later than it completes.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Preemptive
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.ParallelMachines

/-- A job is processed on a set of machines from `start` for `length` time
units. -/
structure Piece (x : Inst) where
  job : Fin x.jobs
  machines : Finset (Fin x.machines)
  start : NNRat
  length : NNRat

/-- The time at which a piece ends. -/
def Piece.finish {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : NNRat := q.start + q.length

structure Sched (x : Inst) where
  pieces : List (Piece x)

/-- The pieces of a job. -/
def piecesOf {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : List (Piece x) :=
  σ.pieces.filter (fun q => decide (q.job = j))

/-- The fraction of a job that a schedule completes. -/
def fraction (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : NNRat :=
  ((piecesOf σ j).map (fun q => q.length / (duration x j q.machines : NNRat))).sum

/-- Two pieces do not overlap in time. -/
def Apart {x : Inst} (a b : Piece x) : Prop :=
  a.finish ≤ b.start ∨ b.finish ≤ a.start

def feasible (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, q.machines.Nonempty) ∧
  σ.pieces.Pairwise (fun a b => (¬ Disjoint a.machines b.machines ∨ a.job = b.job) → Apart a b) ∧
  ∀ j, fraction x σ j = 1 ∨ ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ j, duration x j q.machines = 0

/-- The start of the first piece of a job. -/
def start (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ j).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0

/-- The end of the last piece of a job. -/
def completion (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ j).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The kernel of preemptive scheduling on parallel machines. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := Sched
  feasible := feasible
  start := start
  completion := completion

/-- Preemptive scheduling as a machine model. -/
def model : Model where
  kernel := kernel
  inst x := x
  jobs_eq _ := rfl
  uses _ σ j S := ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ j, q.machines = S

axiom startsBeforeCompletion : kernel.StartsBeforeCompletion

end Lax434175.Preemptive

concepts.title: Preemptive shop problems in three-field notation
concepts.description:
The family of preemptive shop problems has the constraint fields shop type,
machines of the operations, number of machines, number of jobs, processing
times, release dates, deadlines and precedence constraints between jobs,
and the completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ with $\alpha$ one of $O$, $F$, $J$
whose $\beta$ contains $\mathrm{pmtn}$ is one specification of this family.
For example $J2 \mid \mathrm{pmtn} \mid C_{\max}$ is the specification below.

**Theorem.** A specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version reduces
to that of the other.

import Lax434175.Assembly
import Lax434175.Counts
import Lax434175.ReleaseDates
import Lax434175.Deadlines
import Lax434175.Precedence
import Lax434175.Thresholds
import Lax434175.PreemptiveShops

/-!
---
title: Preemptive shop problems in three-field notation
type: theorem
---
The family of preemptive shop problems has the constraint fields shop type,
machines of the operations, number of machines, number of jobs, processing
times, release dates, deadlines and precedence constraints between jobs,
and the completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ with $\alpha$ one of $O$, $F$, $J$
whose $\beta$ contains $\mathrm{pmtn}$ is one specification of this family.
For example $J2 \mid \mathrm{pmtn} \mid C_{\max}$ is the specification below.

**Theorem.** A specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version reduces
to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175

/-- The constraint fields of the family. -/
inductive FieldName
  | shopType
  | machineSets
  | machineCount
  | jobCount
  | processingTimes
  | releaseDates
  | deadlines
  | precedence
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.shopType, .machineSets, .machineCount, .jobCount, .processingTimes, .releaseDates,
    .deadlines, .precedence}
  complete x := by cases x <;> decide

/-- The preemptive shop problems. -/
abbrev family : Family PreemptiveShops.kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .shopType => PreemptiveShops.shopType
    | .machineSets => PreemptiveShops.machineSets
    | .machineCount => Counts.module _ PreemptiveShops.machines 1
    | .jobCount => Counts.module _ PreemptiveShops.kernel.jobs
    | .processingTimes => PreemptiveShops.processingTimes
    | .releaseDates => ReleaseDates.module _
    | .deadlines => Deadlines.module _
    | .precedence => Precedence.module _ PreemptiveShops.machines

/-- The specification `α | pmtn, β | γ` of a preemptive shop problem. -/
def spec (shopType : Shops.ShopType)
    (machineSets : Shops.Machines)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (processingTimes : Shops.ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec family where
  module
    | .shopType => shopType
    | .machineSets => machineSets
    | .machineCount => machineCount
    | .jobCount => jobCount
    | .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .releaseDates => release
    | .deadlines => deadline
    | .precedence => precedence
  objective := objective

/-- `J2 | pmtn | C_max` -/
def job2_makespan : Spec family :=
  spec (shopType := .job) (machineSets := .dedicated) (machineCount := .atMost 2)
    (objective := .makespan)

axiom family_sound : family.Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le {s t : Spec family} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems

  Lax434175.Thresholds.Reduces s t →
    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems.family t)

  s.le t →
    Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems.family t)

concepts.title: Preemptive shop scheduling
concepts.description:
The instances are those of shop scheduling. A preemptive schedule is a
finite list of pieces. A piece processes one operation on a nonempty set of
machines during an interval given by a start time and a length, both
nonnegative rational numbers.

A schedule is feasible for the kernel if two different pieces that belong to
the same job or share a machine are disjoint in time, and every operation is
completed: the lengths of its pieces sum to its processing time, or its
processing time is $0$ and it has a piece. As on parallel machines, an
operation of length $0$ thus still has a piece, which gives it a completion
time. An operation starts
when its first piece starts and completes when its last piece ends, and
likewise a job.

The shop-type field, the machine field and the processing-time field are
those of non-preemptive shops: the operations of a flow shop or job shop
must be processed in their given order, each completing before the next
starts, and every piece of an operation occupies an admissible set of
machines.

**Theorem.** The shop-type, machine and processing-time fields of
preemptive shops are sound.

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Rat
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Ring.Rat
import Lax434175.Shops

/-!
---
title: Preemptive shop scheduling
type: theorem
---
The instances are those of shop scheduling. A preemptive schedule is a
finite list of pieces. A piece processes one operation on a nonempty set of
machines during an interval given by a start time and a length, both
nonnegative rational numbers.

A schedule is feasible for the kernel if two different pieces that belong to
the same job or share a machine are disjoint in time, and every operation is
completed: the lengths of its pieces sum to its processing time, or its
processing time is $0$ and it has a piece. As on parallel machines, an
operation of length $0$ thus still has a piece, which gives it a completion
time. An operation starts
when its first piece starts and completes when its last piece ends, and
likewise a job.

The shop-type field, the machine field and the processing-time field are
those of non-preemptive shops: the operations of a flow shop or job shop
must be processed in their given order, each completing before the next
starts, and every piece of an operation occupies an admissible set of
machines.

**Theorem.** The shop-type, machine and processing-time fields of
preemptive shops are sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.PreemptiveShops
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Shops

/-- An operation is processed on a set of machines from `start` for `length`
time units. -/
structure Piece (x : Inst) where
  op : Op x
  machines : Finset (Fin x.machines)
  start : NNRat
  length : NNRat

/-- The time at which a piece ends. -/
def Piece.finish {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : NNRat := q.start + q.length

structure Sched (x : Inst) where
  pieces : List (Piece x)

/-- The pieces of an operation. -/
def piecesOf {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : List (Piece x) :=
  σ.pieces.filter (fun q => decide (q.op = o))

/-- The pieces of a job. -/
def piecesOfJob {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : List (Piece x) :=
  σ.pieces.filter (fun q => decide (q.op.1 = j))

/-- Two pieces do not overlap in time. -/
def Apart {x : Inst} (a b : Piece x) : Prop :=
  a.finish ≤ b.start ∨ b.finish ≤ a.start

def feasible (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, q.machines.Nonempty) ∧
  σ.pieces.Pairwise
    (fun a b => (a.op.1 = b.op.1 ∨ ¬ Disjoint a.machines b.machines) → Apart a b) ∧
  ∀ o : Op x, ((piecesOf σ o).map fun q => q.length / (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat)).sum = 1 ∨
    ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, x.p o.1 o.2 = 0

/-- The start of the first piece of an operation. -/
def opStart {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0

/-- The end of the last piece of an operation. -/
def opFinish {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : NNRat :=
  (((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The kernel of preemptive shop scheduling. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := Sched
  feasible := feasible
  start _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0
  completion _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The number of machines, a parameter of the kernel. -/
def machines : kernel.Inst → ℕ := Inst.machines

/-- The operations of every job are processed in their given order. -/
def InOrder (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k k' : Fin (x.ops j)), k < k' → opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, k'⟩

/-- The order a shop type imposes on the operations of a job. -/
def ordered : ShopType → (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  | .open, _, _ => True
  | .flow, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .job, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .flexibleFlow, x, σ => InOrder x σ

/-- The shop-type field. -/
def shopType : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopType
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits v x _ := v.holds x
  constraint v x _ σ := ordered v x σ
  le := ShopType.le
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- The machine field. -/
def machineSets : Module kernel where
  Value := Machines
  Data := Machines.Data
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v _ d σ := ∀ q ∈ Sched.pieces σ, v.view d q.op.1 q.op.2 q.machines
  le := Machines.le
  embed := Machines.embed

/-- The processing-time field. -/
def processingTimes : Module kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ProcessingTimes ProcessingTimes.holds
    (fun v w => decide (v.rank ≤ w.rank))

axiom shopType_sound : shopType.Sound

axiom machineSets_sound : machineSets.Sound

axiom processingTimes_sound : processingTimes.Sound

end Lax434175.PreemptiveShops

concepts.title: Optimization problems and embeddings
concepts.description:
An optimization problem consists of a type of instances, for every instance a
type of candidate solutions, a feasibility predicate, and a rational cost to
be minimized.

An embedding of a problem $A$ into a problem $B$ maps every instance $x$ of
$A$ to an instance of $B$ and translates solutions in both directions. It is
sound if both translations preserve feasibility and neither increases the
cost. A sound embedding shows that $A$ is a special case of $B$: the two
instances $x$ and its image have the same optimal cost.

Restricting a problem to the instances satisfying a predicate yields again a
problem, and the inclusion of the restricted instances is an embedding.

Embeddings compose: the instance maps are composed, and so are the
translations of solutions.

**Theorem.** The composition of two sound embeddings is sound.

The decision version of a problem asks, for an instance and a threshold,
whether some feasible solution has cost at most the threshold. A reduction
of the decision version of $A$ to that of $B$ maps every instance of $A$ and
integral threshold to an instance of $B$ and an integral threshold with the
same answer. Problem $A$ is reducible to $B$ if such a reduction exists.

**Theorem.** A special case of a problem is reducible to it, and
reducibility is transitive.

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Rat

/-!
---
title: Optimization problems and embeddings
type: theorem
---
An optimization problem consists of a type of instances, for every instance a
type of candidate solutions, a feasibility predicate, and a rational cost to
be minimized.

An embedding of a problem $A$ into a problem $B$ maps every instance $x$ of
$A$ to an instance of $B$ and translates solutions in both directions. It is
sound if both translations preserve feasibility and neither increases the
cost. A sound embedding shows that $A$ is a special case of $B$: the two
instances $x$ and its image have the same optimal cost.

Restricting a problem to the instances satisfying a predicate yields again a
problem, and the inclusion of the restricted instances is an embedding.

Embeddings compose: the instance maps are composed, and so are the
translations of solutions.

**Theorem.** The composition of two sound embeddings is sound.

The decision version of a problem asks, for an instance and a threshold,
whether some feasible solution has cost at most the threshold. A reduction
of the decision version of $A$ to that of $B$ maps every instance of $A$ and
integral threshold to an instance of $B$ and an integral threshold with the
same answer. Problem $A$ is reducible to $B$ if such a reduction exists.

**Theorem.** A special case of a problem is reducible to it, and
reducibility is transitive.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Problems

/-- A minimization problem. -/
structure Problem where
  /-- The instances. -/
  Inst : Type
  /-- The candidate solutions of an instance. -/
  Sched : Inst → Type
  /-- Which candidate solutions are feasible. -/
  feasible : (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  /-- The cost of a candidate solution. -/
  cost : (x : Inst) → Sched x → ℚ

/-- The data of an embedding of `A` into `B`: a map on instances and
translations of solutions in both directions. -/
structure Embedding (A B : Problem) where
  map : A.Inst → B.Inst
  forth : (x : A.Inst) → A.Sched x → B.Sched (map x)
  back : (x : A.Inst) → B.Sched (map x) → A.Sched x

/-- An embedding is sound if both translations preserve feasibility and do
not increase the cost. -/
structure Embedding.Sound {A B : Problem} (e : Embedding A B) : Prop where
  forth_feasible : ∀ x σ, A.feasible x σ → B.feasible (e.map x) (e.forth x σ)
  forth_cost : ∀ x σ, A.feasible x σ → B.cost (e.map x) (e.forth x σ) ≤ A.cost x σ
  back_feasible : ∀ x τ, B.feasible (e.map x) τ → A.feasible x (e.back x τ)
  back_cost : ∀ x τ, B.feasible (e.map x) τ → A.cost x (e.back x τ) ≤ B.cost (e.map x) τ

/-- `A` is a special case of `B`. -/
def SpecialCase (A B : Problem) : Prop := ∃ e : Embedding A B, e.Sound

/-- The restriction of a problem to the instances satisfying `φ`. -/
def Problem.restrict (P : Problem) (φ : P.Inst → Prop) : Problem where
  Inst := { x : P.Inst // φ x }
  Sched x := P.Sched x.1
  feasible x σ := P.feasible x.1 σ
  cost x σ := P.cost x.1 σ

/-- The inclusion of a restricted problem into the unrestricted one. -/
def Problem.inclusion (P : Problem) (φ : P.Inst → Prop) : Embedding (P.restrict φ) P where
  map x := x.1
  forth _ σ := σ
  back _ σ := σ

/-- The composition of two embeddings. -/
def Embedding.comp {A B C : Problem} (e : Embedding A B) (f : Embedding B C) : Embedding A C where
  map x := f.map (e.map x)
  forth x σ := f.forth (e.map x) (e.forth x σ)
  back x τ := e.back x (f.back (e.map x) τ)

axiom comp_sound {A B C : Problem} (e : Embedding A B) (f : Embedding B C) :
    e.Sound → f.Sound → (e.comp f).Sound

/-- Some feasible solution of the instance has cost at most the threshold. -/
def Problem.Decides (P : Problem) (x : P.Inst) (D : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, P.feasible x σ ∧ P.cost x σ ≤ D

/-- The data of a reduction between decision versions: an instance and a
threshold of `A` are mapped to an instance and a threshold of `B`. -/
structure DecisionReduction (A B : Problem) where
  map : A.Inst → ℤ → B.Inst
  threshold : A.Inst → ℤ → ℤ

/-- A reduction is sound if it preserves the answer. -/
def DecisionReduction.Sound {A B : Problem} (r : DecisionReduction A B) : Prop :=
  ∀ x (D : ℤ), A.Decides x D ↔ B.Decides (r.map x D) (r.threshold x D)

/-- The decision version of `A` reduces to that of `B`. -/
def Reducible (A B : Problem) : Prop := ∃ r : DecisionReduction A B, r.Sound

axiom reducible_of_specialCase {A B : Problem} : SpecialCase A B → Reducible A B

axiom reducible_trans {A B C : Problem} : Reducible A B → Reducible B C → Reducible A C

end Lax434175.Problems

statements.signature:
comp_sound : ∀ {A B C : Lax434175.Problems.Problem} (e : Lax434175.Problems.Embedding A B) (f : Lax434175.Problems.Embedding B C),
  e.Sound → f.Sound → (e.comp f).Sound
reducible_of_specialCase : ∀ {A B : Lax434175.Problems.Problem}, Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase A B → Lax434175.Problems.Reducible A B

reducible_trans : ∀ {A B C : Lax434175.Problems.Problem},
  Lax434175.Problems.Reducible A B → Lax434175.Problems.Reducible B C → Lax434175.Problems.Reducible A C

concepts.title: Results along special cases
concepts.description:
A specification $s$ that is field by field a special case of $t$ embeds its
instances into those of $t$ (the lift): same kernel instance, data read with
the more general values, and schedules unchanged. A reading *lifts* along
$s \le t$ if every word of an instance of $s$ is also a word of its lift, and
every word that writes a schedule of the lift writes the same schedule of the
instance.

**Theorem.** If the reading lifts along $s \le t$, every algorithm for $t$ is one
for $s$ — the same program: deciding within $O(T)$ becomes deciding within
$O(T \circ \mathrm{lift})$, and likewise for approximations within a running
time, randomized ones and approximation schemes, with the ratio read on the lift.
The same holds for approximations and schemes of the kept weight, if the lift
keeps the total weight, and for deciding with wide words, also on the instances
satisfying a predicate: on those of $s$ whose lift satisfies it.

**Theorem.** The standard reading of the operations family lifts along every
$s \le t$ with the same value of the encoding field, and the standard reading of
the batching family lifts along every $s \le t$.

The second theorem holds because the standard words write every field by its
view, and reading data with a more general value does not change its view.

A reading *determines the answer* for $t$ if two instances of $t$ with thresholds
written by one word have the same threshold and the same answer.

**Theorem.** The standard reading of the operations family determines the answer
for every specification with the standard encoding, and the standard reading of
the batching family for every specification: the words parse uniquely, give the
same kernel instance and the same views, and constraints and costs read only the
views.

**Theorem.** Let the reading lift along $s \le t$ and determine the answer for $t$.
Then a word of an instance of $s$ has the same answer for $s$ and for $t$, and:

1. hardness goes up, by the identity on words: NP-hardness and strong
   NP-hardness of $s$ give those of $t$; W[t]-hardness for $\kappa_s$ gives
   W[t]-hardness for $\kappa_t$ if, on every word, $\kappa_t$ of an instance of $t$
   is at most a computable function of $\kappa_s$ of an instance of $s$, and
   para-NP-hardness likewise for any function;
2. the coarse classes go down: in P, pseudo-polynomial, in P for every fixed
   value (with $\kappa_t$ bounded by a function of $\kappa_s$ on every word), and
   FPT (with a computable bound, for a parameter of $s$ computable in polynomial
   time).

namespace Lax434175.Propagation
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Results

variable {K : Kernel} {F : Family K} (hF : F.Sound) (R : Reading F)

/-- The reading lifts along `s ≤ t`. -/
def Lifts {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t) : Prop :=
  (∀ x w, R.Encodes s w x → R.Encodes t w ((lift F hF h).map x)) ∧
    ∀ x w σ, R.Decodes t ((lift F hF h).map x) w σ → R.Decodes s x w σ

variable {hF R}

axiom decidesExact_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℤ → ℕ} :
    DecidesExact (R.at t) T → DecidesExact (R.at s) fun x D => T ((lift F hF h).map x) D

axiom decidesWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    DecidesWithin (R.at t) T → DecidesWithin (R.at s) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom decidesWithinWide_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    DecidesWithinWide (R.at t) T → DecidesWithinWide (R.at s) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom decidesWithinWide_restrict_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {φ : Inst F t → Prop} {T : {x : Inst F t // φ x} → ℕ} :
    DecidesWithinWide ((R.at t).restrict φ) T →
      DecidesWithinWide ((R.at s).restrict fun x => φ ((lift F hF h).map x))
        fun x => T ⟨(lift F hF h).map x.1, x.2⟩

axiom approxWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {ρ : Inst F t → ℝ} {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    ApproxWithin (R.at t) ρ T →
      ApproxWithin (R.at s) (fun x => ρ ((lift F hF h).map x)) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom randomApproxWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {ρ : Inst F t → ℝ} {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    RandomApproxWithin (R.at t) ρ T →
      RandomApproxWithin (R.at s) (fun x => ρ ((lift F hF h).map x))
        fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom schemeWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {T : ℚ → Inst F t → ℕ} :
    SchemeWithin (R.at t) T → SchemeWithin (R.at s) fun ε x => T ε ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom randomDecidesWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    RandomDecidesWithin (R.at t) T → RandomDecidesWithin (R.at s) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom oneSidedDecidesWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    OneSidedDecidesWithin (R.at t) T → OneSidedDecidesWithin (R.at s) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom zeroErrorDecidesWithin_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h) {T : Inst F t → ℕ} :
    ZeroErrorDecidesWithin (R.at t) T → ZeroErrorDecidesWithin (R.at s) fun x => T ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom approxKept_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {W : Parameters.Parameter (problem F s)} {W' : Parameters.Parameter (problem F t)}
    (hW : ∀ x, W' ((lift F hF h).map x) = W x) {ρ : Inst F t → ℝ} :
    ApproxKept (R.at t) W' ρ → ApproxKept (R.at s) W fun x => ρ ((lift F hF h).map x)

axiom ptasKept_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {W : Parameters.Parameter (problem F s)} {W' : Parameters.Parameter (problem F t)}
    (hW : ∀ x, W' ((lift F hF h).map x) = W x) :
    PTASKept (R.at t) W' → PTASKept (R.at s) W

axiom eptasKept_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {W : Parameters.Parameter (problem F s)} {W' : Parameters.Parameter (problem F t)}
    (hW : ∀ x, W' ((lift F hF h).map x) = W x) :
    EPTASKept (R.at t) W' → EPTASKept (R.at s) W

axiom fptasKept_down {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t} (hl : Lifts hF R h)
    {W : Parameters.Parameter (problem F s)} {W' : Parameters.Parameter (problem F t)}
    (hW : ∀ x, W' ((lift F hF h).map x) = W x) :
    FPTASKept (R.at t) W' → FPTASKept (R.at s) W

axiom ops_lifts (hF : OperationsFamily.family.Sound) {s t : Spec OperationsFamily.family}
    (h : s.le t) (he : s.module .encoding = t.module .encoding) :
    Lifts hF StandardReading.ops h

axiom batch_lifts (hF : BatchFamily.family.Sound) {s t : Spec BatchFamily.family}
    (h : s.le t) : Lifts hF StandardReading.batch h

/-- The reading determines the answer for `t`. -/
def Determined (R : Reading F) (t : Spec F) : Prop :=
  ∀ u y y' D D', EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y' D' →
    D = D' ∧ ((problem F t).Decides y D ↔ (problem F t).Decides y' D')

axiom ops_determined {t : Spec OperationsFamily.family} (ht : t.module .encoding = .standard) :
    Determined StandardReading.ops t

axiom batch_determined (t : Spec BatchFamily.family) : Determined StandardReading.batch t

open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions Lax496464.WH_B4_Hierarchies

variable {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t}

axiom yes_iff (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) {u : List ℕ} {x : Inst F s} {D : ℤ}
    (hx : EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D) :
    (decision (R.at t)).Yes u ↔ (decision (R.at s)).Yes u

axiom npHard_up (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) :
    NPHard (R.at s) → NPHard (R.at t)

axiom stronglyNPHard_up (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) :
    StronglyNPHard (R.at s) → StronglyNPHard (R.at t)

axiom paraNPHard_up (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t)
    {κs : TParameter (problem F s)} {κt : TParameter (problem F t)} (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hκ : ∀ u x D y D', EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D' →
      κt y D' ≤ g (κs x D)) :
    ParaNPHard (R.at s) κs → ParaNPHard (R.at t) κt

axiom wHard_up (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) (w : ℕ)
    {κs : TParameter (problem F s)} {κt : TParameter (problem F t)} (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hg : Computable g) (hκ : ∀ u x D y D', EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D' →
      κt y D' ≤ g (κs x D)) :
    WHard (R.at s) w κs → WHard (R.at t) w κt

axiom inP_down (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) : InP (R.at t) → InP (R.at s)

axiom pseudoPoly_down (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t) :
    PseudoPoly (R.at t) → PseudoPoly (R.at s)

axiom inPFixed_down (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t)
    {κs : TParameter (problem F s)} {κt : TParameter (problem F t)} (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hκ : ∀ u x D y D', EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D' →
      κt y D' ≤ g (κs x D)) :
    InPFixed (R.at t) κt → InPFixed (R.at s) κs

axiom isFPT_down (hl : Lifts hF R h) (hd : Determined R t)
    {κs : TParameter (problem F s)} {κt : TParameter (problem F t)} (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hg : Computable g) (hκ : ∀ u x D y D', EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D' →
      κt y D' ≤ g (κs x D))
    (hps : IsParameterized (parameterized (R.at s) κs)) :
    IsFPT (R.at t) κt → IsFPT (R.at s) κs

end Lax434175.Propagation

concepts.title: Parameters along special cases
concepts.description:
The transfers of parameterized results along a special case $s \le t$
(`Propagation`) ask that, on every word, the parameter of an instance of $t$ be at
most a function of the parameter of an instance of $s$. A parameter *agrees
along* $s \le t$ if, on every word, the two parameters are equal; then it is
bounded with the identity.

**Theorem.** Let $s \le t$ be specifications of the operations family, both with
the standard encoding. Under the standard reading the parameters $n$, $m$,
$p_{\max}$, $\#p$, $\#r$, $\#w$, $\#d$, $w_{\max}$, the number of kinds of
machines, the rank of $(p_{ij})$, $q_{\max}$, $\chi$, the largest communication
delay, the width of the precedence order, $pw(I)$ (the most time windows sharing an
instant, minus one) and the maximum slack agree along $s \le t$, and so do their
sums. The same holds for $n$, $p_{\max}$, $\#p$, $\#r$,
$\#w$, $\#d$ and $w_{\max}$ in the batching family.

The words determine the kernel instance, the views and the threshold, and the
lift changes none of them; every parameter listed reads only those. The time
window of a job ends at its deadline, and also at $D$ for the makespan and at
$d_j + D$ for the maximum lateness; the makespan is a special case only of
itself and of the maximum lateness with all due dates $0$, so the windows agree.

Fixed-parameter tractability in the sense of lax-496464 includes that the
parameter is computed in polynomial time. For a parameter that agrees along
$s \le t$, the parameter of a word of $s$ is that of the same word read for $t$,
so it is computed by the same program.

**Theorem.** If the reading lifts along $s \le t$ and determines the answer for
$t$, then fixed-parameter tractability goes down from $t$ to $s$ for every
parameter that agrees along $s \le t$.

namespace Lax434175.PropagationParameters
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Results
open Lax434175.ResultParameters

variable {K : Kernel} {F : Family K}

/-- On every word, the parameter of `t` equals that of `s`. -/
def WordEq (R : Reading F) {s t : Spec F} (κs : TParameter (problem F s))
    (κt : TParameter (problem F t)) : Prop :=
  ∀ u x D y D', EncodesDecision (R.at s) u x D → EncodesDecision (R.at t) u y D' → κt y D' = κs x D

axiom wordEq_tplus {R : Reading F} {s t : Spec F} {κs κs' : TParameter (problem F s)}
    {κt κt' : TParameter (problem F t)} :
    WordEq R κs κt → WordEq R κs' κt' → WordEq R (tplus κs κs') (tplus κt κt')

/-- Fixed-parameter tractability goes down along `s ≤ t` for a parameter that agrees
on every word. -/
axiom isFPT_down_eq {hF : F.Sound} {R : Reading F} {s t : Spec F} {h : s.le t}
    (hl : Propagation.Lifts hF R h) (hd : Propagation.Determined R t)
    {κs : TParameter (problem F s)} {κt : TParameter (problem F t)} (hκ : WordEq R κs κt) :
    IsFPT (R.at t) κt → IsFPT (R.at s) κs

concepts.title: Single-machine scheduling with rejection
concepts.description:
The problem $1 \mid \sum_{j \in \mathrm{reject}} e_j \le B \mid \sum C_j$. An
instance has $n$ jobs with processing times $p_j$ and rejection costs $e_j$,
and a budget $B$. A solution rejects some jobs and assigns a start time to
every accepted job. It is feasible if the rejection costs of the rejected
jobs sum to at most $B$ and no two accepted jobs overlap on the machine. The
cost is the total completion time of the accepted jobs.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
import Lax434175.Problems

/-!
---
title: Single-machine scheduling with rejection
type: definition
---
The problem $1 \mid \sum_{j \in \mathrm{reject}} e_j \le B \mid \sum C_j$. An
instance has $n$ jobs with processing times $p_j$ and rejection costs $e_j$,
and a budget $B$. A solution rejects some jobs and assigns a start time to
every accepted job. It is feasible if the rejection costs of the rejected
jobs sum to at most $B$ and no two accepted jobs overlap on the machine. The
cost is the total completion time of the accepted jobs.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Rejection
open Lax434175.Problems

structure Inst where
  jobs : ℕ
  p : Fin jobs → ℕ
  /-- The rejection cost of a job. -/
  e : Fin jobs → ℕ
  budget : ℕ

structure Sched (x : Inst) where
  /-- The accepted jobs. -/
  accepted : Finset (Fin x.jobs)
  start : Fin x.jobs → ℕ

def completion (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : ℕ := σ.start j + x.p j

/-- The rejected jobs respect the budget and the accepted jobs do not
overlap. -/
def feasible (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ \ σ.accepted, x.e j ≤ x.budget ∧
  ∀ i ∈ σ.accepted, ∀ j ∈ σ.accepted, i ≠ j →
    completion x σ i ≤ σ.start j ∨ completion x σ j ≤ σ.start i

/-- `1 | Σ_{j ∈ reject} e_j ≤ B | ΣC_j` -/
def problem : Problem where
  Inst := Inst
  Sched := Sched
  feasible := feasible
  cost x σ := ((∑ j ∈ σ.accepted, completion x σ j : ℕ) : ℚ)

end Lax434175.Rejection

concepts.title: Release dates
concepts.description:
Every job of every kernel has a release date $r_j$, and no job may start
before its release date. The release-date field has the values

- none: all release dates are $0$;
- release dates: arbitrary release dates;
- online: arbitrary release dates; the value records that the jobs become
  known only at their release dates. This concerns the algorithms that are
  admitted, not the instances and schedules, which are those of the value
  release dates.

The value none is a special case of the value release dates; the value
online is comparable only with itself.

The number of distinct release dates is a parameter of every kernel.

**Theorem.** Over every kernel, the release-date field is sound.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Card
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Image
import Lax434175.Modules

/-!
---
title: Release dates
type: theorem
---
Every job of every kernel has a release date $r_j$, and no job may start
before its release date. The release-date field has the values

- none: all release dates are $0$;
- release dates: arbitrary release dates;
- online: arbitrary release dates; the value records that the jobs become
  known only at their release dates. This concerns the algorithms that are
  admitted, not the instances and schedules, which are those of the value
  release dates.

The value none is a special case of the value release dates; the value
online is comparable only with itself.

The number of distinct release dates is a parameter of every kernel.

**Theorem.** Over every kernel, the release-date field is sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ReleaseDates
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

inductive Value
  | none
  | releaseDates
  | online
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The instances of a value. -/
def Value.holds (K : Kernel) : Value → K.Inst → Prop
  | .none, x => ∀ j, K.release x j = 0
  | .releaseDates, _ => True
  | .online, _ => True

def le : Value → Value → Bool
  | .none, .releaseDates => true
  | v, w => decide (v = w)

/-- The release-date field over a kernel. -/
def module (K : Kernel) : Module K where
  Value := Value
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits v x _ := v.holds K x
  constraint _ x _ σ := ∀ j, (K.release x j : NNRat) ≤ K.start x σ j
  le := le
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- The number of distinct release dates. -/
def distinct (K : Kernel) : K.Inst → ℕ :=
  fun x => (Finset.univ.image (K.release x)).card

axiom sound (K : Kernel) : (module K).Sound

end Lax434175.ReleaseDates

statements.signature: sound : ∀ (K : Lax434175.Kernels.Kernel), (Lax434175.ReleaseDates.module K).Sound

concepts.title: Preemption with restarts on parallel machines
concepts.description:
With restarts a job may be interrupted, but then its processing is lost and
it has to be processed again from the beginning. A schedule is a finite list
of pieces as in preemptive scheduling. It is feasible for the kernel if two
different pieces that share a machine or a job are disjoint in time and
every job has a complete piece, whose length is the full time the job needs
on the machines of the piece. A job starts when its first piece starts and
completes when its first complete piece ends.

**Theorem.** In every feasible schedule, every job starts no later than it
completes.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.Preemptive

/-!
---
title: Preemption with restarts on parallel machines
type: theorem
---
With restarts a job may be interrupted, but then its processing is lost and
it has to be processed again from the beginning. A schedule is a finite list
of pieces as in preemptive scheduling. It is feasible for the kernel if two
different pieces that share a machine or a job are disjoint in time and
every job has a complete piece, whose length is the full time the job needs
on the machines of the piece. A job starts when its first piece starts and
completes when its first complete piece ends.

**Theorem.** In every feasible schedule, every job starts no later than it
completes.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Restarts
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.ParallelMachines Lax434175.Preemptive

/-- A piece processes its job entirely. -/
def Complete {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : Prop :=
  q.length = (duration x q.job q.machines : NNRat)

instance {x : Inst} (q : Piece x) : Decidable (Complete q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (q.length = _))

/-- The complete pieces of a job. -/
def completePieces {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : List (Piece x) :=
  (piecesOf σ j).filter (fun q => decide (Complete q))

def feasible (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, q.machines.Nonempty) ∧
  σ.pieces.Pairwise (fun a b => (¬ Disjoint a.machines b.machines ∨ a.job = b.job) → Apart a b) ∧
  ∀ j, completePieces σ j ≠ []

/-- The end of the first complete piece of a job. -/
def completion (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : NNRat :=
  (((completePieces σ j).map Piece.finish).min?).getD 0

/-- The kernel of scheduling with restarts on parallel machines. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := Sched
  feasible := feasible
  start := start
  completion := completion

/-- Scheduling with restarts as a machine model. -/
def model : Model where
  kernel := kernel
  inst x := x
  jobs_eq _ := rfl
  uses _ σ j S := ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ j, q.machines = S

axiom startsBeforeCompletion : kernel.StartsBeforeCompletion

end Lax434175.Restarts

statements.signature: startsBeforeCompletion : Lax434175.Restarts.kernel.StartsBeforeCompletion

concepts.title: Parameters of the zoo's results
concepts.description:
The parameters in which the zoo states results, as functions of the instances.

On the operations family and the batching family: the number $n$ of jobs, the
number $m$ of machines, the largest processing time $p_{\max}$ and weight
$w_{\max}$, the numbers $\#p$, $\#r$, $\#w$, $\#d$ of distinct processing times,
release dates, weights and due dates, the total weight $W$ and the total
processing time $P$. The processing time of an operation is its time on the
first machine, as in the field of processing times, and that of a job the sum
over its operations. A weight is $1$ and a due date $0$ when the objective has
none.

On the operations family also:

- the number of *kinds* of machines (Knop and Koutecký): machines of one kind
  have the same processing time for every operation, so this is the number of
  distinct columns of the matrix $(p_{ij})$;
- the *rank* of that matrix over the rationals (Chen, Marx, Ye and Zhang);
- $q_{\max}$, the largest processing time of the last operation of a job (and the
  predicate that every job has a last operation of positive length), and
  $\chi$, the largest number of jobs whose last operations, ending at their due
  dates, overlap at one instant — for jobs completed just in time the
  intervals $[d_j - q_j, d_j)$ (Heeger, Hermelin, Itzhaki, Schieber and
  Shabtay; $\omega$ there);
- the largest communication delay $c$;
- the speed ratio $s_{\max}/s_{\min}$ of uniform machines, the least over the
  speeds that represent the instance;
- the width of the precedence order, the largest number of pairwise
  incomparable jobs;
- the number $\tau$ of forbidden times, the instants at which no job may start
  or end;
- $n_{\max}$, the largest number of operations of a job;
- the number $g$ of batches into which batch setups group the jobs;
- with the threshold $D$: the gap $D - \mathrm{LP}$ to the optimum
  $\mathrm{LP}$ of the linear relaxation [CS-LP] of the vertex-cover formulation
  of Correa and Schulz, as in Ambühl and Mastrolilli (2009). With $P$ the
  transitive closure of the precedence relation and $i \parallel j$ for
  different jobs related in neither direction, it minimizes
  $\sum_j p_jw_j + \sum_{(i,j) \in P} p_iw_j + \sum_{i \parallel j} \delta_{ij}p_iw_j$
  over $\delta \ge 0$ with $\delta_{ij} + \delta_{ji} \ge 1$ for $i \parallel j$,
  $\delta_{ik} + \delta_{kj} \ge 1$ for $(i, j) \in P$, $j \parallel k$,
  $k \parallel i$, and $\delta_{il} + \delta_{kj} \ge 1$ for $(i, j), (k, l) \in P$,
  $j \parallel k$, $l \parallel i$. Its optimum equals those of the
  relaxations of Potts and of Chudak and Hochbaum (their Theorems 2 to 4); the
  parameter is $\lceil D - \mathrm{LP} \rceil$, and $0$ when negative;
- with the threshold $D$: the time window of job $j$ runs from its release date
  to its deadline, and also ends at $D$ for the makespan and at $d_j + D$ for the
  maximum lateness, since the decision version asks for that. The pathwidth
  $\mathrm{pw}(I)$ of the interval graph of the windows is the largest number of
  windows containing one instant, minus one, and the maximum slack is the largest
  window length minus processing time (Hanen and Munier Kordon). A window without
  end has length $0$ here; it occurs only without deadlines and with another
  objective.

On the batching family also $\mathrm{pw}(I)$ and the maximum slack, with the
same windows.

On single-machine scheduling with rejection: $n$, $\#p$, $p_{\max}$, the number
$\#e$ of distinct rejection costs, the largest rejection cost $e_{\max}$, and the
number of accepted jobs, read as an instance quantity: the least number of jobs
a feasible solution accepts, $n$ minus the most jobs whose rejection costs fit
the budget. On $P \mid\mid C_{\min}$: $n$ and $m$.

- the *rank* of that matrix over the rationals (Chen, Marx, Ye and Zhang);
- $q_{\max}$, the largest processing time of the last operation of a job (and the
  predicate that every job has a last operation of positive length), and
  $\chi$, the largest number of jobs whose last operations, ending at their due
  dates, overlap at one instant — for jobs completed just in time the
  intervals $[d_j - q_j, d_j)$ (Heeger, Hermelin, Itzhaki, Schieber and
  Shabtay; $\omega$ there);
- the largest communication delay $c$;
- the speed ratio $s_{\max}/s_{\min}$ of uniform machines, the least over the
  speeds that represent the instance;
- the width of the precedence order, the largest number of pairwise
  incomparable jobs;
- the number $\tau$ of forbidden times, the instants at which no job may start
  or end;
- $n_{\max}$, the largest number of operations of a job;
- the number $g$ of batches into which batch setups group the jobs;
- with the threshold $D$: the gap $D - \mathrm{LP}$ to the optimum
  $\mathrm{LP}$ of the linear relaxation [CS-LP] of the vertex-cover formulation
  of Correa and Schulz, as in Ambühl and Mastrolilli (2009). With $P$ the
  transitive closure of the precedence relation and $i \parallel j$ for
  different jobs related in neither direction, it minimizes
  $\sum_j p_jw_j + \sum_{(i,j) \in P} p_iw_j + \sum_{i \parallel j} \delta_{ij}p_iw_j$
  over $\delta \ge 0$ with $\delta_{ij} + \delta_{ji} \ge 1$ for $i \parallel j$,
  $\delta_{ik} + \delta_{kj} \ge 1$ for $(i, j) \in P$, $j \parallel k$,
  $k \parallel i$, and $\delta_{il} + \delta_{kj} \ge 1$ for $(i, j), (k, l) \in P$,
  $j \parallel k$, $l \parallel i$. Its optimum equals those of the
  relaxations of Potts and of Chudak and Hochbaum (their Theorems 2 to 4); the
  parameter is $\lceil D - \mathrm{LP} \rceil$, and $0$ when negative;
- with the threshold $D$: the time window of job $j$ runs from its release date
  to its deadline, and also ends at $D$ for the makespan and at $d_j + D$ for the
  maximum lateness, since the decision version asks for that. The pathwidth
  $\mathrm{pw}(I)$ of the interval graph of the windows is the largest number of
  windows containing one instant, minus one, and the maximum slack is the largest
  window length minus processing time (Hanen and Munier Kordon). A window without
  end has length $0$ here; it occurs only without deadlines and with another
  objective.

On the batching family also $\mathrm{pw}(I)$ and the maximum slack, with the
same windows.

On single-machine scheduling with rejection: $n$, $\#p$, $p_{\max}$, the number
$\#e$ of distinct rejection costs, the largest rejection cost $e_{\max}$, and the
number of accepted jobs, read as an instance quantity: the least number of jobs
a feasible solution accepts, $n$ minus the most jobs whose rejection costs fit
the budget. On $P \mid\mid C_{\min}$: $n$ and $m$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ResultParameters
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Parameters
open Lax434175.Results

/-- The sum of two parameters. -/
def plus {P : Problem} (κ κ' : Parameter P) : Parameter P := fun x => κ x + κ' x

/-- The largest number of the intervals `[a i, b i)` that contain one instant. -/
noncomputable def overlap {n : ℕ} (a b : Fin n → ℕ∞) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k | ∃ t : ℕ, k = (Finset.univ.filter fun j => a j ≤ t ∧ (t : ℕ∞) < b j).card}

namespace Ops

variable (s : Spec OperationsFamily.family)

/-- The number of jobs. -/
def n : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => x.base.jobs

/-- The number of machines. -/
def m : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => x.base.machines

/-- The largest processing time of an operation. -/
def pmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  Finset.univ.sup fun o : Operations.Op x.base => Operations.opTime x.base o

/-- The number of distinct processing times of operations. -/
def numP : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  (Finset.univ.image fun o : Operations.Op x.base => Operations.opTime x.base o).card

/-- The number of distinct release dates. -/
def numR : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ZooParameters.distinct x.base.r

/-- The number of distinct weights. -/
def numW : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  ZooParameters.weights Operations.kernel s.objective x.base x.objectiveData

/-- The number of distinct due dates. -/
def numD : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  ZooParameters.dueDates Operations.kernel s.objective x.base x.objectiveData

/-- The weight of a job. -/
def weight (x : Inst _ s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.weight (K := Operations.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The due date of a job. -/
def due (x : Inst _ s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.dueDate (K := Operations.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The largest weight. -/
def wmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => Finset.univ.sup (weight s x)

/-- The total weight. -/
def totalW : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ∑ j, weight s x j

/-- The processing time of a job: the sum over its operations. -/
def ptime (x : Operations.Inst) (j : Fin x.jobs) : ℕ :=
  ∑ k : Fin (x.ops j), Operations.opTime x ⟨j, k⟩

/-- The total processing time. -/
def totalP : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ∑ j, ptime x.base j

/-- The number of kinds of machines: distinct columns of the matrix of
processing times. -/
def kinds : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  (Finset.univ.image fun i : Fin x.base.machines =>
    fun o : Operations.Op x.base => x.base.p o.1 o.2 i).card

/-- The rank of the matrix of processing times. -/
noncomputable def rank : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  (Matrix.of fun (o : Operations.Op x.base) (i : Fin x.base.machines) =>
    (x.base.p o.1 o.2 i : ℚ)).rank

/-- The processing time of the last operation of a job, `0` without operations. -/
def lastTime (x : Operations.Inst) (j : Fin x.jobs) : ℕ :=
  if h : 0 < x.ops j then Operations.opTime x ⟨j, ⟨x.ops j - 1, by omega⟩⟩ else 0

/-- Every job has a last operation of positive length. -/
def lastPositive (x : (problem _ s).Inst) : Prop := ∀ j, 0 < lastTime x.base j

/-- `q_max`: the largest processing time of a last operation. -/
def qmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => Finset.univ.sup (lastTime x.base)

/-- `χ`: the largest number of jobs whose last operations, ending at their due
dates, overlap at one instant. -/
noncomputable def chi : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  overlap (fun j => ((due s x j - lastTime x.base j : ℕ) : ℕ∞)) (fun j => (due s x j : ℕ∞))

/-- The largest communication delay. -/
noncomputable def cmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  sSup {c | ∃ i j, CommunicationDelays.view (s.module .communicationDelays)
    (x.data .communicationDelays : CommunicationDelays.Data _ x.base.toPar) i j c}

/-- The speed ratio `s_max / s_min` of uniform machines: the least over the
speeds representing the instance. -/
noncomputable def speedRatio (x : Inst _ s) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ (q : Operations.Op x.base → ℕ) (sp : Fin x.base.machines → ℕ),
    (∀ o i, 0 < sp i ∧ x.base.p o.1 o.2 i * sp i = q o) ∧
    ∀ i i', (sp i : ℝ) ≤ r * sp i'}

/-- The precedence relation of an instance. -/
def prec (x : Inst _ s) (i j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Prop :=
  (s.module .precedence).order.view (x.data .precedence).1 i j

/-- The width of the precedence order: the largest set of jobs no two of which
are related by the transitive closure. -/
noncomputable def width : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  sSup {k | ∃ S : Finset (Fin x.base.jobs), S.card = k ∧
    ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, ¬ Relation.TransGen (prec s x) i j}

/-- The end of the time window of a job with the threshold `D`: its deadline,
and also `D` for the makespan and `d_j + D` for the maximum lateness. -/
noncomputable def windowEnd (x : Inst _ s) (D : ℤ) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ∞ :=
  min (Deadlines.view (K := Operations.kernel) (s.module .deadlines) (x.data .deadlines) j)
    (match s.objective with
      | .makespan => (D.toNat : ℕ∞)
      | .lmax => (((due s x j : ℤ) + D).toNat : ℕ∞)
      | _ => ⊤)

/-- `pw(I)`: the largest number of time windows containing one instant, minus
one. -/
noncomputable def pw : TParameter (problem _ s) := fun x D =>
  overlap (fun j => (x.base.r j : ℕ∞)) (windowEnd s x D) - 1

/-- The maximum slack: the largest window length minus processing time. -/
noncomputable def slackmax : TParameter (problem _ s) := fun x D =>
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => (windowEnd s x D j).toNat - ptime x.base j - x.base.r j

/-- `τ`: the number of forbidden times, the instants at which no job may start or end. -/
def tau : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  (ForbiddenTimes.view (s.module .forbiddenTimes) (x.data .forbiddenTimes)).dedup.length

/-- `n_max`: the largest number of operations of a job. -/
def nmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => Finset.univ.sup x.base.ops

/-- `g`: the number of batches into which batch setups group the jobs. -/
def numBatches : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  (Finset.univ.image fun j => ShopExtras.BatchSetups.batch (x := x.base.toShop)
    (s.module .batchSetups) (x.data .batchSetups) j).card

/-- Two different jobs related in neither direction by the precedence order. -/
def Incomparable (x : Inst _ s) (i j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Prop :=
  i ≠ j ∧ ¬ Relation.TransGen (prec s x) i j ∧ ¬ Relation.TransGen (prec s x) j i

/-- A feasible solution of [CS-LP] (Correa and Schulz; Ambühl and Mastrolilli 2009). -/
def CSFeasible (x : Inst _ s) (δ : Fin x.base.jobs → Fin x.base.jobs → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, 0 ≤ δ i j) ∧
  (∀ i j, Incomparable s x i j → 1 ≤ δ i j + δ j i) ∧
  (∀ i j k, Relation.TransGen (prec s x) i j → Incomparable s x j k → Incomparable s x k i →
    1 ≤ δ i k + δ k j) ∧
  (∀ i j k l, Relation.TransGen (prec s x) i j → Incomparable s x j k →
    Relation.TransGen (prec s x) k l → Incomparable s x l i → 1 ≤ δ i l + δ k j)

open Classical in
/-- The objective of [CS-LP]. -/
noncomputable def csValue (x : Inst _ s) (δ : Fin x.base.jobs → Fin x.base.jobs → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, (ptime x.base j * weight s x j : ℝ) +
    ∑ i, ∑ j, (if Relation.TransGen (prec s x) i j then (ptime x.base i * weight s x j : ℝ)
      else if Incomparable s x i j then δ i j * ptime x.base i * weight s x j else 0)

/-- The optimum of [CS-LP], a lower bound on the total weighted completion time
on one machine. -/
noncomputable def csLP (x : Inst _ s) : ℝ :=
  sInf (csValue s x '' {δ | CSFeasible s x δ})

/-- `D − LP`: the threshold minus the optimum of [CS-LP], rounded up, and `0`
when negative. -/
noncomputable def gapLP : TParameter (problem _ s) := fun x D => ⌈(D : ℝ) - csLP s x⌉₊

end Ops

namespace Batch

variable (s : Spec BatchFamily.family)

/-- The number of jobs. -/
def n : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => x.base.jobs

/-- The largest processing time. -/
def pmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => Finset.univ.sup x.base.p

/-- The number of distinct processing times. -/
def numP : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ZooParameters.distinct x.base.p

/-- The number of distinct release dates. -/
def numR : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ZooParameters.distinct x.base.r

/-- The number of distinct weights. -/
def numW : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  ZooParameters.weights BatchFamily.kernel s.objective x.base x.objectiveData

/-- The number of distinct due dates. -/
def numD : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x =>
  ZooParameters.dueDates BatchFamily.kernel s.objective x.base x.objectiveData

/-- The weight of a job. -/
def weight (x : Inst _ s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.weight (K := BatchFamily.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The largest weight. -/
def wmax : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => Finset.univ.sup (weight s x)

/-- The total weight. -/

/-- The total processing time. -/
def totalP : Parameter (problem _ s) := fun x => ∑ j, x.base.p j

/-- The due date of a job. -/
def due (x : Inst _ s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.dueDate (K := BatchFamily.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The end of the time window of a job with the threshold `D`, as on the
operations family. -/
noncomputable def windowEnd (x : Inst _ s) (D : ℤ) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ∞ :=
  min (Deadlines.view (K := BatchFamily.kernel) (s.module (.field .deadlines))
      (x.data (.field .deadlines)) j)
    (match s.objective with
      | .makespan => (D.toNat : ℕ∞)
      | .lmax => (((due s x j : ℤ) + D).toNat : ℕ∞)
      | _ => ⊤)

/-- `pw(I)`: the largest number of time windows containing one instant, minus
one. -/
noncomputable def pw : TParameter (problem _ s) := fun x D =>
  overlap (fun j => (x.base.r j : ℕ∞)) (windowEnd s x D) - 1

/-- The maximum slack: the largest window length minus processing time. -/
noncomputable def slackmax : TParameter (problem _ s) := fun x D =>
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => (windowEnd s x D j).toNat - x.base.p j - x.base.r j

end Batch

namespace Reject

/-- The number of jobs. -/
def n : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x => x.jobs

/-- The number of distinct processing times. -/
def numP : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x => ZooParameters.distinct x.p

/-- The largest processing time. -/
def pmax : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x => Finset.univ.sup x.p

/-- The number of distinct rejection costs. -/
def numE : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x => ZooParameters.distinct x.e

/-- The largest rejection cost. -/
def emax : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x => Finset.univ.sup x.e

/-- The least number of jobs a feasible solution accepts: `n` minus the most
jobs whose rejection costs fit the budget. -/
noncomputable def accepted : Parameter Rejection.problem := fun x =>
  x.jobs - sSup {k | ∃ S : Finset (Fin x.jobs), S.card = k ∧ ∑ j ∈ S, x.e j ≤ x.budget}

end Reject

namespace Cover

/-- The number of jobs. -/
def n : Parameter MachineCovering.problem := fun x => x.jobs

def m : Parameter MachineCovering.problem := fun x => x.machines

end Cover
