concepts.title: The kinds of results on scheduling problems
concepts.description:
A result on a scheduling problem is a statement about its decision version on
words, about algorithms that output schedules, or about online play. Such
statements depend on how instances and schedules are written, so they are made
relative to a reading of the problem: which words encode which instance, which
words write which schedule, and what an online scheduler sees at each time. A
reading of a family gives one for every specification. The results of the
literature are claims about the standard binary readings; here every result
is a proposition about a given reading.

Fix a reading and parameters $\kappa$: functions of the instance and the
threshold into the naturals (most depend on the instance only; some, such as the
pathwidth of time windows that end at the threshold, depend on both). The decision version on words: a word of an instance, then the sign
and absolute value of an integral threshold $D$, is a yes-instance if some
feasible schedule has cost at most $D$. Running times are those of the word RAM
(lax-496464, lax-808846).

**Exact algorithms and hardness.** *In P*: decided in time $c\,(|w|+1)^d$ in
the bit size $|w|$. *Pseudo-polynomial*: in time $c\,(M+1)^e(|w|+1)^d$, where
$M$ is the largest number of the word. *NP-hard*: `NPHardIn` of lax-496464;
*strongly NP-hard*: NP-hard on the words whose numbers are at most
$c\,(\text{length}+1)^d$. *In P (pseudo-polynomial) for every fixed value* of
$\kappa$; *FPT*, *W[t]-hard* (strongly: on such words), *para-NP-hard*: NP-hard
for one fixed value.

**Running times.** An algorithm can be stated with its exact running time, a
function $T$ of the instance (of $n$, $m$, $p_{\max}$, the total weight, …): one
program halts, writing the answer for the instance and the threshold, within
$c\,(T(x)+1)$ instructions on the word of every instance $x$, at every word length $\ell$ with $(|w| + M + 2)^c \le 2^\ell$, where $|w|$ is
the length of the word and $M$ its largest number — words of $O(\log)$ bits, as
on the word RAM of the literature. Deciding, approximating, approximating with
random bits and approximation schemes each have such a form; a submitted
algorithm is a program with a proof of one of them. Deciding can also be stated
without the constant: one program halts with the answer within exactly $T(x, D)$
instructions, a function of the instance and the threshold, at the same word lengths.

**Randomized deciding.** The program reads, after the word, at most $c\,(T(x)+1)$
random bits and halts within $c\,(T(x)+1)$ instructions on every choice of them.
With *bounded error* its answer is right for at least two thirds of the choices.
With *one-sided error* it never accepts a no-instance and accepts a yes-instance
for at least half of the choices. With *zero error* (Las Vegas) it is always
right and the bound $c\,(T(x)+1)$ holds for the number of instructions averaged
over the choices. Repetition turns any of these into error $2^{-k}$ at $k$ times
the cost, so the constants $2/3$ and $1/2$ are not essential.

**Approximation.** A ratio is a function $\rho$ of the instance into the reals.
A $\rho$-approximation is a polynomial-time program that on the word of an
instance with a feasible schedule writes the word of a feasible schedule
costing at most $\rho$ times every feasible schedule; for a maximization
problem, whose cost is the negative of its value, the value is at least $\rho$
times every value. A randomized one reads polynomially many random bits; every
choice gives a feasible schedule, the average cost is within the ratio, and
the running time is polynomial in the worst case or, for an expected-time
algorithm, on average over the bits. Approximations may be restricted to the
instances of a set. PTAS, EPTAS and FPTAS are as usual; inapproximability below
$\rho$ unless P = NP says that if P ≠ NP no $\rho'$-approximation exists for a
constant $\rho' < \rho$. An *additive* $\delta$-approximation writes a feasible
schedule costing at most every feasible cost plus $\delta$, a function of the
instance; an additive scheme does so with $\varepsilon\,\delta$ for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, in polynomial time for each fixed $\varepsilon$. A
*parameterized approximation scheme* for a parameter $\kappa$ is one program that
writes a $(1 + a/b)$-approximate schedule from the word of an instance followed
by $a, b$, in time $f(\kappa + b/a)\,(|w|+1)^d$.

**Running times and word size.** A running time, upper or lower, is stated with
short words, $\ell \ge c \log_2(|u| + M + 2)$; the classes keep the long words
of the registered notions and are reached from running times through the
transfer theorems. A lower bound is stated for the time plus the length of the
shortest word of the instance.

**Wide words.** An algorithm whose running time $T$ exceeds every polynomial may
need words that hold the address of every step, $c\,(T(x)+1) \le 2^\ell$ besides
the short words above; this is the standard assumption for such algorithms, whose
tables are as large as their running times. Deciding within $O(T)$ with wide words
asks the program to work only at those word lengths.

**Restrictions.** A result may hold on the instances satisfying a predicate
$\varphi$ only: it is then a result on the problem restricted to them, read with the
same words.

**Kept weight.** A problem that minimizes the weight of the jobs it rejects
(late, or not just in time) is read with the same instances, schedules and
costs when a source maximizes the weight it keeps. The kept weight of a
schedule is the total weight $W$ of the instance minus its cost. A
$\rho$-approximation of the kept weight, for $\rho \le 1$, writes a feasible
schedule that keeps at least $\rho$ times the weight of every feasible
schedule; schemes keep $1 - a/b$ times it. An online algorithm is
$\rho$-competitive for the kept weight, $\rho \ge 1$, if every feasible schedule
keeps at most $\rho$ times what the algorithm keeps plus a constant, the
convention of the sources on throughput.

**Kernels.** A kernelization for a parameter is a polynomial-time map on the
words of instances that keeps the answer and whose output has size (bit length)
and parameter at most $g(\kappa)$ for a computable $g$; a polynomial kernel has
$g$ polynomial.

**The exponential time hypothesis.** A formula is written as the number $n$ of
variables followed, for every clause, by its length and its literals, the
literal of variable $v$ being $2v+1$ if positive and $2v$ if negative. ETH: for
some $q > 0$ no program decides the satisfiability of formulas whose clauses have
three literals over variables below $n$ within $c\,2^{\lfloor n/q \rfloor}(|w|+1)^c$
instructions, at the word lengths above. A function $f$ is $o(g)$ if for every
rational $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $f(k) \le \varepsilon\, g(k)$.

**Online.** A deterministic algorithm is $\rho$-competitive if it is
non-anticipative for the revelation and, for some additive constant, its cost is
at most $\rho$ times every feasible cost plus that constant; a randomized one is
a finite distribution over non-anticipative algorithms. A lower bound $\rho$
says that no algorithm is $\rho'$-competitive for $\rho' < \rho$.

choice gives a feasible schedule, the average cost is within the ratio, and
the running time is polynomial in the worst case or, for an expected-time
algorithm, on average over the bits. Approximations may be restricted to the
instances of a set. PTAS, EPTAS and FPTAS are as usual; inapproximability below
$\rho$ unless P = NP says that if P ≠ NP no $\rho'$-approximation exists for a
constant $\rho' < \rho$. An *additive* $\delta$-approximation writes a feasible
schedule costing at most every feasible cost plus $\delta$, a function of the
instance; an additive scheme does so with $\varepsilon\,\delta$ for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, in polynomial time for each fixed $\varepsilon$. A
*parameterized approximation scheme* for a parameter $\kappa$ is one program that
writes a $(1 + a/b)$-approximate schedule from the word of an instance followed
by $a, b$, in time $f(\kappa + b/a)\,(|w|+1)^d$.

**Running times and word size.** A running time, upper or lower, is stated with
short words, $\ell \ge c \log_2(|u| + M + 2)$; the classes keep the long words
of the registered notions and are reached from running times through the
transfer theorems. A lower bound is stated for the time plus the length of the
shortest word of the instance.

**Wide words.** An algorithm whose running time $T$ exceeds every polynomial may
need words that hold the address of every step, $c\,(T(x)+1) \le 2^\ell$ besides
the short words above; this is the standard assumption for such algorithms, whose
tables are as large as their running times. Deciding within $O(T)$ with wide words
asks the program to work only at those word lengths.

**Restrictions.** A result may hold on the instances satisfying a predicate
$\varphi$ only: it is then a result on the problem restricted to them, read with the
same words.

**Kept weight.** A problem that minimizes the weight of the jobs it rejects
(late, or not just in time) is read with the same instances, schedules and
costs when a source maximizes the weight it keeps. The kept weight of a
schedule is the total weight $W$ of the instance minus its cost. A
$\rho$-approximation of the kept weight, for $\rho \le 1$, writes a feasible
schedule that keeps at least $\rho$ times the weight of every feasible
schedule; schemes keep $1 - a/b$ times it. An online algorithm is
$\rho$-competitive for the kept weight, $\rho \ge 1$, if every feasible schedule
keeps at most $\rho$ times what the algorithm keeps plus a constant, the
convention of the sources on throughput.

**Kernels.** A kernelization for a parameter is a polynomial-time map on the
words of instances that keeps the answer and whose output has size (bit length)
and parameter at most $g(\kappa)$ for a computable $g$; a polynomial kernel has
$g$ polynomial.

**The exponential time hypothesis.** A formula is written as the number $n$ of
variables followed, for every clause, by its length and its literals, the
literal of variable $v$ being $2v+1$ if positive and $2v$ if negative. ETH: for
some $q > 0$ no program decides the satisfiability of formulas whose clauses have
three literals over variables below $n$ within $c\,2^{\lfloor n/q \rfloor}(|w|+1)^c$
instructions, at the word lengths above. A function $f$ is $o(g)$ if for every
rational $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $f(k) \le \varepsilon\, g(k)$.

**Online.** A deterministic algorithm is $\rho$-competitive if it is
non-anticipative for the revelation and, for some additive constant, its cost is
at most $\rho$ times every feasible cost plus that constant; a randomized one is
a finite distribution over non-anticipative algorithms. A lower bound $\rho$
says that no algorithm is $\rho'$-competitive for $\rho' < \rho$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Results
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Parameters
open Lax434175.WordProblems Lax434175.Online
open Lax808846.Ram Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding
open Lax496464.WH_A1_FptTime Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions Lax496464.WH_B4_Hierarchies

/-- Parameterized problems on words. -/
abbrev WP := Lax888481.ParameterizedComplexity.Problem

/-- A reading of a problem: words of instances, schedules from words, and what
an online scheduler sees. -/
structure PReading (P : Problem) where
  /-- The word encodes the instance. -/
  Encodes : List ℕ → P.Inst → Prop
  /-- The word writes the schedule of the instance. -/
  Decodes : (x : P.Inst) → List ℕ → P.Sched x → Prop
  /-- What is revealed over time. -/
  reveal : Revelation P

/-- A reading of a family. -/
structure Reading {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) where
  /-- The word encodes the instance. -/
  Encodes : (s : Spec F) → List ℕ → Inst F s → Prop
  /-- The word writes the schedule of the instance. -/
  Decodes : (s : Spec F) → (x : Inst F s) → List ℕ → (problem F s).Sched x → Prop
  /-- What is revealed over time. -/
  reveal : (s : Spec F) → Revelation (problem F s)

/-- The reading of the problem of one specification. -/
def Reading.at {K : Kernel} {F : Family K} (R : Reading F) (s : Spec F) :
    PReading (problem F s) :=
  ⟨R.Encodes s, R.Decodes s, R.reveal s⟩

/-- The reading of a problem on the instances satisfying `φ`: the same words. -/
def PReading.restrict {P : Problem} (R : PReading P) (φ : P.Inst → Prop) :
    PReading (P.restrict φ) where
  Encodes w x := R.Encodes w x.1
  Decodes x w σ := R.Decodes x.1 w σ
  reveal := ⟨fun x y t => R.reveal.same x.1 y.1 t, fun x y σ τ t => R.reveal.agree x.1 y.1 σ τ t⟩

/-- A parameter of the decision version: a function of the instance and the
threshold. -/
abbrev TParameter (P : Problem) := P.Inst → ℤ → ℕ

/-- A parameter of the instance, ignoring the threshold. -/
def lift {P : Problem} (κ : Parameter P) : TParameter P := fun x _ => κ x

/-- The sum of two parameters. -/
def tplus {P : Problem} (κ κ' : TParameter P) : TParameter P := fun x D => κ x D + κ' x D

variable {P : Problem} (R : PReading P)

-- Words

/-- The largest number of a word. -/
def maxEntry (w : List ℕ) : ℕ := w.foldr max 0

/-- The word presents the instance with the threshold. -/
def EncodesDecision (w : List ℕ) (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ y, w = y ++ [if D < 0 then 1 else 0, D.natAbs] ∧ R.Encodes y x

open Classical in
/-- The decision version with a parameter, as a parameterized problem on words. -/
noncomputable def parameterized (κ : TParameter P) : WP where
  Domain := {w | ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D}
  Yes w := ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D ∧ P.Decides x D
  param w := if h : ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D then κ h.choose h.choose_spec.choose else 0

/-- The decision version on words. -/
noncomputable def decision : WP := parameterized R fun _ => 0

open Classical in
/-- The answer of a word, `[1]` or `[0]`. -/
noncomputable def answer (Q : WP) (w : List ℕ) : List ℕ := if Q.Yes w then [1] else [0]

/-- The problem on fewer words. -/
def restrict (Q : WP) (D : Set (List ℕ)) : WP where
  Domain := Q.Domain ∩ D
  Yes := Q.Yes
  param := Q.param

/-- The words whose numbers are polynomial in their length. -/
def Small (c d : ℕ) : Set (List ℕ) := {w | ∀ v ∈ w, v ≤ c * (w.length + 1) ^ d}

/-- The words of instances with parameter at most `k`. -/
def Upto (κ : TParameter P) (k : ℕ) : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {w | ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D ∧ κ x D ≤ k}

-- Exact algorithms and hardness

/-- Decided in polynomial time. -/
def PolyDecides (Q : WP) : Prop := PolyTimeOn Q.Domain (answer Q)

/-- Decided in pseudo-polynomial time. -/
def PseudoPolyDecides (Q : WP) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ),
    ComputesInFptTime p Q.Domain maxEntry (answer Q) (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d

/-- The problem is in P. -/
def InP : Prop := PolyDecides (decision R)

/-- The problem is solvable in pseudo-polynomial time. -/
def PseudoPoly : Prop := PseudoPolyDecides (decision R)

/-- The problem is NP-hard. -/
def NPHard : Prop := Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (decision R)

/-- The problem is strongly NP-hard. -/
def StronglyNPHard : Prop :=
  ∃ c d, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (restrict (decision R) (Small c d))

/-- In P for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
def InPFixed (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, PolyDecides (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))

/-- Pseudo-polynomial for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
def PseudoPolyFixed (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, PseudoPolyDecides (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))

/-- Fixed-parameter tractable. -/
def IsFPT (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := parameterized R κ ∈ FPT

/-- W[t]-hard. -/
def WHard (t : ℕ) (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := Hard (W t) (parameterized R κ)

/-- Strongly W[t]-hard: W[t]-hard on the words whose numbers are polynomial in
their length. -/
def StronglyWHard (t : ℕ) (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ c d, Hard (W t) (restrict (parameterized R κ) (Small c d))

/-- Para-NP-hard: NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter. -/
def ParaNPHard (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))

/-- Strongly NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter. -/
def StronglyParaNPHard (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ k c d, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn
    (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k ∩ Small c d))

-- Approximation

open Classical in
/-- The length of the shortest word of the instance, `0` if it has none. Lower
bounds on running times are stated for a time plus this length, so that they
cannot hold just because the input cannot be read. -/
noncomputable def inputSize (x : P.Inst) : ℕ := sInf {k | ∃ w, R.Encodes w x ∧ w.length = k}

/-- The instance has a feasible schedule. -/
def Solvable (x : P.Inst) : Prop := ∃ τ, P.feasible x τ

/-- `σ` is feasible and within the ratio of every feasible schedule. -/
def Within (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
  P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (P.cost x σ : ℝ) ≤ ρ * P.cost x τ

/-- For a maximization problem: `σ` is feasible and its value is at least `ρ`
times every value. -/
def WithinMax (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
  P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → ρ * (-(P.cost x τ : ℝ)) ≤ -(P.cost x σ : ℝ)

/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the ratio. -/
def Good (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ Within (ρ x) x σ

/-- The same for a maximization problem. -/
def GoodMax (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinMax (ρ x) x σ

/-- All instances. -/
def univ : Set P.Inst := Set.univ

/-- A constant ratio. -/
def const (ρ : ℝ) : P.Inst → ℝ := fun _ => ρ

/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation on the instances of `S`. -/
def ApproxOn (S : Set P.Inst) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x ∈ S, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → x ∈ S → Solvable x → Good R ρ x (A w)

/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation. -/
def Approx (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop := ApproxOn R univ ρ

/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation for a maximization problem. -/
def ApproxMax (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodMax R ρ x (A w)

/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
def ApproxFixed (κ : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, ApproxOn R {x | κ x ≤ k} ρ

/-- The random bits `r` as a word. -/
def bits {L : ℕ} (r : Fin L → Bool) : List ℕ := List.ofFn fun i => if r i then 1 else 0

/-- Every choice of the random bits gives a feasible schedule, and the average
cost is within the ratio. -/
def GoodOnAverage {L : ℕ} (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : (Fin L → Bool) → List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : (Fin L → Bool) → P.Sched x,
    (∀ r, R.Decodes x (out r) (σ r) ∧ P.feasible x (σ r)) ∧
    ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (∑ r, (P.cost x (σ r) : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L ≤ ρ * P.cost x τ

/-- A randomized polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation: it reads `L(|w|)` random
bits, with `L` polynomial, and runs in polynomial time on every choice. -/
def RandomApprox (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ) (c e : ℕ), (∀ n, L n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ e) ∧
    PolyTimeOn {u | ∃ w x, R.Encodes w x ∧ ∃ r : Fin (L (bitSize w)) → Bool, u = w ++ bits r} A ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x →
      GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x fun r : Fin (L (bitSize w)) → Bool => A (w ++ bits r)

/-- The word lengths a program may use on input `u`: `c` times the logarithm of
the length plus the largest number. -/
def WordOk (c : ℕ) (u : List ℕ) (ℓ : ℕ) : Prop := (u.length + maxEntry u + 2) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ ℓ

/-- A randomized `ρ`-approximation in expected polynomial time: averaged over
the random bits, the number of instructions is at most `c (|w|+1)^c`. -/
def RandomApproxExpected (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, L n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ c) ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x →
      ∃ out : (Fin (L w.length) → Bool) → List ℕ, GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x out ∧
        ∀ ℓ, (∀ r : Fin (L w.length) → Bool, WordOk c (w ++ bits r) ℓ) →
          ∃ t : (Fin (L w.length) → Bool) → ℕ,
            (∀ r, RunsTo ℓ p ((w ++ bits r).length :: (w ++ bits r)) (out r) (t r)) ∧
            (∑ r, (t r : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L w.length ≤ c * (w.length + 1 : ℝ) ^ c

/-- A polynomial-time approximation scheme. -/
def PTAS : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → Approx R (const (1 + ε))

/-- A PTAS for a maximization problem: value at least `1 - ε` times every
value. -/
def PTASMax : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ApproxMax R (const (1 - ε))

/-- A PTAS for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
def PTASFixed (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∀ k (ε : ℚ), 0 < ε → ApproxOn R {x | κ x ≤ k} (const (1 + ε))

/-- The words of instances followed by a precision `a / b`. -/
def WordsEps : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {u | ∃ w x, R.Encodes w x ∧ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ u = w ++ [a, b]}

/-- One program writes a `(1 + a / b)`-approximate schedule from the word of an
instance followed by `a, b`. -/
def Scheme (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ w x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes w x → 0 < a → 0 < b → Solvable x →
    Good R (const (1 + (a : ℝ) / b)) x (A (w ++ [a, b]))

/-- An efficient PTAS: time `f(b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
def EPTAS : Prop :=
  ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A

/-- A fully polynomial-time approximation scheme: time polynomial in `|w|` and
`b/a`. -/
def FPTAS : Prop :=
  ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ), ComputesInFptTime p (WordsEps R)
    (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d

/-- P ≠ NP. -/
def PneNP : Prop :=
  Lax434930.PolynomialTime.P ≠ Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP

/-- No `ρ'`-approximation for a constant `ρ' < ρ` on the instances of `S`,
unless P = NP. -/
def NoApproxBelowOn (S : Set P.Inst) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  PneNP → ∀ ρ' : ℝ, ρ' < ρ → ¬ ApproxOn R S (const ρ')

/-- No `ρ'`-approximation for a constant `ρ' < ρ`, unless P = NP. -/
def NoApproxBelow (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := NoApproxBelowOn R univ ρ

/-- No PTAS unless P = NP (the consequence of APX-hardness). -/
def NoPTAS : Prop := PneNP → ¬ PTAS R

/-- `σ` is feasible and costs at most every feasible cost plus `δ`. -/
def WithinAdd (δ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
  P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (P.cost x σ : ℝ) ≤ P.cost x τ + δ

/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the additive error. -/
def GoodAdd (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinAdd (δ x) x σ

/-- A polynomial-time approximation with additive error `δ`. -/
def ApproxAdd (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodAdd R δ x (A w)

/-- An additive approximation scheme: additive error `ε δ` for every `ε > 0`, in polynomial
time for each fixed `ε`. -/
def AddScheme (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ApproxAdd R fun x => (ε : ℝ) * δ x

open Classical in
/-- The parameter of the instance a word followed by a precision writes, plus the inverse
precision `b / a`. -/
noncomputable def paramEps (κ : Parameter P) (u : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (if h : ∃ x, R.Encodes (u.dropLast.dropLast) x then κ h.choose else 0) +
    u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1

/-- A parameterized approximation scheme: time `f(κ + b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
def ParamScheme (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (paramEps R κ) A

/-- A kernelization: a polynomial-time map on the words of instances with a threshold that
keeps the answer and the words, and whose output has size and parameter at most `g κ`. -/
def KernelWithin (κ : TParameter P) (g : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn (parameterized R κ).Domain K ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (parameterized R κ).Domain, K w ∈ (parameterized R κ).Domain ∧
      ((parameterized R κ).Yes w ↔ (parameterized R κ).Yes (K w)) ∧
      bitSize (K w) ≤ g ((parameterized R κ).param w) ∧
      (parameterized R κ).param (K w) ≤ g ((parameterized R κ).param w)

/-- A kernel: a kernelization for a computable `g`. -/
def HasKernel (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := ∃ g, Computable g ∧ KernelWithin R κ g

/-- A polynomial kernel: a kernelization with `g` polynomial. -/
def PolyKernel (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := ∃ c d : ℕ, KernelWithin R κ fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ d

-- Kept weight

/-- `σ` is feasible and keeps at least `ρ` times the weight every feasible
schedule keeps, the kept weight being the total weight minus the cost. -/
def WithinKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
  P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
    ρ * ((total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ) ≤ (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x σ

/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the ratio of
the kept weight. -/
def GoodKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinKept total (ρ x) x σ

/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation of the kept weight, `ρ ≤ 1`. -/
def ApproxKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
    ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodKept R total ρ x (A w)

/-- One program keeps `1 - a / b` times the optimal kept weight, from the word
of an instance followed by `a, b` with `a < b`. -/
def SchemeKept (total : Parameter P) (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ w x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes w x → 0 < a → a < b → Solvable x →
    GoodKept R total (const (1 - (a : ℝ) / b)) x (A (w ++ [a, b]))

/-- A PTAS for the kept weight. -/
def PTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ApproxKept R total (const (1 - ε))

/-- An efficient PTAS for the kept weight: time `f(b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
def EPTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧
    FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A

/-- An FPTAS for the kept weight: time polynomial in `|w|` and `b/a`. -/
def FPTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧ ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ), ComputesInFptTime p (WordsEps R)
    (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d

/-- A parameterized approximation scheme for the kept weight. -/
def ParamSchemeKept (total : Parameter P) (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (paramEps R κ) A

/-- No `ρ'`-approximation of the kept weight for a constant `ρ' > ρ`, unless
P = NP. -/
def NoApproxKeptAbove (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  PneNP → ∀ ρ' : ℝ, ρ < ρ' → ¬ ApproxKept R total (const ρ')

-- Running times

open Classical in
/-- The answer for an instance and a threshold: `[1]` if some feasible schedule
costs at most the threshold, `[0]` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def verdict (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) : List ℕ := if P.Decides x D then [1] else [0]

/-- One program decides the decision version within `O(T(x))` instructions: on
every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D` it writes the answer for `x`
and `D`. -/
def DecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t

/-- One program decides the decision version within `T x D` instructions, with no
hidden constant: on every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D` it writes the
answer within `T x D` steps of the word RAM. -/
def DecidesExact (T : P.Inst → ℤ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ t ≤ T x D, RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t

/-- One program decides the decision version within `O(T(x))` instructions with wide
words: on every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D`, at every word length `ℓ` with
`WordOk c u ℓ` and `c (T(x) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ ℓ`, it writes the answer for `x` and `D` within
`c (T(x) + 1)` instructions. This is the standard assumption for algorithms whose running
time exceeds a polynomial: a word holds the address of every step. -/
def DecidesWithinWide (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → c * (T x + 1) ≤ 2 ^ ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t

open Classical in
/-- The choices of `L` random bits for which `out` writes the answer for `x` and `D`. -/
noncomputable def rightChoices {L : ℕ} (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) (out : (Fin L → Bool) → List ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun r => out r = verdict x D).card

/-- A randomized program decides the decision version with bounded error within
`O(T(x))` instructions: on the word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D`
followed by at most `O(T(x))` random bits, it halts within `O(T(x))`
instructions on every choice, and writes the answer for at least two thirds of
the choices. -/
def RandomDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
    ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ,
      2 * 2 ^ L u.length ≤ 3 * rightChoices x D out ∧
      ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
        RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t

/-- The same with one-sided error: a no-instance is never accepted, and a
yes-instance is accepted for at least half of the choices. -/
def OneSidedDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
    ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ,
      (∀ r, out r = verdict x D ∨ out r = [0]) ∧
      2 ^ L u.length ≤ 2 * rightChoices x D out ∧
      ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
        RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t

/-- The same with zero error (Las Vegas): the answer is always right, and the
number of instructions, averaged over the choices, is `O(T(x))`. -/
def ZeroErrorDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
    L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
    ∀ ℓ, (∀ r : Fin (L u.length) → Bool, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ) →
      ∃ t : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → ℕ,
        (∀ r, RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (verdict x D) (t r)) ∧
        (∑ r, (t r : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L u.length ≤ c * ((T x : ℝ) + 1)

/-- A `ρ`-approximation running within `O(T(x))` instructions. -/
def ApproxWithin (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x, R.Encodes u x → Solvable x →
    ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) out t ∧ Good R ρ x out

/-- A randomized `ρ`-approximation running within `O(T(x))` instructions on
every choice of random bits and reading at most that many. -/
def RandomApproxWithin (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x, R.Encodes u x → Solvable x →
    L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
    ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ, GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x out ∧
      ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
        RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t

/-- An approximation scheme: one program reads the word of an instance and `a, b`
and writes a `(1 + a/b)`-approximate schedule within `O(T(a/b, x))`
instructions. -/
def SchemeWithin (T : ℚ → P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes u x → 0 < a → 0 < b →
    Solvable x → ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ [a, b]) ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T ((a : ℚ) / b) x + 1),
      RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ [a, b]).length :: (u ++ [a, b])) out t ∧
      Good R (const (1 + (a : ℝ) / b)) x out

/-- The same for a maximization problem: value at least `1 - a/b` times every
value, for `a < b`. -/
def SchemeMaxWithin (T : ℚ → P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes u x → 0 < a → a < b →
    Solvable x → ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ [a, b]) ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T ((a : ℚ) / b) x + 1),
      RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ [a, b]).length :: (u ++ [a, b])) out t ∧
      GoodMax R (const (1 - (a : ℝ) / b)) x out

-- The exponential time hypothesis

/-- The word of a formula on `n` variables. -/
def formulaWord (n : ℕ) (Φ : Lax429075.CNF.Formula) : List ℕ :=
  n :: Φ.flatMap fun C => C.length :: C.map fun l => 2 * l.index + if l.positive then 1 else 0

open Classical in
/-- The exponential time hypothesis: for some `q > 0`, no program decides 3-SAT
on `n` variables within `c · 2^⌊n/q⌋ · (|w|+1)^c` instructions. -/
def ETH : Prop :=
  ∃ q : ℕ, 0 < q ∧ ∀ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (Φ : Lax429075.CNF.Formula),
    (∀ C ∈ Φ, C.length = 3 ∧ ∀ l ∈ C, l.index < n) →
    ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (formulaWord n Φ) ℓ →
      ∃ t ≤ c * 2 ^ (n / q) * ((formulaWord n Φ).length + 1) ^ c,
        RunsTo ℓ p ((formulaWord n Φ).length :: formulaWord n Φ)
          (if Lax429075.CNF.Satisfiable Φ then [1] else [0]) t

/-- `f` is `o(g)`. -/
def LittleO (f g : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, (f k : ℚ) ≤ ε * g k

-- Online

/-- A deterministic algorithm with ratio `ρ` and additive constant `α`, over the
reals. -/
def CompetitiveR (A : Algorithm P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, P.feasible x (A x) ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
    (P.cost x (A x) : ℝ) ≤ ρ x * P.cost x τ + α

/-- Some non-anticipative deterministic algorithm is `ρ`-competitive. -/
def DetCompetitive (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A α, NonAnticipative R.reveal A ∧ CompetitiveR A ρ α

/-- A distribution over non-anticipative algorithms is `ρ`-competitive. -/
def RandCompetitive (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (μ : Randomized R.reveal) (α : ℝ), ∀ x,
    (∀ a ∈ μ.algorithms, P.feasible x (a.2 x)) ∧
    ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (μ.cost x : ℝ) ≤ ρ x * P.cost x τ + α

/-- No deterministic algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for a constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
def DetLowerBound (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ DetCompetitive R (const ρ')

/-- No randomized algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for a constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
def RandLowerBound (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ RandCompetitive R (const ρ')

/-- For some `c > 0`, no deterministic algorithm is `c f`-competitive. -/
def DetLowerBoundFn (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ DetCompetitive R fun x => c * f x

/-- For some `c > 0`, no randomized algorithm is `c f`-competitive. -/
def RandLowerBoundFn (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ RandCompetitive R fun x => c * f x

-- Online, kept weight

/-- A deterministic algorithm with ratio `ρ ≥ 1` and additive constant `α` for
the kept weight: every feasible schedule keeps at most `ρ` times what the
algorithm keeps, plus `α`. -/
def CompetitiveKeptR (total : Parameter P) (A : Algorithm P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, P.feasible x (A x) ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
    (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ ≤ ρ x * ((total x : ℝ) - P.cost x (A x)) + α

/-- Some non-anticipative deterministic algorithm is `ρ`-competitive for the
kept weight. -/
def DetCompetitiveKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A α, NonAnticipative R.reveal A ∧ CompetitiveKeptR total A ρ α

/-- A distribution over non-anticipative algorithms is `ρ`-competitive for the
kept weight, in expectation. -/
def RandCompetitiveKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (μ : Randomized R.reveal) (α : ℝ), ∀ x,
    (∀ a ∈ μ.algorithms, P.feasible x (a.2 x)) ∧
    ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ ≤ ρ x * ((total x : ℝ) - μ.cost x) + α

/-- No deterministic algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for the kept weight, for a
constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
def DetLowerBoundKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ DetCompetitiveKept R total (const ρ')

/-- No randomized algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for the kept weight, for a
constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
def RandLowerBoundKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ RandCompetitiveKept R total (const ρ')

/-- For some `c > 0`, no deterministic algorithm is `c f`-competitive for the
kept weight. -/
def DetLowerBoundFnKept (total : Parameter P) (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ DetCompetitiveKept R total fun x => c * f x

/-- For some `c > 0`, no randomized algorithm is `c f`-competitive for the kept
weight. -/
def RandLowerBoundFnKept (total : Parameter P) (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ RandCompetitiveKept R total fun x => c * f x

end Lax434175.Results

concepts.title: From exact running times to complexity classes
concepts.description:
An algorithm stated with its exact running time — one program deciding the
decision version within $O(T(x))$ instructions on the word of every instance
$x$ (`Results.DecidesWithin`) — gives the coarser results by bounding $T$ alone,
without looking at the program again. Let $|u|$ be the bit size of the word $u$ of
an instance $x$ with a threshold, and $M$ its largest number.

**Theorem.**

1. If $T(x) \le c\,(|u|+1)^d$, the problem is in P.
2. If $T(x) \le c\,(M+1)^e\,(|u|+1)^d$, it is solvable in pseudo-polynomial time.
3. If $T(x) \le c\,(|u|+1)^{g(\kappa)}$ for a function $g$ of the parameter $\kappa$,
   it is in P for every fixed value of $\kappa$.
4. If $T(x) \le f(\kappa)\,(|u|+1)^d$ for a computable $f$ and the parameter is
   computable in polynomial time on the words, it is fixed-parameter tractable
   in $\kappa$.

**Theorem.** A program deciding within exactly $T(x)$ instructions decides within
$O(T(x))$ (`Results.DecidesExact`).

**Theorem.** A program deciding within $O(T(x))$ decides within $O(T(x))$ with wide words
(`Results.DecidesWithinWide`): the wide words are among the short ones.

open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions

variable {P : Problem} (R : PReading P)

axiom decidesWithin_of_exact {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (h : DecidesExact R fun x _ => T x) : DecidesWithin R T

axiom decidesWithinWide_of_decidesWithin {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (h : DecidesWithin R T) :
    DecidesWithinWide R T

axiom inP_of_decidesWithin {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (h : DecidesWithin R T)
    (hT : ∃ c d : ℕ, ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D → T x ≤ c * (bitSize u + 1) ^ d) :
    InP R

axiom pseudoPoly_of_decidesWithin {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (h : DecidesWithin R T)
    (hT : ∃ c e d : ℕ, ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      T x ≤ c * (maxEntry u + 1) ^ e * (bitSize u + 1) ^ d) :
    PseudoPoly R

axiom inPFixed_of_decidesWithin {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (κ : TParameter P) (h : DecidesWithin R T)
    (hT : ∃ (c : ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      T x ≤ c * (bitSize u + 1) ^ g (κ x D)) :
    InPFixed R κ

axiom isFPT_of_decidesWithin {T : P.Inst → ℕ} (κ : TParameter P) (h : DecidesWithin R T)
    (hκ : IsParameterized (parameterized R κ))
    (hT : ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (d : ℕ), Computable f ∧ ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      T x ≤ f (κ x D) * (bitSize u + 1) ^ d) :
    IsFPT R κ

concepts.title: Two tests from the words up: NP-hardness of 1|r_j|L_max and Smith's rule
concepts.description:
A test of the hardness statements end to end, on a registered result. Elffers
and de Weerdt prove single-machine scheduling with release times and deadlines
NP-complete when the job lengths lie in $\{p, q\}$ for fixed $p > q > 1$
(formalized in lax-391470, on binary words). An instance with integer release
times $r_j$ and deadlines $d_j$, all shifted up by the largest absolute value
among them, is an instance of $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ with due dates the shifted
deadlines, and it is feasible exactly when the maximum lateness can be made at
most $0$; its standard word with threshold $0$ is computed from the binary word
in polynomial time.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ is NP-hard on the standard reading.

A test of the algorithmic side end to end: Smith's rule. On one machine, the
total weighted completion time is smallest when the jobs run without idle time
in the order of $p_j / w_j$ (jobs of weight $0$ last). A program reads the
standard word of an instance of $1 \mid\mid \sum w_jC_j$ (not a problem of the
zoo's data, which leaves out problems this easy) and its threshold, sorts the
jobs by comparing $p_iw_j$ with $p_jw_i$, adds up the weighted completion times
and compares with the threshold.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid\mid \sum w_jC_j$ is decided within $O(n \log n)$ instructions,
plus the length of the word, on short words.

axiom npHard_rjLmax : NPHard (StandardReading.ops.at ZooParallel.p158)

/-- `1||ΣwjCj`, a single machine and the total weighted completion time. -/
def singleWC : Spec OperationsFamily.family :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumWC)

instructions plus the length of the word. -/

      (ResultParameters.Ops.n singleWC x + 1) * (Nat.log 2 (ResultParameters.Ops.n singleWC x) + 1) +
        inputSize (StandardReading.ops.at singleWC) x

concepts.title: 1|r_j|L_max is para-NP-hard for the largest and the number of processing times
concepts.description:
The reduction that makes $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ NP-hard (concept `Sanity`, from
lax-391470 with the job lengths $\{3, 2\}$) produces only instances whose
processing times are $2$ or $3$; on a word that is not such an instance it produces
the instance without jobs. So the problem is NP-hard already on the instances with
$p_{\max} \le 3$, and on those with at most two distinct processing times.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ is para-NP-hard parameterized by $p_{\max}$,
and parameterized by the number $\#p$ of distinct processing times, on the
standard reading.

The explicit reductions of lax-391470 (Cook–Levin to satisfiability, then the formula
instance, then the stacked instance) produce release times and deadlines at most a
constant times the number of jobs: the time line of the formula instance has length
$2nS$ with $S$ linear in the number $m$ of clauses, the stacked instance has
$n + (2n-1)m \ge n(m+1)$ connected pairs, five jobs each, and stacking adds at most
$(p + 2q)$ per pair. So every number of the emitted word is linear in its length.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ is strongly NP-hard on the standard reading.

import Lax434175.Sanity
import Lax434175.ZooParallelResults

/-!
---
title: 1|r_j|L_max is para-NP-hard for the largest and the number of processing times
type: theorem
---
The reduction that makes $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ NP-hard (concept `Sanity`, from
lax-391470 with the job lengths $\{3, 2\}$) produces only instances whose
processing times are $2$ or $3$; on a word that is not such an instance it produces
the instance without jobs. So the problem is NP-hard already on the instances with
$p_{\max} \le 3$, and on those with at most two distinct processing times.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ is para-NP-hard parameterized by $p_{\max}$,
and parameterized by the number $\#p$ of distinct processing times, on the
standard reading.

The explicit reductions of lax-391470 (Cook–Levin to satisfiability, then the formula
instance, then the stacked instance) produce release times and deadlines at most a
constant times the number of jobs: the time line of the formula instance has length
$2nS$ with $S$ linear in the number $m$ of clauses, the stacked instance has
$n + (2n-1)m \ge n(m+1)$ connected pairs, five jobs each, and stacking adds at most
$(p + 2q)$ per pair. So every number of the emitted word is linear in its length.

**Theorem.** $1 \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ is strongly NP-hard on the standard reading.
-/

concepts.title: A single server with setup times
concepts.description:
With a single server, every job on parallel machines, and every operation in
a shop, needs a setup immediately before it is processed. The setup of job
$j$ takes $s_j$ time units, during which it occupies both the machines of
the job and the server. Hence

- the setup of a job starts no earlier than its release date $r_j$, so the
  job starts no earlier than $r_j + s_j$; in a shop this holds for the first
  operation of the job, the one that starts when the job starts;
- the setups of two different jobs do not overlap, since there is one
  server;
- of two jobs that share a machine, the later one starts no earlier than the
  completion of the earlier one plus its own setup time.

In a shop the setup of a later operation of a job may overlap the job's
previous operation on another machine: setups are separable, and only the
setup of the first operation waits for the release date. This is the model of
Brucker, Knust and Wang (2005) and of the papers of the same group on a single
server.

The field has the value "none", without server and setups, and three values
with a server: unit setup times, equal setup times, and arbitrary setup
times. Unit is a special case of equal and equal of arbitrary; the value
none is incomparable with the others.

**Theorem.** The server field is sound over every machine model on parallel
machines and for shops.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Rat
import Lax434175.ParallelMachines
import Lax434175.Shops

/-!
---
title: A single server with setup times
type: theorem
---
With a single server, every job on parallel machines, and every operation in
a shop, needs a setup immediately before it is processed. The setup of job
$j$ takes $s_j$ time units, during which it occupies both the machines of
the job and the server. Hence

- the setup of a job starts no earlier than its release date $r_j$, so the
  job starts no earlier than $r_j + s_j$; in a shop this holds for the first
  operation of the job, the one that starts when the job starts;
- the setups of two different jobs do not overlap, since there is one
  server;
- of two jobs that share a machine, the later one starts no earlier than the
  completion of the earlier one plus its own setup time.

In a shop the setup of a later operation of a job may overlap the job's
previous operation on another machine: setups are separable, and only the
setup of the first operation waits for the release date. This is the model of
Brucker, Knust and Wang (2005) and of the papers of the same group on a single
server.

The field has the value "none", without server and setups, and three values
with a server: unit setup times, equal setup times, and arbitrary setup
times. Unit is a special case of equal and equal of arbitrary; the value
none is incomparable with the others.

**Theorem.** The server field is sound over every machine model on parallel
machines and for shops.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Servers
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

inductive Value
  | none
  | unit
  | equal
  | arbitrary
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Setup times of `n` items; no data without a server. -/
def Data (Item : Type) : Value → Type
  | .none => Unit
  | .unit | .equal | .arbitrary => Item → ℕ

/-- The setup times, where there is a server. -/
def view {Item : Type} : (v : Value) → Data Item v → Option (Item → ℕ)
  | .none, _ => Option.none
  | .unit, s | .equal, s | .arbitrary, s => some s

/-- The condition on the setup times. -/
def Admits {Item : Type} : (v : Value) → Data Item v → Prop
  | .unit, s => ∀ a, s a = 1
  | .equal, s => ∃ c, ∀ a, s a = c
  | _, _ => True

def le : Value → Value → Bool
  | .unit, .unit | .unit, .equal | .unit, .arbitrary => true
  | .equal, .equal | .equal, .arbitrary => true
  | .arbitrary, .arbitrary => true
  | .none, .none => true
  | _, _ => false

def embed {Item : Type} : {v w : Value} → le v w = true → Data Item v → Data Item w
  | .none, .none, _, _ => ()
  | .unit, .unit, _, s | .unit, .equal, _, s | .unit, .arbitrary, _, s
  | .equal, .equal, _, s | .equal, .arbitrary, _, s | .arbitrary, .arbitrary, _, s => s
  | .none, .unit, h, _ | .none, .equal, h, _ | .none, .arbitrary, h, _
  | .unit, .none, h, _ | .equal, .none, h, _ | .equal, .unit, h, _
  | .arbitrary, .none, h, _ | .arbitrary, .unit, h, _ | .arbitrary, .equal, h, _ =>
      absurd h Bool.false_ne_true

/-- The server constraints for items with given start and completion times,
release dates of their setups, setup times, and a relation "share a
machine". -/
def Served {Item : Type} (start completion release : Item → ℚ)
    (shares : Item → Item → Prop) (s : Item → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ a, release a + s a ≤ start a) ∧
  (∀ a b, a ≠ b → start a + s b ≤ start b ∨ start b + s a ≤ start a) ∧
  ∀ a b, a ≠ b → shares a b → completion a + s b ≤ start b ∨ completion b + s a ≤ start a

/-- The release date of the setup of an item: the release date of its job if
the item starts when its job starts (the first operation of the job), and `0`
otherwise. -/
def setupRelease {Item : Type} (start jobStart release : Item → ℚ) (a : Item) : ℚ :=
  if start a = jobStart a then release a else 0

/-- The server field of a machine model on parallel machines. -/
def parallel (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : Module M.kernel where
  Value := Value
  Data v x := Data (Fin (M.kernel.jobs x)) v
  admits v _ d := Admits v d
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ s, view v d = some s →
    Served (fun j => (M.kernel.start x σ j : ℚ)) (fun j => (M.kernel.completion x σ j : ℚ))
      (fun j => (M.kernel.release x j : ℚ)) (fun i j => ∃ S S', M.uses x σ (Fin.cast (M.jobs_eq x) i) S ∧
        M.uses x σ (Fin.cast (M.jobs_eq x) j) S' ∧ ¬ Disjoint S S') s
  le := le
  embed h _ d := embed h d

/-- The server field of shops: every operation needs a setup. -/
def shop : Module Shops.kernel where
  Value := Value
  Data v x := Data (Shops.Op x) v
  admits v _ d := Admits v d
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ s, view v d = some s →
    Served (fun o : Shops.Op x => (Shops.Sched.start σ o.1 o.2 : ℚ))
      (fun o => (Shops.finish x σ o : ℚ))
      (setupRelease (fun o : Shops.Op x => (Shops.Sched.start σ o.1 o.2 : ℚ))
        (fun o => (Shops.jobStart x σ o.1 : ℚ)) (fun o => (x.r o.1 : ℚ)))
      (fun a b => ¬ Disjoint (Shops.Sched.machines σ a.1 a.2) (Shops.Sched.machines σ b.1 b.2)) s
  le := le
  embed h _ d := embed h d

axiom parallel_sound (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : (parallel M).Sound

axiom shop_sound : shop.Sound

end Lax434175.Servers

concepts.title: No-idle shops and batch setup times
concepts.description:
Two further constraint fields of shops.

The no-idle field has the values "none" and "no-idle". With no-idle, no
machine is idle between two operations: every operation that occupies a
machine is immediately followed on that machine by another operation, unless
no operation on that machine completes later. The two values are
incomparable.

The batch-setup field has the values "none" and "batch setups". With batch
setups, every job belongs to a batch and a setup time $s_{pq}$ is given for
every ordered pair of batches. Two operations of jobs of different batches
that share a machine do not interleave, and if one follows the other on a
machine, with no operation on that machine in between, the later one may not
start before the completion of the earlier one plus the setup time from the
batch of the earlier to the batch of the later. The setup is charged only
between consecutive operations, as in the usual model of sequence-dependent
setups ("when the machine switches"); setup times need not satisfy the
triangle inequality. Without batch setups all jobs are read as one batch.

**Theorem.** Both fields are sound.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.Shops

/-!
---
title: No-idle shops and batch setup times
type: theorem
---
Two further constraint fields of shops.

The no-idle field has the values "none" and "no-idle". With no-idle, no
machine is idle between two operations: every operation that occupies a
machine is immediately followed on that machine by another operation, unless
no operation on that machine completes later. The two values are
incomparable.

The batch-setup field has the values "none" and "batch setups". With batch
setups, every job belongs to a batch and a setup time $s_{pq}$ is given for
every ordered pair of batches. Two operations of jobs of different batches
that share a machine do not interleave, and if one follows the other on a
machine, with no operation on that machine in between, the later one may not
start before the completion of the earlier one plus the setup time from the
batch of the earlier to the batch of the later. The setup is charged only
between consecutive operations, as in the usual model of sequence-dependent
setups ("when the machine switches"); setup times need not satisfy the
triangle inequality. Without batch setups all jobs are read as one batch.

**Theorem.** Both fields are sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ShopExtras
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Shops

inductive NoIdle
  | none
  | noIdle
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- An operation occupies a machine. -/
def Occupies {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) (i : Fin x.machines) : Prop :=
  i ∈ σ.machines o.1 o.2

/-- Every operation on a machine is immediately followed by another one on
that machine, unless none completes later. -/
def Contiguous (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ i (a : Op x), Occupies σ a i →
    (∃ b : Op x, b ≠ a ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧ σ.start b.1 b.2 = finish x σ a) ∨
    ∀ b : Op x, Occupies σ b i → finish x σ b ≤ finish x σ a

/-- The no-idle field. -/
def noIdle : Module kernel where
  Value := NoIdle
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v = .noIdle → Contiguous x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

inductive BatchSetups
  | none
  | batchSetups

/-- The data of a value: the batch of every job and the setup times between
batches. -/
def BatchSetups.Data : BatchSetups → Inst → Type
  | .none, _ => Unit
  | .batchSetups, x => (Fin x.jobs → ℕ) × (ℕ → ℕ → ℕ)

/-- The batch of a job; a single batch when the field is absent. -/
def BatchSetups.batch {x : Inst} : (v : BatchSetups) → v.Data x → Fin x.jobs → ℕ
  | .none, _ => fun _ => 0
  | .batchSetups, d => d.1

/-- The setup time between two batches. -/
def BatchSetups.setup {x : Inst} : (v : BatchSetups) → v.Data x → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
  | .none, _ => fun _ _ => 0
  | .batchSetups, d => d.2

def BatchSetups.le : BatchSetups → BatchSetups → Bool
  | .batchSetups, .none => false
  | _, _ => true

def BatchSetups.embed : {v w : BatchSetups} → BatchSetups.le v w = true → (x : Inst) →
    v.Data x → w.Data x
  | _, .none, _, _, _ => ()
  | v, .batchSetups, _, _, d => (v.batch d, v.setup d)

/-- On some machine, operation `b` follows operation `a`: `b` starts after `a`
completes, and no other operation on that machine lies in between. -/
def Follows {x : Inst} (σ : Sched x) (a b : Op x) : Prop :=
  finish x σ a ≤ σ.start b.1 b.2 ∧ ∃ i, Occupies σ a i ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧
    ∀ c : Op x, c ≠ a → c ≠ b → Occupies σ c i →
      ¬ (finish x σ a ≤ σ.start c.1 c.2 ∧ finish x σ c ≤ σ.start b.1 b.2)

/-- The batch-setup field. -/
def batchSetups : Module kernel where
  Value := BatchSetups
  Data := BatchSetups.Data
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ a b : Op x, v.batch d a.1 ≠ v.batch d b.1 →
    (¬ Disjoint (σ.machines a.1 a.2) (σ.machines b.1 b.2) →
      finish x σ a ≤ σ.start b.1 b.2 ∨ finish x σ b ≤ σ.start a.1 a.2) ∧
    (Follows σ a b → finish x σ a + v.setup d (v.batch d a.1) (v.batch d b.1) ≤ σ.start b.1 b.2)
  le := BatchSetups.le
  embed := BatchSetups.embed

axiom noIdle_sound : noIdle.Sound

axiom batchSetups_sound : batchSetups.Sound

end Lax434175.ShopExtras

noIdle_sound : Lax434175.ShopExtras.noIdle.Sound

concepts.title: One family for shops with and without preemption
concepts.description:
Non-preemptive and preemptive shops share one machine model, in which a
schedule is a finite list of pieces of operations as in preemptive shops. A
schedule is feasible for this model if every piece occupies some machine and
two different pieces that belong to the same job or share a machine are
disjoint in time. An operation starts when its first piece starts and
completes when its last piece ends; a job starts when its first piece starts
and completes when its last piece ends.

The interruption field has the values of parallel machines, read per
operation:

- none: every operation has exactly one piece, it starts at an integral time,
  and its length is the processing time of the operation;
- restarts: some piece of the operation has the full processing time as its
  length, no piece of the operation ends later, and every such piece ends at
  the same time;
- preemption: the lengths of the pieces of every operation sum to its
  processing time, or the processing time is $0$ and the operation has a
  piece;
- preemption without migration: preemption, and all pieces of every
  operation occupy the same set of machines.

The other fields are those of shops, read through the start and completion
of operations: the shop type orders the operations of a job; the machine
field restricts the machines of every piece; with no-wait a job completes at
its start plus the sum of its processing times; of two operations of a job,
the later one waits for the transportation delay, unless both delays between
them are $0$; with a robot, one robot carries every job from an operation to
the next and travels empty between the machines that the pieces of the
operations occupy; the server, no-idle and batch-setup fields read "two
operations share a machine" as "a piece of the one and a piece of the other
share a machine". The remaining fields are the generic ones.

A problem of non-preemptive shops determines the problem of this family with
the same values and no interruption, and a problem of preemptive shops the
problem with the same values, preemption, and the value none in the fields
that preemptive shops do not have.

**Theorem.** The two problems are special cases of each other. The fields of
the family are sound, so that a specification that is field by field a
special case of another describes a special case of the other's problem,
and one that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version
reduces to that of the other.

import Lax434175.ShopProblems
import Lax434175.PreemptiveShopProblems
import Lax434175.Interruption

/-!
---
title: One family for shops with and without preemption
type: theorem
---
Non-preemptive and preemptive shops share one machine model, in which a
schedule is a finite list of pieces of operations as in preemptive shops. A
schedule is feasible for this model if every piece occupies some machine and
two different pieces that belong to the same job or share a machine are
disjoint in time. An operation starts when its first piece starts and
completes when its last piece ends; a job starts when its first piece starts
and completes when its last piece ends.

The interruption field has the values of parallel machines, read per
operation:

- none: every operation has exactly one piece, it starts at an integral time,
  and its length is the processing time of the operation;
- restarts: some piece of the operation has the full processing time as its
  length, no piece of the operation ends later, and every such piece ends at
  the same time;
- preemption: the lengths of the pieces of every operation sum to its
  processing time, or the processing time is $0$ and the operation has a
  piece;
- preemption without migration: preemption, and all pieces of every
  operation occupy the same set of machines.

The other fields are those of shops, read through the start and completion
of operations: the shop type orders the operations of a job; the machine
field restricts the machines of every piece; with no-wait a job completes at
its start plus the sum of its processing times; of two operations of a job,
the later one waits for the transportation delay, unless both delays between
them are $0$; with a robot, one robot carries every job from an operation to
the next and travels empty between the machines that the pieces of the
operations occupy; the server, no-idle and batch-setup fields read "two
operations share a machine" as "a piece of the one and a piece of the other
share a machine". The remaining fields are the generic ones.

A problem of non-preemptive shops determines the problem of this family with
the same values and no interruption, and a problem of preemptive shops the
problem with the same values, preemption, and the value none in the fields
that preemptive shops do not have.

**Theorem.** The two problems are special cases of each other. The fields of
the family are sound, so that a specification that is field by field a
special case of another describes a special case of the other's problem,
and one that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version
reduces to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ShopFamily
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Shops
open Lax434175.PreemptiveShops (Piece piecesOf piecesOfJob Apart opStart opFinish)

/-- Every piece occupies some machine, and two different pieces that belong to
the same job or share a machine do not overlap. -/
def feasible {x : Inst} (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, q.machines.Nonempty) ∧
  σ.pieces.Pairwise
    (fun a b => (a.op.1 = b.op.1 ∨ ¬ Disjoint a.machines b.machines) → Apart a b)

/-- The kernel of shops with pieces. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := PreemptiveShops.Sched
  feasible _ σ := feasible σ
  start _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.start).min?).getD 0
  completion _ σ j := (((piecesOfJob σ j).map Piece.finish).max?).getD 0

/-- The schedules that respect a way of interruption. -/
def holds : Interruption.Mode → (x : Inst) → PreemptiveShops.Sched x → Prop
  | .none, x, σ => ∀ o : Op x, ∃ q, piecesOf σ o = [q] ∧
      q.length = (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat) ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, q.start = (n : NNRat)
  | .restarts, x, σ => ∀ o : Op x, ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, q.length = (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat) ∧
      ∀ q' ∈ piecesOf σ o, q'.finish ≤ q.finish ∧
        (q'.length = (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat) → q'.finish = q.finish)
  | .pmtn, x, σ => ∀ o : Op x,
      ((piecesOf σ o).map fun q => q.length / (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat)).sum = 1 ∨
        ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, x.p o.1 o.2 = 0
  | .pmtnNoMigration, x, σ => ∀ o : Op x,
      (((piecesOf σ o).map fun q => q.length / (x.p o.1 o.2 : NNRat)).sum = 1 ∨
        ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, x.p o.1 o.2 = 0) ∧
        ∀ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, ∀ q' ∈ piecesOf σ o, q.machines = q'.machines

/-- The interruption field. -/
def interruption : Module kernel where
  Value := Interruption.Mode
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := holds v x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- The shop-type field. -/
def shopType : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopType
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits v x _ := v.holds x
  constraint v x _ σ := PreemptiveShops.ordered v x σ
  le := ShopType.le
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- The machine field. -/
def machineSets : Module kernel where
  Value := Machines
  Data := Machines.Data
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v _ d σ := ∀ q ∈ σ.pieces, v.view d q.op.1 q.op.2 q.machines
  le := Machines.le
  embed := Machines.embed

/-- The processing-time field. -/
def processingTimes : Module kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ProcessingTimes ProcessingTimes.holds
    (fun v w => decide (v.rank ≤ w.rank))

/-- The no-wait field. -/
def noWait : Module kernel where
  Value := NoWait
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v = .noWait →
    ∀ j, kernel.completion x σ j = kernel.start x σ j + ∑ k, (x.p j k : NNRat)
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- Of two operations of a job, the later one waits for the delay, unless both
delays between them are `0`. -/
def Delayed (x : Inst) (t : Transportation.Delays x) (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), k ≠ l → (t j k l = 0 ∧ t j l k = 0) ∨
    opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ + (t j k l : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, l⟩ ∨
    opFinish σ ⟨j, l⟩ + (t j l k : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, k⟩

/-- The machines that the pieces of an operation occupy. -/
def opMachines {x : Inst} (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) (o : Op x) : Finset (Fin x.machines) :=
  ((piecesOf σ o).map Piece.machines).foldr (· ∪ ·) ∅

/-- A single robot carries every job from each operation to the next, and
between two transports it travels empty from the machines where it delivers
the one to the machines where it picks up the other. -/
def Carried (x : Inst) (t : Transportation.Delays x) (e : Transportation.EmptyMoves x)
    (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∃ depart : (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ,
    (∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      opFinish σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ (depart j k : NNRat) ∧
        ((depart j k + t j k l : ℕ) : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ ⟨j, l⟩) ∧
    ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)) j' (k' l' : Fin (x.ops j')), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      l'.val = k'.val + 1 → (⟨j, k⟩ : Op x) ≠ ⟨j', k'⟩ →
      depart j k + t j k l +
          Transportation.emptyTime e (opMachines σ ⟨j, l⟩) (opMachines σ ⟨j', k'⟩) ≤
        depart j' k' ∨
      depart j' k' + t j' k' l' +
          Transportation.emptyTime e (opMachines σ ⟨j', l'⟩) (opMachines σ ⟨j, k⟩) ≤
        depart j k

/-- The field of transportation delays. -/
def transportation : Module kernel where
  Value := Transportation.Value
  Data _ x := Transportation.Data x
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v x d σ := Delayed x d.1 σ ∧ (v.robot = true → Carried x d.1 d.2 σ)
  le := Transportation.Value.le
  embed _ _ d := d

/-- A piece of one operation and a piece of another share a machine. -/
def Shares {x : Inst} (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) (a b : Op x) : Prop :=
  ∃ qa ∈ piecesOf σ a, ∃ qb ∈ piecesOf σ b, ¬ Disjoint qa.machines qb.machines

/-- The server field: every operation needs a setup. -/
def server : Module kernel where
  Value := Servers.Value
  Data v x := Servers.Data (Op x) v
  admits v _ d := Servers.Admits v d
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ s, Servers.view v d = some s →
    Servers.Served (fun o : Op x => (opStart σ o : ℚ)) (fun o => (opFinish σ o : ℚ))
      (Servers.setupRelease (fun o : Op x => (opStart σ o : ℚ))
        (fun o => (kernel.start x σ o.1 : ℚ)) (fun o => (x.r o.1 : ℚ)))
      (Shares σ) s
  le := Servers.le
  embed h _ d := Servers.embed h d

/-- A piece of an operation occupies a machine. -/
def Occupies {x : Inst} (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) (o : Op x) (i : Fin x.machines) : Prop :=
  ∃ q ∈ piecesOf σ o, i ∈ q.machines

/-- Every operation on a machine is immediately followed by another one on
that machine, unless none completes later. -/
def Contiguous (x : Inst) (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ i (a : Op x), Occupies σ a i →
    (∃ b : Op x, b ≠ a ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧ opStart σ b = opFinish σ a) ∨
    ∀ b : Op x, Occupies σ b i → opFinish σ b ≤ opFinish σ a

/-- The no-idle field. -/
def noIdle : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopExtras.NoIdle
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v = .noIdle → Contiguous x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

/-- On some machine, operation `b` follows operation `a`: `b` starts after `a`
completes, and no other operation on that machine lies in between. -/
def Follows {x : Inst} (σ : PreemptiveShops.Sched x) (a b : Op x) : Prop :=
  opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ b ∧ ∃ i, Occupies σ a i ∧ Occupies σ b i ∧
    ∀ c : Op x, c ≠ a → c ≠ b → Occupies σ c i →
      ¬ (opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ c ∧ opFinish σ c ≤ opStart σ b)

/-- The batch-setup field. -/
def batchSetups : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopExtras.BatchSetups
  Data := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.Data
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x d σ := ∀ a b : Op x, v.batch d a.1 ≠ v.batch d b.1 →
    (Shares σ a b → opFinish σ a ≤ opStart σ b ∨ opFinish σ b ≤ opStart σ a) ∧
    (Follows σ a b →
      opFinish σ a + (v.setup d (v.batch d a.1) (v.batch d b.1) : NNRat) ≤ opStart σ b)
  le := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.le
  embed := ShopExtras.BatchSetups.embed

/-- The number of machines, a parameter of the kernel. -/
def machines : kernel.Inst → ℕ := Inst.machines

/-- The fields of the family: interruption and the fields of shops. -/
inductive FieldName
  | interruption
  | field (i : ShopProblems.FieldName)
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.interruption, .field .shopType, .field .machineSets, .field .machineCount,
    .field .jobCount, .field .processingTimes, .field .noWait, .field .transportation,
    .field .server, .field .noIdle, .field .batchSetups, .field .releaseDates,
    .field .deadlines, .field .precedence}
  complete x := by
    cases x with
    | interruption => decide
    | field i => cases i <;> decide

/-- The shop problems. -/
abbrev family : Family kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .interruption => interruption
    | .field .shopType => shopType
    | .field .machineSets => machineSets
    | .field .machineCount => Counts.module _ machines 1
    | .field .jobCount => Counts.module _ kernel.jobs
    | .field .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .field .noWait => noWait
    | .field .transportation => transportation
    | .field .server => server
    | .field .noIdle => noIdle
    | .field .batchSetups => batchSetups
    | .field .releaseDates => ReleaseDates.module _
    | .field .deadlines => Deadlines.module _
    | .field .precedence => Precedence.module _ machines

instance : Fintype family.ModuleName :=
  inferInstanceAs (Fintype FieldName)

/-- The specification `α | β | γ` of a shop problem. -/
def spec (interruption : Interruption.Mode := .none)
    (shopType : ShopType)
    (machineSets : Machines)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (processingTimes : ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (waiting : NoWait := .none)
    (transportation : Transportation.Value := .none)
    (server : Servers.Value := .none)
    (idling : ShopExtras.NoIdle := .none)
    (setups : ShopExtras.BatchSetups := .none)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => interruption
    | .field .shopType => shopType
    | .field .machineSets => machineSets
    | .field .machineCount => machineCount
    | .field .jobCount => jobCount
    | .field .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .field .noWait => waiting
    | .field .transportation => transportation
    | .field .server => server
    | .field .noIdle => idling
    | .field .batchSetups => setups
    | .field .releaseDates => release
    | .field .deadlines => deadline
    | .field .precedence => precedence
  objective := objective

/-- The specification of the family with the values of a non-preemptive shop
problem. -/
def ofShop (s : Spec ShopProblems.family) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => Interruption.Mode.none
    | .field .shopType => s.module .shopType
    | .field .machineSets => s.module .machineSets
    | .field .machineCount => s.module .machineCount
    | .field .jobCount => s.module .jobCount
    | .field .processingTimes => s.module .processingTimes
    | .field .noWait => s.module .noWait
    | .field .transportation => s.module .transportation
    | .field .server => s.module .server
    | .field .noIdle => s.module .noIdle
    | .field .batchSetups => s.module .batchSetups
    | .field .releaseDates => s.module .releaseDates
    | .field .deadlines => s.module .deadlines
    | .field .precedence => s.module .precedence
  objective := s.objective

/-- The specification of the family with the values of a preemptive shop
problem. -/
def ofPreemptiveShop (s : Spec PreemptiveShopProblems.family) : Spec family where
  module
    | .interruption => Interruption.Mode.pmtn
    | .field .shopType => s.module .shopType
    | .field .machineSets => s.module .machineSets
    | .field .machineCount => s.module .machineCount
    | .field .jobCount => s.module .jobCount
    | .field .processingTimes => s.module .processingTimes
    | .field .noWait => NoWait.none
    | .field .transportation => Transportation.Value.none
    | .field .server => Servers.Value.none
    | .field .noIdle => ShopExtras.NoIdle.none
    | .field .batchSetups => ShopExtras.BatchSetups.none
    | .field .releaseDates => s.module .releaseDates
    | .field .deadlines => s.module .deadlines
    | .field .precedence => s.module .precedence
  objective := s.objective

axiom shop_faithful (s : Spec ShopProblems.family) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofShop s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofShop s)) (problem _ s)

axiom preemptiveShop_faithful (s : Spec PreemptiveShopProblems.family) :
    SpecialCase (problem _ s) (problem family (ofPreemptiveShop s)) ∧
      SpecialCase (problem family (ofPreemptiveShop s)) (problem _ s)

axiom family_sound : family.Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le {s t : Spec family} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.ShopFamily

concepts.title: Shop problems in three-field notation
concepts.description:
The family of shop problems has the constraint fields shop type, machines of
the operations, number of machines, number of jobs, processing times, no-wait, no-idle, transportation
delays, a server, batch setups, release dates, deadlines and precedence constraints between jobs, and the completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ with $\alpha$ one of $O$, $F$, $J$,
possibly followed by a number of machines, is one specification of this
family. Without an entry on machine sets, the operations of an open shop or
flow shop occupy the machines by position and those of a job shop occupy
dedicated machines. For example $F2 \mid\mid C_{\max}$ and
$J \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ are the specifications below.
The concept on one family for shops joins these problems and the preemptive
shop problems into a single family with an interruption field.

**Theorem.** A specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version reduces
to that of the other. In particular
$F2 \mid\mid C_{\max}$ is a special case of $J \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$.

import Lax434175.Assembly
import Lax434175.Counts
import Lax434175.ReleaseDates
import Lax434175.Deadlines
import Lax434175.Precedence
import Lax434175.Thresholds
import Lax434175.Shops
import Lax434175.Transportation
import Lax434175.Servers
import Lax434175.ShopExtras

/-!
---
title: Shop problems in three-field notation
type: theorem
---
The family of shop problems has the constraint fields shop type, machines of
the operations, number of machines, number of jobs, processing times, no-wait, no-idle, transportation
delays, a server, batch setups, release dates, deadlines and precedence constraints between jobs, and the completion-time objectives.

A problem $\alpha \mid \beta \mid \gamma$ with $\alpha$ one of $O$, $F$, $J$,
possibly followed by a number of machines, is one specification of this
family. Without an entry on machine sets, the operations of an open shop or
flow shop occupy the machines by position and those of a job shop occupy
dedicated machines. For example $F2 \mid\mid C_{\max}$ and
$J \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$ are the specifications below.
The concept on one family for shops joins these problems and the preemptive
shop problems into a single family with an interruption field.

**Theorem.** A specification that is field by field a special case of
another describes a special case of the other's problem, and a specification
that reduces to another describes a problem whose decision version reduces
to that of the other. In particular
$F2 \mid\mid C_{\max}$ is a special case of $J \mid r_j \mid L_{\max}$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ShopProblems
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175

/-- The constraint fields of the family. -/
inductive FieldName
  | shopType
  | machineSets
  | machineCount
  | jobCount
  | processingTimes
  | noWait
  | transportation
  | server
  | noIdle
  | batchSetups
  | releaseDates
  | deadlines
  | precedence
  deriving DecidableEq

instance : Fintype FieldName where
  elems := {.shopType, .machineSets, .machineCount, .jobCount, .processingTimes, .noWait, .transportation, .server, .noIdle, .batchSetups, .releaseDates,
    .deadlines, .precedence}
  complete x := by cases x <;> decide

/-- The shop problems. -/
abbrev family : Family Shops.kernel :=
  Thresholds.family FieldName fun
    | .shopType => Shops.shopType
    | .machineSets => Shops.machineSets
    | .machineCount => Counts.module _ Shops.machines 1
    | .jobCount => Counts.module _ Shops.kernel.jobs
    | .processingTimes => Shops.processingTimes
    | .noWait => Shops.noWait
    | .transportation => Transportation.module
    | .server => Servers.shop
    | .noIdle => ShopExtras.noIdle
    | .batchSetups => ShopExtras.batchSetups
    | .releaseDates => ReleaseDates.module _
    | .deadlines => Deadlines.module _
    | .precedence => Precedence.module _ Shops.machines

instance : Fintype family.ModuleName := inferInstanceAs (Fintype FieldName)

/-- The specification `α | β | γ` of a shop problem. -/
def spec (shopType : Shops.ShopType)
    (machineSets : Shops.Machines)
    (machineCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (jobCount : Counts.Bound := .any)
    (processingTimes : Shops.ProcessingTimes := .arbitrary)
    (waiting : Shops.NoWait := .none)
    (transportation : Transportation.Value := .none)
    (server : Servers.Value := .none)
    (idling : ShopExtras.NoIdle := .none)
    (setups : ShopExtras.BatchSetups := .none)
    (release : ReleaseDates.Value := .none)
    (deadline : Deadlines.Value := .none)
    (precedence : Precedence.Value := .none)
    (objective : Objectives.Value) : Spec family where
  module
    | .shopType => shopType
    | .machineSets => machineSets
    | .machineCount => machineCount
    | .jobCount => jobCount
    | .processingTimes => processingTimes
    | .noWait => waiting
    | .transportation => transportation
    | .server => server
    | .noIdle => idling
    | .batchSetups => setups
    | .releaseDates => release
    | .deadlines => deadline
    | .precedence => precedence
  objective := objective

/-- `F2 || C_max` -/
def flow2_makespan : Spec family :=
  spec (shopType := .flow) (machineSets := .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `J | r_j | L_max` -/
def job_release_lmax : Spec family :=
  spec (shopType := .job) (machineSets := .dedicated) (release := .releaseDates) (objective := .lmax)

axiom family_sound : family.Sound

axiom specialCase_of_le {s t : Spec family} :
    s.le t → SpecialCase (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom reducible_of_reduces {s t : Spec family} :
    Thresholds.Reduces s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

axiom flow2_makespan_specialCase :
    SpecialCase (problem family flow2_makespan) (problem family job_release_lmax)

end Lax434175.ShopProblems

  (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family Lax434175.ShopProblems.flow2_makespan)
  (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family Lax434175.ShopProblems.job_release_lmax)

    Lax434175.Problems.Reducible (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family t)
