  s.le t →
    Lax434175.Problems.SpecialCase (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family s)
      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.ShopProblems.family t)

concepts.title: Shop scheduling
concepts.description:
An instance of a shop has $n$ jobs and $m$ machines. Every job consists of a
sequence of operations, each with a processing time. A schedule assigns to
every operation a nonempty set of machines and an integral start time; the
operation occupies these machines without interruption for its processing
time. A schedule is feasible for the kernel if two different operations of
the same job, or sharing a machine, do not overlap. A job starts when its
first operation starts and completes when its last operation completes.

The shop-type field has the values

- open shop: every job has exactly $m$ operations, which may be processed in
  any order;
- flow shop: every job has exactly $m$ operations, which must be processed
  in their given order;
- job shop: the operations of a job must be processed in their given order;
- two-stage flexible flow shop: every job has exactly two operations, which
  must be processed in their given order.

A flow shop and a two-stage flexible flow shop are special cases of a job
shop.

The machine field determines which sets of machines an operation may
occupy. Its values are

- by position: the $k$-th operation of every job occupies machine $k$, as in
  the classical open shop and flow shop;
- dedicated: every operation occupies a given machine, and no two operations
  of a job are given the same machine, as in the classical job shop;
- recirculation: every operation occupies a given machine;
- stages: the first operation of every job occupies the first machine, and
  every later operation occupies any one of the other machines, as in the
  two-stage flexible flow shop;
- machine sets: every operation occupies one machine of a given set;
- fixed sets: every operation occupies all machines of a given set
  simultaneously;
- general: the admissible sets of machines of every operation are given
  explicitly.

Each of the first three values is a special case of the next and of all
later ones: an operation with a given machine has a machine set, and a fixed
set, consisting of that machine alone. Machine sets and fixed sets are
special cases of the general value and incomparable with each other. Stages
are a special case of machine sets.

The processing-time field restricts the instances to unit operations,
$p_{ij} = 1$, or to equal operations, $p_{ij} = p$.

The no-wait field has the values "none" and "no-wait". With no-wait, every
job is processed without interruption between its first start and its
completion: the time between them is the sum of its processing times. Its
two values are incomparable.

**Theorem.** The shop-type, machine, processing-time and no-wait fields are
sound.

import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
import Mathlib.Data.NNRat.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic
import Lax434175.Modules

/-!
---
title: Shop scheduling
type: theorem
---
An instance of a shop has $n$ jobs and $m$ machines. Every job consists of a

time. A schedule is feasible for the kernel if two different operations of
the same job, or sharing a machine, do not overlap. A job starts when its
first operation starts and completes when its last operation completes.

The shop-type field has the values

- open shop: every job has exactly $m$ operations, which may be processed in
  any order;
- flow shop: every job has exactly $m$ operations, which must be processed
  in their given order;
- job shop: the operations of a job must be processed in their given order;
- two-stage flexible flow shop: every job has exactly two operations, which
  must be processed in their given order.

A flow shop and a two-stage flexible flow shop are special cases of a job
shop.

The machine field determines which sets of machines an operation may
occupy. Its values are

- by position: the $k$-th operation of every job occupies machine $k$, as in

- dedicated: every operation occupies a given machine, and no two operations
  of a job are given the same machine, as in the classical job shop;
- recirculation: every operation occupies a given machine;
- stages: the first operation of every job occupies the first machine, and
  every later operation occupies any one of the other machines, as in the
  two-stage flexible flow shop;
- machine sets: every operation occupies one machine of a given set;
- fixed sets: every operation occupies all machines of a given set
  simultaneously;
- general: the admissible sets of machines of every operation are given
  explicitly.

Each of the first three values is a special case of the next and of all
later ones: an operation with a given machine has a machine set, and a fixed
set, consisting of that machine alone. Machine sets and fixed sets are
special cases of the general value and incomparable with each other. Stages
are a special case of machine sets.

The processing-time field restricts the instances to unit operations,
$p_{ij} = 1$, or to equal operations, $p_{ij} = p$.

The no-wait field has the values "none" and "no-wait". With no-wait, every
job is processed without interruption between its first start and its

**Theorem.** The shop-type, machine, processing-time and no-wait fields are
sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Shops
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

structure Inst where
  jobs : ℕ
  machines : ℕ
  /-- The number of operations of a job. -/
  ops : Fin jobs → ℕ
  /-- The processing time of an operation. -/
  p : (j : Fin jobs) → Fin (ops j) → ℕ
  /-- The release date of a job. -/
  r : Fin jobs → ℕ

/-- An operation: a job and a position in its sequence. -/
abbrev Op (x : Inst) := (j : Fin x.jobs) × Fin (x.ops j)

structure Sched (x : Inst) where
  machines : (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Finset (Fin x.machines)
  start : (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ

/-- The time at which an operation completes. -/
def finish (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (o : Op x) : ℕ :=
  σ.start o.1 o.2 + x.p o.1 o.2

/-- Every operation occupies some machine, and two different operations of
the same job or sharing a machine do not overlap. -/
def feasible (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  (∀ o : Op x, (σ.machines o.1 o.2).Nonempty) ∧
  ∀ a b : Op x, a ≠ b →
    (a.1 = b.1 ∨ ¬ Disjoint (σ.machines a.1 a.2) (σ.machines b.1 b.2)) →
    finish x σ a ≤ σ.start b.1 b.2 ∨ finish x σ b ≤ σ.start a.1 a.2

/-- The start of the first operation of a job. -/
def jobStart (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : ℕ :=
  ((List.ofFn (σ.start j)).min?).getD 0

/-- The completion of the last operation of a job. -/
def jobCompletion (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) (j : Fin x.jobs) : ℕ :=
  ((List.ofFn (fun k => finish x σ ⟨j, k⟩)).max?).getD 0

/-- The kernel of non-preemptive shop scheduling. -/
def kernel : Kernel where
  Inst := Inst
  jobs := Inst.jobs
  release := Inst.r
  Sched := Sched
  feasible := feasible
  start x σ j := (jobStart x σ j : NNRat)
  completion x σ j := (jobCompletion x σ j : NNRat)

/-- The number of machines, a parameter of the kernel. -/
def machines : kernel.Inst → ℕ := Inst.machines

/-- Every job has exactly one operation per machine. -/
def OnePerMachine (x : Inst) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, x.ops j = x.machines

/-- The operations of every job are processed in their given order. -/
def InOrder (x : Inst) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k k' : Fin (x.ops j)), k < k' → finish x σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ σ.start j k'

inductive ShopType
  | open
  | flow
  | job
  | flexibleFlow
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The instances of a shop type. -/
def ShopType.holds : ShopType → Inst → Prop
  | .open, x => OnePerMachine x
  | .flow, x => OnePerMachine x
  | .job, _ => True
  | .flexibleFlow, x => ∀ j, x.ops j = 2

/-- The order a shop type imposes on the operations of a job. -/
def ShopType.ordered : ShopType → (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  | .open, _, _ => True
  | .flow, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .job, x, σ => InOrder x σ
  | .flexibleFlow, x, σ => InOrder x σ

def ShopType.le : ShopType → ShopType → Bool
  | .flow, .job | .flexibleFlow, .job => true
  | v, w => decide (v = w)

/-- The shop-type field. -/
def shopType : Module kernel where
  Value := ShopType
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits v x _ := v.holds x
  constraint v x _ σ := v.ordered x σ
  le := ShopType.le
  embed _ _ _ := ()

inductive Machines
  | byPosition
  | dedicated
  | recirculation
  | stages
  | sets
  | fix
  | general

/-- The data of a value of the machine field. -/
def Machines.Data : Machines → Inst → Type
  | .byPosition, _ | .stages, _ => Unit
  | .dedicated, x | .recirculation, x => (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ
  | .sets, x => (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Fin x.machines → Prop
  | .fix, x => (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Finset (Fin x.machines)
  | .general, x => (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Finset (Fin x.machines) → Prop

/-- The set consisting of the machine with a given number. Machines are
numbered from `0`. -/
def machineNumbered (x : Inst) (i : ℕ) : Finset (Fin x.machines) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun i' => i'.val = i)

/-- Whether an operation may occupy a set of machines. -/
def Machines.view {x : Inst} : (v : Machines) → v.Data x →
    (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Finset (Fin x.machines) → Prop
  | .byPosition, _ => fun _ k S => S = machineNumbered x k.val
  | .dedicated, μ | .recirculation, μ => fun j k S => S = machineNumbered x (μ j k)
  | .stages, _ => fun _ k S =>
      (k.val = 0 → S = machineNumbered x 0) ∧ (k.val ≠ 0 → S.card = 1 ∧ ∀ i ∈ S, i.val ≠ 0)
  | .sets, M => fun j k S => S.card = 1 ∧ ∀ i ∈ S, M j k i
  | .fix, F => fun j k S => S = F j k
  | .general, allowed => allowed

/-- The condition on the data: a given machine number is the number of a
machine, and with dedicated machines no two operations of a job are given
the same machine. -/
def Machines.admits {x : Inst} : (v : Machines) → v.Data x → Prop
  | .byPosition, _ => ∀ j (k : Fin (x.ops j)), k.val < x.machines
  | .dedicated, μ => (∀ j k, μ j k < x.machines) ∧ ∀ j k k', μ j k = μ j k' → k = k'
  | .recirculation, μ => ∀ j k, μ j k < x.machines
  | .stages, _ => 0 < x.machines
  | _, _ => True

def Machines.le : Machines → Machines → Bool
  | .byPosition, .stages | .dedicated, .stages | .recirculation, .stages => false
  | .byPosition, _ => true
  | .dedicated, .byPosition => false
  | .dedicated, _ => true
  | .recirculation, .byPosition | .recirculation, .dedicated => false
  | .recirculation, _ => true
  | .stages, .stages | .stages, .sets | .stages, .general => true
  | .sets, .sets | .sets, .general => true
  | .fix, .fix | .fix, .general => true
  | .general, .general => true
  | _, _ => false

def Machines.embed : {v w : Machines} → Machines.le v w = true → (x : Inst) →
    v.Data x → w.Data x
  | .byPosition, .byPosition, _, _, _ => ()
  | .byPosition, .dedicated, _, _, _ | .byPosition, .recirculation, _, _, _ =>
      fun _ k => k.val
  | .byPosition, .sets, _, _, _ => fun _ k i => i.val = k.val
  | .byPosition, .fix, _, x, _ => fun _ k => machineNumbered x k.val
  | .dedicated, .dedicated, _, _, μ | .dedicated, .recirculation, _, _, μ
  | .recirculation, .recirculation, _, _, μ => μ
  | .dedicated, .sets, _, _, μ | .recirculation, .sets, _, _, μ => fun j k i => i.val = μ j k
  | .dedicated, .fix, _, x, μ | .recirculation, .fix, _, x, μ =>
      fun j k => machineNumbered x (μ j k)
  | .stages, .stages, _, _, _ => ()
  | .stages, .sets, _, _, _ => fun _ k i => (k.val = 0 ∧ i.val = 0) ∨ (k.val ≠ 0 ∧ i.val ≠ 0)
  | .sets, .sets, _, _, d => d
  | .fix, .fix, _, _, d => d
  | v, .general, _, _, d => v.view d
  | .byPosition, .stages, h, _, _ | .dedicated, .stages, h, _, _
  | .recirculation, .stages, h, _, _ | .sets, .stages, h, _, _ | .fix, .stages, h, _, _
  | .general, .stages, h, _, _ | .stages, .byPosition, h, _, _ | .stages, .dedicated, h, _, _
  | .stages, .recirculation, h, _, _ | .stages, .fix, h, _, _
  | .dedicated, .byPosition, h, _, _
  | .recirculation, .byPosition, h, _, _ | .recirculation, .dedicated, h, _, _
  | .sets, .byPosition, h, _, _ | .sets, .dedicated, h, _, _
  | .sets, .recirculation, h, _, _ | .sets, .fix, h, _, _ | .fix, .byPosition, h, _, _
  | .fix, .dedicated, h, _, _ | .fix, .recirculation, h, _, _ | .fix, .sets, h, _, _
  | .general, .byPosition, h, _, _ | .general, .dedicated, h, _, _
  | .general, .recirculation, h, _, _ | .general, .sets, h, _, _ | .general, .fix, h, _, _ =>
      absurd h Bool.false_ne_true

/-- The machine field. -/
def machineSets : Module kernel where
  Value := Machines
  Data := Machines.Data
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v _ d σ := ∀ j k, v.view d j k (Sched.machines σ j k)
  le := Machines.le
  embed := Machines.embed

inductive ProcessingTimes
  | unit
  | equal
  | arbitrary

/-- The instances of a processing-time restriction. -/
def ProcessingTimes.holds : ProcessingTimes → Inst → Prop
  | .unit, x => ∀ j k, x.p j k = 1
  | .equal, x => ∃ p, ∀ j k, x.p j k = p
  | .arbitrary, _ => True

/-- The position of a value in the chain unit, equal, arbitrary. -/
def ProcessingTimes.rank : ProcessingTimes → ℕ
  | .unit => 0
  | .equal => 1
  | .arbitrary => 2

/-- The processing-time field. -/
def processingTimes : Module kernel :=
  Module.ofRestriction ProcessingTimes ProcessingTimes.holds
    (fun v w => decide (v.rank ≤ w.rank))

inductive NoWait
  | none
  | noWait
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Every job is processed without interruption. -/
def NoWait.constraint : NoWait → (x : Inst) → Sched x → Prop
  | .none, _, _ => True
  | .noWait, x, σ => ∀ j, jobCompletion x σ j = jobStart x σ j + ∑ k, x.p j k

/-- The no-wait field. -/
def noWait : Module kernel where
  Value := NoWait
  Data _ _ := Unit
  admits _ _ _ := True
  constraint v x _ σ := v.constraint x σ
  le v w := decide (v = w)
  embed _ _ _ := ()

axiom shopType_sound : shopType.Sound

axiom machineSets_sound : machineSets.Sound

axiom processingTimes_sound : processingTimes.Sound

axiom noWait_sound : noWait.Sound

end Lax434175.Shops

concepts.title: The standard reading of scheduling instances and schedules
concepts.description:
The words in which the literature writes scheduling instances, schedules and
online information, for the operations family, the batching family and the two
standalone problems. All numbers are written in binary, as entries of the word.

**Blocks.** A finite set of tuples of numbers is written canonically: the
number of tuples, then every tuple, preceded by its length, in increasing
lexicographic order and without repetition.

**Instances of the operations family.** A field is written by its *view*, the
meaning its constraints use, and not by its internal representation, so that
two representations of the same constraints have the same word. The word
consists of

- a flag, `0` for the standard encoding and `1` for high multiplicity, the number
  of jobs and the number of machines;
- for every job a record, preceded by its length: its number of operations, the
  processing time of every operation on every machine, its deadline (`0` for
  none, or `1` followed by the deadline), and three blocks: the sets of machines
  each operation may occupy, the setup time of each operation at the server, and
  the transport delays between its operations; and its batch for batch setups;
- a block of the facts on pairs of jobs: `(0, i, j)` when `i` precedes `j`,
  `(1, i, j, s, l)` for the lag `±l` of such a pair (`s = 1` for a negative lag),
  and `(2, i, j, c)` when the pair has communication delay `c`;
- a block of the global facts: `(0, t)` for every forbidden time,
  `(1, a, b, s)` for the setup time `s` from batch `a` to batch `b`, for the
  batches of jobs, and, when the problem has a transport robot, `(2, i, i', t)`
  for the empty moving time `t` of the robot from machine `i` to machine `i'`,
  for all machines (all `0` when the robot has no empty moves);
- for every job its release date, weight and due date (`1` and `0` when the
  objective has none), three numbers each, in the order of the jobs.

The release dates, weights and due dates come last so that changing the
objective — which the threshold steps between objectives do — rewrites only the
end of the word. With high multiplicity the jobs are written as a block of their
distinct records, each followed by the job's release date, weight and due date and
preceded by the number of jobs that have both, and there are no facts on pairs.

**Instances of batching**: the number of jobs, the setup time and the capacity,
then for every job its processing time, release date, weight, due date, deadline
and size, then the block of precedence pairs, each with its lag. **Rejection**: the number of jobs
and the budget, then the processing time and rejection cost of every job.
**Machine covering**: the numbers of jobs and machines and the processing times.

**Schedules.** A schedule of the operations family is the list of its pieces,
each written as its job, operation, start and length (a rational as numerator
and reduced denominator) and the sorted machines it occupies. With high
multiplicity a schedule is written compactly, by *machine patterns*: a list of
groups, each a number $c$ of machines followed by the pieces every one of them
runs, a piece written as the type of its job (the position of the job's tuple in
the block of distinct records), its operation, start and length. The groups use
consecutive machines, $c$ for a group, and the $k$-th piece of a type and an
operation goes to the $k$-th job of that type, in the order of the jobs; every
operation is one piece. A batch schedule
writes for every job its batch and the start and processing time of that batch;
a rejection schedule for every job whether it is accepted and its start; a
covering the machine of every job.

**Online.** For problems whose jobs arrive online, the scheduler sees at time $t$
the records of the jobs released by $t$ (with their numbers), the facts on pairs
of them, and the global facts; two schedules made the same decisions up to $t$ if
they have the same pieces starting before $t$. Other problems are revealed at
once.

namespace Lax434175.StandardReading
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Results
open Lax434175.ResultParameters

-- Blocks

/-- The list writes the set: increasing, without repetition, and with the same
elements. -/
def Lists (S : Set (List ℕ)) (L : List (List ℕ)) : Prop :=
  L.Pairwise (· < ·) ∧ ∀ t, t ∈ L ↔ t ∈ S

/-- A list of tuples, each preceded by its length, after their number. -/
def flat (L : List (List ℕ)) : List ℕ := L.length :: L.flatMap fun t => t.length :: t

/-- The word is the canonical block of the set. -/
def Block (S : Set (List ℕ)) (b : List ℕ) : Prop := ∃ L, Lists S L ∧ b = flat L

/-- An integer as sign and absolute value. -/
def int (z : ℤ) : List ℕ := [if z < 0 then 1 else 0, z.natAbs]

/-- A deadline: `0` for none, `1` and the value otherwise. -/
def enat (e : ℕ∞) : List ℕ := if e = ⊤ then [0] else [1, e.toNat]

/-- A rational as numerator and denominator. -/
def rat (q : NNRat) : List ℕ := [q.num, q.den]

/-- A set of machines, sorted. -/
def machinesWord {m : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin m)) : List ℕ :=
  (S.image Fin.val).sort (· ≤ ·)

-- The operations family

section Ops

variable {s : Spec OperationsFamily.family} (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s)

/-- The fixed part of the record of a job. -/
def jobHead (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : List ℕ :=
  [x.base.ops j] ++
    (List.ofFn fun k : Fin (x.base.ops j) => List.ofFn fun i => x.base.p j k i).flatten ++
    enat (Deadlines.view (K := Operations.kernel) (s.module .deadlines) (x.data .deadlines) j)

/-- The release date, weight and due date of a job. -/
def objOf (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : List ℕ := [x.base.r j, Ops.weight s x j, Ops.due s x j]

/-- The release dates, weights and due dates of all jobs, three numbers each. -/
def objWord : List ℕ := (List.ofFn (objOf x)).flatten

/-- The machines an operation of the job may occupy. -/
def machineTuples (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ (k : Fin (x.base.ops j)) (S : Finset (Fin x.base.machines)),
    Operations.Machines.view (s.module .machineSets)
      (x.data .machineSets : Operations.Machines.Data _ x.base) ⟨j, k⟩ S ∧
    t = k.val :: machinesWord S}

/-- The setup times of the operations of the job at the server. -/
def serverTuples (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ (k : Fin (x.base.ops j)) (f : Operations.Op x.base → ℕ),
    Servers.view (s.module .server) (x.data .server : Servers.Data (Operations.Op x.base) _) =
      some f ∧ t = [k.val, f ⟨j, k⟩]}

/-- The transport delays between the operations of the job. -/
def transportTuples (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ k k' : Fin (x.base.ops j),
    t = [k.val, k'.val, (x.data .transportation : Transportation.Data x.base.toShop).1 j k k']}

/-- The batch of the job for batch setups. -/
def batchOf (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  ShopExtras.BatchSetups.batch (x := x.base.toShop) (s.module .batchSetups)
    (x.data .batchSetups) j

/-- The word is the record of the job. -/
def Record (j : Fin x.base.jobs) (b : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ b₁ b₂ b₃, Block (machineTuples x j) b₁ ∧ Block (serverTuples x j) b₂ ∧
    Block (transportTuples x j) b₃ ∧ b = jobHead x j ++ b₁ ++ b₂ ++ b₃ ++ [batchOf x j]

/-- The facts on pairs of jobs. -/
def pairTuples : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ i j : Fin x.base.jobs, Ops.prec s x i j ∧ t = [0, i.val, j.val]} ∪
  {t | ∃ i j : Fin x.base.jobs, Ops.prec s x i j ∧
    t = [1, i.val, j.val] ++ int ((s.module .precedence).lags.view (x.data .precedence).2 i j)} ∪
  {t | ∃ (i j : Fin x.base.jobs) (c : ℕ), CommunicationDelays.view (s.module .communicationDelays)
    (x.data .communicationDelays : CommunicationDelays.Data _ x.base.toPar) i j c ∧
    t = [2, i.val, j.val, c]}

/-- The global facts. -/
def globalTuples : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ τ ∈ ForbiddenTimes.view (s.module .forbiddenTimes) (x.data .forbiddenTimes), t = [0, τ]} ∪
  {t | ∃ i j : Fin x.base.jobs, t = [1, batchOf x i, batchOf x j,
    ShopExtras.BatchSetups.setup (x := x.base.toShop) (s.module .batchSetups)
      (x.data .batchSetups) (batchOf x i) (batchOf x j)]} ∪
  {t | (s.module .transportation).robot = true ∧ ∃ i i' : Fin x.base.machines,
    t = [2, i.val, i'.val, (x.data .transportation : Transportation.Data x.base.toShop).2 i i']}

/-- The records of all jobs, in order, each preceded by its length. -/
def Records (b : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ R : Fin x.base.jobs → List ℕ, (∀ j, Record x j (R j)) ∧
    b = (List.ofFn fun j => (R j).length :: R j).flatten

/-- The distinct records, each with the number of jobs that have it. -/
noncomputable def typeTuples : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ b j, Record x j b ∧
    t = Nat.card {j' // Record x j' b ∧ objOf x j' = objOf x j} :: (b ++ objOf x j)}

/-- The word of an instance of the operations family. -/
def EncodesOps (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ b₂ b₃, Block (pairTuples x) b₂ ∧ Block (globalTuples x) b₃ ∧
    ((s.module .encoding = .standard ∧ ∃ b₁, Records x b₁ ∧
        w = [0, x.base.jobs, x.base.machines] ++ b₁ ++ b₂ ++ b₃ ++ objWord x) ∨
     (s.module .encoding = .highMultiplicity ∧ pairTuples x = ∅ ∧ ∃ b₁, Block (typeTuples x) b₁ ∧
        w = [1, x.base.jobs, x.base.machines] ++ b₁ ++ b₂ ++ b₃))

/-- The word of a piece of a schedule. -/
def pieceWord (q : Operations.Piece x.base) : List ℕ :=
  [q.op.1.val, q.op.2.val] ++ rat q.start ++ rat q.length ++ machinesWord q.machines

/-- The word of a schedule: its pieces in order. -/
def schedWord (σ : Operations.Sched x.base) : List ℕ := flat (σ.pieces.map (pieceWord x))

/-- The type of a job in a high-multiplicity word: the position of its tuple in
the canonical list of the distinct records. -/
def TypeIndex (j : Fin x.base.jobs) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ L b, Lists (typeTuples x) L ∧ Record x j b ∧
    L[t]? = some (Nat.card {j' // Record x j' b ∧ objOf x j' = objOf x j} :: (b ++ objOf x j))

end Ops

/-- A piece of a machine pattern: the type of its job, its operation, start and
length. -/
structure Slot where
  type : ℕ
  op : ℕ
  start : NNRat
  length : NNRat

/-- A group of a compact schedule: a number of machines and the pieces each of
them runs. -/
abbrev Group := ℕ × List Slot

/-- The word of a group. -/
def groupWord (g : Group) : List ℕ :=
  g.1 :: flat (g.2.map fun q => [q.type, q.op] ++ rat q.start ++ rat q.length)

/-- The word of a compact schedule. -/
def compactWord (G : List Group) : List ℕ := flat (G.map groupWord)

/-- The pieces of a compact schedule with their machines, the groups using
consecutive machines from `base` on. -/
def expand : List Group → ℕ → List (ℕ × Slot)
  | [], _ => []
  | (c, P) :: G, base =>
      (List.range c).flatMap (fun k => P.map fun q => (base + k, q)) ++ expand G (base + c)

section Ops

variable {s : Spec OperationsFamily.family} (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s)

/-- The schedule is the one the compact schedule writes: piece by piece the same
machine, operation, start and length, a job of the slot's type, and the `k`-th
slot of a type and an operation for the `k`-th job of that type. -/
def ExpandsTo (G : List Group) (σ : Operations.Sched x.base) : Prop :=
  σ.pieces.length = (expand G 0).length ∧
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (hσ : n < σ.pieces.length) (hG : n < (expand G 0).length),
    (σ.pieces[n].machines.image Fin.val = {((expand G 0)[n]).1}) ∧
    σ.pieces[n].op.2.val = ((expand G 0)[n]).2.op ∧
    σ.pieces[n].start = ((expand G 0)[n]).2.start ∧
    σ.pieces[n].length = ((expand G 0)[n]).2.length ∧
    TypeIndex x σ.pieces[n].op.1 ((expand G 0)[n]).2.type ∧
    Nat.card {j : Fin x.base.jobs // j < σ.pieces[n].op.1 ∧ TypeIndex x j ((expand G 0)[n]).2.type} =
      ((expand G 0).take n).countP fun b =>
        b.2.type == ((expand G 0)[n]).2.type && b.2.op == ((expand G 0)[n]).2.op

/-- What is revealed at time `t`: the records of the jobs released by `t` with
their numbers, the facts on pairs of them, and the global facts. -/
def RevealedOps (t : NNRat) (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (R : Fin x.base.jobs → List ℕ) (b₂ b₃ : List ℕ), (∀ j, Record x j (R j)) ∧
    Block {u ∈ pairTuples x | ∀ v ∈ u.drop 1 |>.take 2,
      ∃ j : Fin x.base.jobs, j.val = v ∧ (x.base.r j : NNRat) ≤ t} b₂ ∧
    Block (globalTuples x) b₃ ∧
    w = [x.base.machines] ++ ((List.ofFn fun j => (j, R j)).filter fun p =>
      decide ((x.base.r p.1 : NNRat) ≤ t)).flatMap
        (fun p => p.1.val :: p.2.length :: (p.2 ++ objOf x p.1)) ++
      b₂ ++ b₃

end Ops

open Classical in
/-- The standard reading of the operations family. -/
noncomputable def ops : Reading OperationsFamily.family where
  Encodes _ w x := EncodesOps x w
  Decodes s x w σ := if s.module .encoding = .highMultiplicity then
    ∃ G, w = compactWord G ∧ ExpandsTo x G σ else w = schedWord x σ
  reveal s :=
    { same := fun x y t =>
        if s.module .releaseDates = .online then ∀ w, RevealedOps x t w ↔ RevealedOps y t w
        else ∀ w, EncodesOps x w ↔ EncodesOps y w
      agree := fun x y σ τ t =>
        flat ((σ.pieces.filter fun q => decide (q.start < t)).map (pieceWord x)) =
          flat ((τ.pieces.filter fun q => decide (q.start < t)).map (pieceWord y)) }

-- The batching family

section Batch

variable {s : Spec BatchFamily.family} (x : Inst BatchFamily.family s)

/-- The record of a job. -/
def batchRecord (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : List ℕ :=
  [x.base.p j, x.base.r j, Batch.weight s x j,
    Objectives.dueDate (K := BatchFamily.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j] ++
  enat (Deadlines.view (K := BatchFamily.kernel) (s.module (.field .deadlines))
    (x.data (.field .deadlines)) j) ++
  [Batching.Capacity.size (x := x.base) (s.module (.field .capacity)) (x.data (.field .capacity)) j]

/-- The precedence pairs, each with its lag. -/
def batchPairs : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {t | ∃ i j : Fin x.base.jobs,
    (s.module (.field .precedence)).order.view (x.data (.field .precedence)).1 i j ∧
    t = [i.val, j.val] ++ int ((s.module (.field .precedence)).lags.view (x.data (.field .precedence)).2 i j)}

/-- The word of a batching instance. -/
def EncodesBatch (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ b, Block (batchPairs x) b ∧
    w = [x.base.jobs, x.base.setup,
      Batching.Capacity.bound (x := x.base) (s.module (.field .capacity)) (x.data (.field .capacity))] ++
      (List.ofFn fun j => batchRecord x j).flatten ++ b

/-- The word of a batch schedule: for every job its batch and that batch's start
and processing time. -/
def batchSchedWord (σ : BatchFamily.Sched x.base) : List ℕ :=
  (List.ofFn fun j => [σ.batch j, σ.start (σ.batch j), σ.length (σ.batch j)]).flatten

end Batch

/-- The standard reading of the batching family. -/
noncomputable def batch : Reading BatchFamily.family where
  Encodes _ w x := EncodesBatch x w
  Decodes _ x w σ := w = batchSchedWord x σ
  reveal _ :=
    { same := fun x y _ => ∀ w, EncodesBatch x w ↔ EncodesBatch y w
      agree := fun x y σ τ _ => batchSchedWord x σ = batchSchedWord y τ }

-- The standalone problems

/-- The standard reading of single-machine scheduling with rejection. -/
noncomputable def rejection : PReading Rejection.problem where
  Encodes w x := w = [x.jobs, x.budget] ++ (List.ofFn fun j => [x.p j, x.e j]).flatten
  Decodes _ w σ := w = (List.ofFn fun j =>
    [if j ∈ σ.accepted then 1 else 0, σ.start j]).flatten
  reveal :=
    { same := fun x y _ => x = y
      agree := fun _ _ _ _ _ => True }

/-- The standard reading of machine covering. -/
def covering : PReading MachineCovering.problem where
  Encodes w x := w = [x.jobs, x.machines] ++ List.ofFn x.p
  Decodes _ w σ := w = List.ofFn fun j => (σ j).val
  reveal :=
    { same := fun x y _ => x = y
      agree := fun _ _ _ _ _ => True }

end Lax434175.StandardReading

concepts.title: Strong and plain hardness
concepts.description:
A problem is *strongly* NP-hard, W[t]-hard or para-NP-hard when it is hard already on
the words whose numbers are at most a fixed polynomial in the length of the word, as
when the numbers are written in unary. Plain hardness asks the same of all words,
the numbers written in binary. The words with small numbers form a subproblem, and
the identity reduces it to the whole problem.

**Theorem.** Strong NP-hardness implies NP-hardness, strong W[t]-hardness implies
W[t]-hardness, and strong para-NP-hardness implies para-NP-hardness, for every
parameter.

The algorithmic counterpart of strong hardness: a problem is *pseudo-polynomially
fixed-parameter tractable* in $\kappa$ when, for every polynomial bound on the
numbers, it is fixed-parameter tractable in $\kappa$ on the words whose numbers obey
the bound. A problem that is W[t]-hard and pseudo-polynomially fixed-parameter
tractable is *weakly* W[t]-hard: its hardness needs large numbers.

**Theorem.** If a problem is strongly W[t]-hard and pseudo-polynomially
fixed-parameter tractable for the same parameter, then W[t] ⊆ FPT.

/-!
---
title: Strong and plain hardness
type: theorem

-/

namespace Lax434175.StrongHardness
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results
open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions Lax496464.WH_B4_Hierarchies

variable {P : Problem} (R : PReading P)

/-- Fixed-parameter tractable in `κ` on the words with numbers at most any fixed
polynomial in their length. -/
def PseudoFPT (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
  ∀ c d, restrict (parameterized R κ) (Small c d) ∈ FPT

/-- W[t]-hard, and pseudo-polynomially fixed-parameter tractable for the same
parameter. -/
def WeaklyWHard (t : ℕ) (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := WHard R t κ ∧ PseudoFPT R κ

variable {R}

axiom npHard_of_strongly : StronglyNPHard R → NPHard R

axiom wHard_of_strongly {t : ℕ} {κ : TParameter P} : StronglyWHard R t κ → WHard R t κ

axiom paraNPHard_of_strongly {κ : TParameter P} : StronglyParaNPHard R κ → ParaNPHard R κ

axiom exclusive_weak {t : ℕ} {κ : TParameter P} :
    StronglyWHard R t κ → PseudoFPT R κ → W t ⊆ FPT

end Lax434175.StrongHardness

concepts.title: Para-NP-hardness along the steps between objectives
concepts.description:
A step between objectives (concept `ThresholdWords`: the makespan and the maximum
lateness to the number of late jobs and to the total tardiness, flow time to
tardiness, completion time to flow time) rewrites only the objective data and the
threshold of the standard word; the instance of the kernel, with its jobs,
machines, processing times and release dates, stays the same. So a parameter that
reads only the kernel instance takes the same value before and after the step.

A parameter of the target objective is *bounded on the kernel instance* by one of
the source objective if, for any two instances with the same kernel instance, the
first is at most the second.

**Theorem.** If the source objective is para-NP-hard for a parameter, and a
parameter of the target is bounded on the kernel instance by it, the target is
para-NP-hard for that parameter.

**Theorem.** The number of jobs $n$, the number of machines $m$, the largest
processing time $p_{\max}$, the numbers $\#p$ and $\#r$ of distinct processing
times and release dates, the number of kinds of machines and the rank of the
processing time matrix are each bounded on the kernel instance by themselves.

namespace Lax434175.ThresholdParams
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ThresholdWords
open Lax434175.ResultParameters

variable (values : (i : OperationsFamily.FieldName) → (OperationsFamily.family.module i).Value)

/-- `κt` is at most `κs` on any two instances with the same kernel instance. -/
def BaseBound (o o' : Objectives.Value) (κs : TParameter (problem _ (Thresholds.withObjective values o)))
    (κt : TParameter (problem _ (Thresholds.withObjective values o'))) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y D D', y.base = x.base → κt y D' ≤ κs x D

axiom paraNPHard_step (hs : values .encoding = .standard) {o o' : Objectives.Value} {mode : StepMode}
    (hm : stepOf o o' = some mode) {κs : TParameter (problem _ (Thresholds.withObjective values o))}
    {κt : TParameter (problem _ (Thresholds.withObjective values o'))}
    (hκ : BaseBound values o o' κs κt) :
    ParaNPHard (StandardReading.ops.at (Thresholds.withObjective values o)) κs →
      ParaNPHard (StandardReading.ops.at (Thresholds.withObjective values o')) κt

axiom base_n (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.n _)) (lift (Ops.n _))
axiom base_m (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.m _)) (lift (Ops.m _))
axiom base_pmax (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.pmax _)) (lift (Ops.pmax _))
axiom base_numP (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.numP _)) (lift (Ops.numP _))
axiom base_numR (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.numR _)) (lift (Ops.numR _))
axiom base_kinds (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.kinds _)) (lift (Ops.kinds _))
axiom base_rank (o o' : Objectives.Value) :
    BaseBound values o o' (lift (Ops.rank _)) (lift (Ops.rank _))

end Lax434175.ThresholdParams

concepts.title: Threshold reductions between objectives
concepts.description:
Consider the problems assembled from arbitrary constraint modules over a
kernel and the completion-time objectives.

Some relations between objectives hold for decision versions only. Let $D$
be an integer.

- The makespan is at most $D$ exactly if no job is late for the common due
  date $D$: $C_{\max} \le D$ if and only if $\sum_j U_j \le 0$. For negative
  $D$ both sides are made false: the due date is $0$ and the threshold $-1$.
- The maximum lateness is at most $D$ exactly if no job is tardy for the due
  dates $d_j + D$: $L_{\max} \le D$ if and only if $\sum_j T_j \le 0$. If
  some $d_j + D$ is negative, or there are no jobs and $D$ is negative, the
  left side is false and the threshold is $-1$.
- The maximum lateness is at most $D$ exactly if no job is late for the due
  dates $d_j + D$: $L_{\max} \le D$ if and only if $\sum_j U_j \le 0$, with
  the same treatment of negative due dates.
- Flow time is tardiness for the due dates $d_j = r_j$: $\sum_j w_j F_j$ and
  $\sum_j w_j T_j$ with these due dates are the same cost, weighted or not.
- If every job completes no earlier than its release date in every feasible
  schedule, the maximum flow time is the maximum lateness for the due dates
  $d_j = r_j$.
- If every job completes no earlier than its release date in every feasible
  schedule, then $\sum_j w_j F_j = \sum_j w_j C_j - \sum_j w_j r_j$, so
  $\sum_j w_j C_j \le D$ if and only if
  $\sum_j w_j F_j \le D - \sum_j w_j r_j$; likewise without weights.

In all cases the kernel instance, the data of the constraint modules and the
schedule are unchanged.

A specification $s$ reduces to a specification $t$ if $s$ is field by field
a special case of $t$, possibly after replacing the makespan or maximum
lateness of $s$ by the number of late jobs or by the total tardiness, or the
total flow time of $s$, weighted or not, by the total tardiness. It reduces to
$t$ through flow time if it is so after replacing the total completion time of
$s$ by the total flow time, weighted or not, or the maximum flow time by the
maximum lateness.
Both relations are decidable.

**Theorem.** The equivalences hold. If the constraint modules are sound and
$s$ reduces to $t$, then the decision version of the problem of $s$ reduces
to that of the problem of $t$; the same holds for reductions through flow
time if release dates are respected.

**Theorem.** Every reduction obtained from these steps and a field-wise
comparison is in place: it keeps the kernel instance and every invariant
parameter of a constraint field, and changes only the due dates and the
threshold.

namespace Lax434175.Thresholds
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175

/-- The family of given constraint modules with the completion-time
objectives. -/
def family {K : Kernel} (Name : Type) (module : Name → Module K) : Family K where
  ModuleName := Name
  module := module
  objective := Objectives.objective K

variable {K : Kernel} {Name : Type} {module : Name → Module K}

instance [Fintype Name] : Fintype (family Name module).ModuleName :=
  inferInstanceAs (Fintype Name)

/-- The specification with given module values and a given objective. -/
def withObjective (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value) (objective : Objectives.Value) :
    Spec (family Name module) where
  module := values
  objective := objective

/-- An instance with the makespan objective and a threshold, read as an
instance counting the jobs that are late for the threshold. -/
def toLate (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .makespan)) (D : ℤ) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumU) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := fun _ => D.toNat
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- The threshold for the number of late jobs. -/
def lateThreshold (D : ℤ) : ℤ := if D < 0 then -1 else 0

/-- An instance with the maximum-lateness objective and a threshold, read as
an instance measuring tardiness for the due dates increased by the
threshold. -/
def toTardy (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax)) (D : ℤ) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumT) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := fun j => ((Objectives.dueDate .lmax x.objectiveData j : ℤ) + D).toNat
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- The threshold for the total tardiness. -/
def tardyThreshold (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax)) (D : ℤ) : ℤ :=
  if (K.jobs x.base = 0 ∧ D < 0) ∨
      ∃ j, (Objectives.dueDate .lmax x.objectiveData j : ℤ) + D < 0 then -1 else 0

/-- An instance with the maximum-lateness objective and a threshold, read as
an instance counting the jobs that are late for the due dates increased by
the threshold. -/
def toLateShifted (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax)) (D : ℤ) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumU) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := fun j => ((Objectives.dueDate .lmax x.objectiveData j : ℤ) + D).toNat
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- An instance with total flow time, read with total tardiness for the due
dates equal to the release dates. -/
def flowToTardy (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumF)) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumT) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := fun j => K.release x.base j
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- An instance with total weighted flow time, read with total weighted
tardiness for the due dates equal to the release dates. -/
def weightedFlowToTardy (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWF)) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWT) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := (Objectives.weight .sumWF x.objectiveData, fun j => K.release x.base j)
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- An instance with maximum flow time, read with maximum lateness for the due
dates equal to the release dates. -/
def flowToLateness (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .fmax)) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := fun j => K.release x.base j
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- An instance with total completion time, read with total flow time. -/
def toFlow (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumC)) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumF) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := ()
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- An instance with total weighted completion time, read with total weighted
flow time. -/
def toWeightedFlow (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWC)) :
    Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWF) where
  base := x.base
  data := x.data
  admitted := x.admitted
  objectiveData := Objectives.weight .sumWC x.objectiveData
  objectiveAdmitted := trivial

/-- In every schedule that is feasible for the kernel and the modules, every
job completes no earlier than its release date. -/
def ReleaseRespected (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : K.Inst) (data : (i : Name) → (module i).Data (values i) x) (σ : K.Sched x),
    (∀ i, (module i).admits (values i) x (data i)) → K.feasible x σ →
    (∀ i, (module i).constraint (values i) x (data i) σ) →
    ∀ j, (K.release x j : NNRat) ≤ K.completion x σ j

axiom makespan_iff_sumU (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .makespan)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .makespan)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumU)).Decides (toLate values x D) (lateThreshold D)

axiom lmax_iff_sumT (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .lmax)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumT)).Decides (toTardy values x D)
        (tardyThreshold values x D)

axiom lmax_iff_sumU (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .lmax)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .lmax)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumU)).Decides (toLateShifted values x D)
        (tardyThreshold values x D)

axiom sumF_iff_sumT (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumF)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .sumF)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumT)).Decides (flowToTardy values x) D

axiom sumWF_iff_sumWT (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWF)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .sumWF)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumWT)).Decides (weightedFlowToTardy values x) D

axiom fmax_iff_lmax (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value) (h : ReleaseRespected values)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .fmax)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .fmax)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .lmax)).Decides (flowToLateness values x) D

axiom sumC_iff_sumF (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value) (h : ReleaseRespected values)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumC)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .sumC)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumF)).Decides (toFlow values x)
        ((D - ∑ j, (K.release x.base j : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℚ)

axiom sumWC_iff_sumWF (values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value) (h : ReleaseRespected values)
    (x : Inst (family Name module) (withObjective values .sumWC)) (D : ℤ) :
    (problem _ (withObjective values .sumWC)).Decides x D ↔
      (problem _ (withObjective values .sumWF)).Decides (toWeightedFlow values x)
        ((D - ∑ j, (Objectives.weight .sumWC x.objectiveData j : ℤ) * (K.release x.base j : ℤ) :
          ℤ) : ℚ)

/-- The objective of a specification. -/
def objectiveOf (s : Spec (family Name module)) : Objectives.Value := s.objective

/-- The specification `s` reduces to `t`: field by field, possibly after one
of the threshold steps. -/
def Reduces (s t : Spec (family Name module)) : Prop :=
  s.le t ∨
  ((objectiveOf s = .makespan ∨ objectiveOf s = .lmax) ∧
    (withObjective s.module .sumU : Spec (family Name module)).le t) ∨
  ((objectiveOf s = .makespan ∨ objectiveOf s = .lmax ∨ objectiveOf s = .sumF) ∧
    (withObjective s.module .sumT : Spec (family Name module)).le t) ∨
  (objectiveOf s = .sumWF ∧ (withObjective s.module .sumWT : Spec (family Name module)).le t)

/-- The specification `s` reduces to `t` after replacing completion time by
flow time. -/
def ReducesThroughFlow (s t : Spec (family Name module)) : Prop :=
  (objectiveOf s = .sumC ∧ (withObjective s.module .sumF : Spec (family Name module)).le t) ∨
  (objectiveOf s = .sumWC ∧ (withObjective s.module .sumWF : Spec (family Name module)).le t) ∨
  (objectiveOf s = .fmax ∧ (withObjective s.module .lmax : Spec (family Name module)).le t)

instance [Fintype Name] (s t : Spec (family Name module)) : Decidable (Reduces s t) := by
  unfold Reduces
  infer_instance

instance [Fintype Name] (s t : Spec (family Name module)) :
    Decidable (ReducesThroughFlow s t) := by
  unfold ReducesThroughFlow
  infer_instance

axiom reducible_of_reduces (sound : ∀ i, (module i).Sound) {s t : Spec (family Name module)} :
    Reduces s t → Reducible (problem _ s) (problem _ t)

axiom reducible_of_reducesThroughFlow (sound : ∀ i, (module i).Sound)
    (respected : ∀ values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value, ReleaseRespected values)
    {s t : Spec (family Name module)} :
    ReducesThroughFlow s t → Reducible (problem _ s) (problem _ t)

axiom inPlace_of_reduces (sound : ∀ i, (module i).Sound) {s t : Spec (family Name module)} :
    Reduces s t → Parameters.ReducibleInPlace s t

axiom inPlace_of_reducesThroughFlow (sound : ∀ i, (module i).Sound)
    (respected : ∀ values : (i : Name) → (module i).Value, ReleaseRespected values)
    {s t : Spec (family Name module)} :
    ReducesThroughFlow s t → Parameters.ReducibleInPlace s t

end Lax434175.Thresholds

concepts.title: The steps between objectives on words
concepts.description:
The zoo relates objectives by reductions of decision versions that change the
objective data and the threshold: the makespan and the maximum lateness reduce to
the number of late jobs and to the total tardiness, flow time to tardiness with
due dates at the release dates, and completion time to flow time with the
threshold lowered by the release dates (`Thresholds`). On standard words such a
step rewrites only the final block of release dates, weights and due dates and
the threshold.

There are five modes. With the threshold $D$, the release date $r_j$, the weight
$w_j$ and the due date $d_j$ of job $j$:

| Mode | Steps | New due date | New threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| late, constant | $C_{\max} \to \sum U_j, \sum T_j$ | $\max(D, 0)$ | $-1$ if $D < 0$, else $0$ |
| late, shifted | $L_{\max} \to \sum U_j, \sum T_j$ | $\max(d_j + D, 0)$ | $-1$ if $n = 0$ and $D < 0$ or some $d_j + D < 0$, else $0$ |
| release | $\sum F_j \to \sum T_j$, $\sum w_jF_j \to \sum w_jT_j$, $F_{\max} \to L_{\max}$ | $r_j$ | $D$ |
| shift | $\sum C_j \to \sum F_j$ | $d_j$ | $D - \sum_j r_j$ |
| weighted shift | $\sum w_jC_j \to \sum w_jF_j$ | $d_j$ | $D - \sum_j w_j r_j$ |

The word map reads the number $n$ of jobs from the second number of the word and
the threshold from its last two numbers, and rewrites the $3n$ numbers before the
threshold; a word too short for this is left unchanged.

**Theorem.** The word map of every mode is computable in polynomial time on the
word RAM. On the standard word of an instance $x$ of a specification of the
operations family with the standard encoding and the source objective, with
threshold $D$, it writes the standard word of the stepped instance with the new
threshold, which has the same answer.

**Theorem.** Consequently NP-hardness and strong NP-hardness go from the source
objective to the target objective.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.StandardReading

/-!
---
title: The steps between objectives on words
type: theorem
---
The zoo relates objectives by reductions of decision versions that change the
objective data and the threshold: the makespan and the maximum lateness reduce to
the number of late jobs and to the total tardiness, flow time to tardiness with
due dates at the release dates, and completion time to flow time with the
threshold lowered by the release dates (`Thresholds`). On standard words such a
step rewrites only the final block of release dates, weights and due dates and
the threshold.

There are five modes. With the threshold $D$, the release date $r_j$, the weight
$w_j$ and the due date $d_j$ of job $j$:

| Mode | Steps | New due date | New threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| late, constant | $C_{\max} \to \sum U_j, \sum T_j$ | $\max(D, 0)$ | $-1$ if $D < 0$, else $0$ |
| late, shifted | $L_{\max} \to \sum U_j, \sum T_j$ | $\max(d_j + D, 0)$ | $-1$ if $n = 0$ and $D < 0$ or some $d_j + D < 0$, else $0$ |
| release | $\sum F_j \to \sum T_j$, $\sum w_jF_j \to \sum w_jT_j$, $F_{\max} \to L_{\max}$ | $r_j$ | $D$ |
| shift | $\sum C_j \to \sum F_j$ | $d_j$ | $D - \sum_j r_j$ |
| weighted shift | $\sum w_jC_j \to \sum w_jF_j$ | $d_j$ | $D - \sum_j w_j r_j$ |

The word map reads the number $n$ of jobs from the second number of the word and
the threshold from its last two numbers, and rewrites the $3n$ numbers before the
threshold; a word too short for this is left unchanged.

**Theorem.** The word map of every mode is computable in polynomial time on the
word RAM. On the standard word of an instance $x$ of a specification of the
operations family with the standard encoding and the source objective, with
threshold $D$, it writes the standard word of the stepped instance with the new
threshold, which has the same answer.

**Theorem.** Consequently NP-hardness and strong NP-hardness go from the source
objective to the target objective.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ThresholdWords
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly Lax434175.Results

/-- The modes of the steps. -/
inductive StepMode
  | lateConst
  | lateShift
  | toRelease
  | shift
  | weightedShift
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The step from one objective to another, if there is one. -/
def stepOf : Objectives.Value → Objectives.Value → Option StepMode
  | .makespan, .sumU | .makespan, .sumT => some .lateConst
  | .lmax, .sumU | .lmax, .sumT => some .lateShift
  | .sumF, .sumT | .sumWF, .sumWT | .fmax, .lmax => some .toRelease
  | .sumC, .sumF => some .shift
  | .sumWC, .sumWF => some .weightedShift
  | _, _ => none

/-- The threshold of the sign and the absolute value. -/
def readThr (neg a : ℕ) : ℤ := if neg = 0 then (a : ℤ) else -(a : ℤ)

/-- The threshold as sign and absolute value. -/
def thrWord (D : ℤ) : List ℕ := [if D < 0 then 1 else 0, D.natAbs]

/-- The new due date. -/
def newDue : StepMode → ℤ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
  | .lateConst, D, _, _ => D.toNat
  | .lateShift, D, _, d => ((d : ℤ) + D).toNat
  | .toRelease, _, r, _ => r
  | .shift, _, _, d => d
  | .weightedShift, _, _, d => d

open Classical in
/-- The new threshold. -/
noncomputable def newThr : StepMode → ℕ → ℤ → (ℕ → ℕ) → (ℕ → ℕ) → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℤ
  | .lateConst, _, D, _, _, _ => if D < 0 then -1 else 0
  | .lateShift, n, D, _, _, d =>
      if (n = 0 ∧ D < 0) ∨ ∃ j < n, (d j : ℤ) + D < 0 then -1 else 0
  | .toRelease, _, D, _, _, _ => D
  | .shift, n, D, r, _, _ => D - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (r j : ℤ)
  | .weightedShift, n, D, r, w, _ => D - ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (w j : ℤ) * (r j : ℤ)

open Classical in
/-- The word map of a mode. -/
noncomputable def stepWord (mode : StepMode) (u : List ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  if u.length < 3 * u.getD 1 0 + 2 then u else
    let n := u.getD 1 0
    let base := u.length - 2 - 3 * n
    let D := readThr (u.getD (u.length - 2) 0) (u.getD (u.length - 1) 0)
    let r := fun j => u.getD (base + 3 * j) 0
    let w := fun j => u.getD (base + 3 * j + 1) 0
    let d := fun j => u.getD (base + 3 * j + 2) 0
    u.take base ++ (List.ofFn fun j : Fin n => [r j, w j, newDue mode D (r j) (d j)]).flatten ++
      thrWord (newThr mode n D r w d)

concepts.title: Time reversal
concepts.description:
Running a schedule backwards from a horizon $H$ turns a piece processing an
operation during $[a, b]$ into one processing it during $[H - b, H - a]$. A
job that completes at $C_j$ then starts at $H - C_j$, and a precedence
constraint $C_i + l_{ij} \le S_j$ becomes the constraint
$C'_j + l_{ij} \le S'_i$ of the reversed relation.

Hence the maximum lateness without release dates and the makespan with
release dates are equivalent:

- $L_{\max} \le D$ for due dates $d_j$ exactly if the reversed problem with
  release dates $r'_j = H - (d_j + D)$, $H = \max_j (d_j + D)$, has makespan
  at most $H$ (if some $d_j + D$ is negative, or there are no jobs and $D$ is
  negative, the threshold is $-1$);
- $C_{\max} \le D$ for release dates $r_j$ exactly if the reversed problem
  without release dates and with due dates $D - r_j$ has maximum lateness at
  most $0$ (if $D$ is negative or some $r_j$ exceeds $D$, the answer is no,
  and the reduction asks whether the maximum lateness for due dates $0$ is at
  most $-1$).

This is shown for the problems of the family with operations that have one
operation per job, no restarts, a reversible precedence class, no deadlines,
and none of the communication delays, server, forbidden times, transportation
delays, no-idle and batch setups, whose meaning changes under reversal. The
reversed specification has the reversed precedence class, the release dates
or none, and the makespan or the maximum lateness.

A specification $s$ reduces to $t$ by reversal if it is of this kind, and
either minimizes the maximum lateness without release dates and its reversal
with release dates and the makespan is field by field a special case of $t$,
or minimizes the makespan with release dates or none and its reversal without
release dates and with the maximum lateness is so. The relation is decidable.

**Theorem.** A specification that reduces to another by reversal describes a
problem whose decision version reduces to that of the other.

import Lax434175.DeadlineSteps
import Lax434175.PrecedenceReversal

/-!
---
title: Time reversal
type: theorem
---

  at most $H$ (if some $d_j + D$ is negative, or there are no jobs and $D$ is
  negative, the threshold is $-1$);
- $C_{\max} \le D$ for release dates $r_j$ exactly if the reversed problem
  without release dates and with due dates $D - r_j$ has maximum lateness at
  most $0$ (if $D$ is negative or some $r_j$ exceeds $D$, the answer is no,
  and the reduction asks whether the maximum lateness for due dates $0$ is at
  most $-1$).

This is shown for the problems of the family with operations that have one
operation per job, no restarts, a reversible precedence class, no deadlines,
and none of the communication delays, server, forbidden times, transportation
delays, no-idle and batch setups, whose meaning changes under reversal. The
reversed specification has the reversed precedence class, the release dates
or none, and the makespan or the maximum lateness.

A specification $s$ reduces to $t$ by reversal if it is of this kind, and

**Theorem.** A specification that reduces to another by reversal describes a
problem whose decision version reduces to that of the other.
-/

namespace Lax434175.TimeReversal
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Operations Lax434175.OperationsFamily

def isSingle : Structure → Bool
  | .single => true
  | _ => false

def notRestarts : Interruption.Mode → Bool
  | .restarts => false
  | _ => true

def noDelays : CommunicationDelays.Value → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def noServer : Servers.Value → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def noForbidden : ForbiddenTimes.Value → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def noTransport (v : Transportation.Value) : Bool :=
  (match v.shape with
    | .none => true
    | _ => false) && !v.robot

def noIdling : ShopExtras.NoIdle → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def noSetups : ShopExtras.BatchSetups → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def releaseNone : ReleaseDates.Value → Bool
  | .none => true
  | _ => false

def releaseKnown : ReleaseDates.Value → Bool
  | .online => false
  | _ => true

/-- The specification can be reversed. -/
def Reversible (s : Spec family) : Bool :=
  notRestarts (s.module .interruption) && isSingle (s.module .jobStructure) &&
    PrecedenceReversal.reversible (s.module .precedence).order && DeadlineSteps.noDeadlines (s.module .deadlines) &&
    noDelays (s.module .communicationDelays) && noServer (s.module .server) &&
    noForbidden (s.module .forbiddenTimes) && noTransport (s.module .transportation) &&
    noIdling (s.module .noIdle) && noSetups (s.module .batchSetups)

/-- The reversed specification, with given release dates and objective. -/
def reversed (s : Spec family) (release : ReleaseDates.Value) (objective : Objectives.Value) :
    Spec family where
  module
    | .precedence => (⟨PrecedenceReversal.reverse (s.module .precedence).order, (s.module .precedence).lags⟩ :
        Precedence.Value)
    | .releaseDates => release
    | i => s.module i
  objective := objective

/-- `s` reduces to `t` by reversal. -/
def ReducesByReversal (s t : Spec family) : Prop :=
  Reversible s = true ∧
    ((Thresholds.objectiveOf s = .lmax ∧ releaseNone (s.module .releaseDates) = true ∧
        (reversed s .releaseDates .makespan).le t) ∨
      (Thresholds.objectiveOf s = .makespan ∧ releaseKnown (s.module .releaseDates) = true ∧
        (reversed s .none .lmax).le t))

instance (s t : Spec family) : Decidable (ReducesByReversal s t) := by
  unfold ReducesByReversal
  infer_instance

axiom reducible_of_reducesByReversal {s t : Spec family} :
    ReducesByReversal s t → Reducible (problem family s) (problem family t)

end Lax434175.TimeReversal

      (Lax434175.Assembly.problem Lax434175.OperationsFamily.family t)

concepts.title: Transportation delays and a transport robot
concepts.description:
In a shop with transportation delays an instance carries, for every job $j$
and every ordered pair of its operations $k, l$, a delay $t_{jkl}$. Of any
two operations of a job, the later one may not start before the completion
of the earlier one plus the delay from the earlier to the later.

The shape field restricts the delays:

- none: all delays are $0$;
- uniform: all delays equal one number $T$;
- two values: there are two numbers, and the delays of each job all equal
  one of them;
- job: the delay depends on the job only, $t_j$;
- source: the delay depends on the earlier operation only, $t_k$;
- job and source: the delay does not depend on the later operation,
  $t_{jk}$;
- pair: the delay depends on the two positions only, $t_{kl}$, possibly
  required to be symmetric, $t_{kl} = t_{lk}$;
- job and pair: arbitrary delays $t_{jkl}$, possibly required to be
  symmetric, $t_{jkl} = t_{jlk}$.

A shape is a special case of another if its delays are among the other's.

With a transport robot, in addition every transport of a job from an
operation to the next one in its sequence is carried out by a single robot:
the transport starts no earlier than the completion of the operation, lasts
for the delay, and ends no later than the start of the next operation. The
robot may need time to travel empty, as in Brucker and Knust, *Complex
Scheduling*, §4.6: an instance then carries, for every two machines $i, i'$,
an empty moving time $t'_{ii'}$. Of any two transports, the later one departs
no earlier than the arrival of the earlier one plus the time the robot needs
to travel empty from the machines where it delivers the earlier one to the
machines where it picks up the later one, the largest empty moving time
between them. Unless the robot has empty moves, all empty moving times are
$0$, and two transports merely do not overlap.

A problem with a robot and one without are incomparable. A robot without
empty moves is a special case of one with them.

**Theorem.** The field of transportation delays is sound.

import Lax434175.Shops

/-!
---
title: Transportation delays and a transport robot
type: theorem
---
In a shop with transportation delays an instance carries, for every job $j$
and every ordered pair of its operations $k, l$, a delay $t_{jkl}$. Of any
two operations of a job, the later one may not start before the completion
of the earlier one plus the delay from the earlier to the later.

The shape field restricts the delays:

- none: all delays are $0$;
- uniform: all delays equal one number $T$;
- two values: there are two numbers, and the delays of each job all equal
  one of them;
- job: the delay depends on the job only, $t_j$;
- source: the delay depends on the earlier operation only, $t_k$;
- job and source: the delay does not depend on the later operation,
  $t_{jk}$;
- pair: the delay depends on the two positions only, $t_{kl}$, possibly
  required to be symmetric, $t_{kl} = t_{lk}$;
- job and pair: arbitrary delays $t_{jkl}$, possibly required to be
  symmetric, $t_{jkl} = t_{jlk}$.

A shape is a special case of another if its delays are among the other's.

With a transport robot, in addition every transport of a job from an
operation to the next one in its sequence is carried out by a single robot:
the transport starts no earlier than the completion of the operation, lasts
for the delay, and ends no later than the start of the next operation. The
robot may need time to travel empty, as in Brucker and Knust, *Complex
Scheduling*, §4.6: an instance then carries, for every two machines $i, i'$,
an empty moving time $t'_{ii'}$. Of any two transports, the later one departs
no earlier than the arrival of the earlier one plus the time the robot needs
to travel empty from the machines where it delivers the earlier one to the
machines where it picks up the later one, the largest empty moving time
between them. Unless the robot has empty moves, all empty moving times are
$0$, and two transports merely do not overlap.

A problem with a robot and one without are incomparable. A robot without
empty moves is a special case of one with them.

**Theorem.** The field of transportation delays is sound.
-/

namespace Lax434175.Transportation
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Shops

/-- The delays of an instance. -/
abbrev Delays (x : Inst) := (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ

inductive Shape
  | none
  | uniform
  | twoValues
  | job
  | source
  | jobSource
  | pairSymmetric
  | pair
  | jobPairSymmetric
  | jobPair
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The delays of a shape. -/
def Shape.holds {x : Inst} : Shape → Delays x → Prop
  | .none, t => ∀ j k l, t j k l = 0
  | .uniform, t => ∃ T, ∀ j k l, t j k l = T
  | .twoValues, t => ∃ T₁ T₂, ∀ j, (∀ k l, t j k l = T₁) ∨ (∀ k l, t j k l = T₂)
  | .job, t => ∀ j k l k' l', t j k l = t j k' l'
  | .source, t => ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ j k l, t j k l = g k.val
  | .jobSource, t => ∀ j k l l', t j k l = t j k l'
  | .pairSymmetric, t => ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, (∀ a b, g a b = g b a) ∧ ∀ j k l, t j k l = g k.val l.val
  | .pair, t => ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ j k l, t j k l = g k.val l.val
  | .jobPairSymmetric, t => ∀ j k l, t j k l = t j l k
  | .jobPair, _ => True

def Shape.le : Shape → Shape → Bool
  | _, .jobPair => true
  | .none, _ => true
  | .uniform, .none => false
  | .uniform, _ => true
  | .twoValues, .twoValues | .twoValues, .job | .twoValues, .jobSource
  | .twoValues, .jobPairSymmetric => true
  | .job, .job | .job, .jobSource | .job, .jobPairSymmetric => true
  | .source, .source | .source, .jobSource | .source, .pair => true
  | .jobSource, .jobSource => true
  | .pairSymmetric, .pairSymmetric | .pairSymmetric, .pair
  | .pairSymmetric, .jobPairSymmetric => true
  | .pair, .pair => true
  | .jobPairSymmetric, .jobPairSymmetric => true
  | _, _ => false

/-- Of two operations of a job, the later one waits for the delay. -/
def Delayed (x : Inst) (t : Delays x) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), k ≠ l →
    finish x σ ⟨j, k⟩ + t j k l ≤ σ.start j l ∨ finish x σ ⟨j, l⟩ + t j l k ≤ σ.start j k

/-- The empty moving times of the robot, from a machine to a machine. -/
abbrev EmptyMoves (x : Inst) := Fin x.machines → Fin x.machines → ℕ

/-- The time the robot needs to travel empty from a set of machines to
another: the largest empty moving time from a machine of the first to a
machine of the second. -/
def emptyTime {m : ℕ} (e : Fin m → Fin m → ℕ) (S S' : Finset (Fin m)) : ℕ :=
  S.sup fun i => S'.sup (e i)

/-- A single robot carries every job from each operation to the next, and
between two transports it travels empty from the machines where it delivers
the one to the machines where it picks up the other. -/
def Carried (x : Inst) (t : Delays x) (e : EmptyMoves x) (σ : Sched x) : Prop :=
  ∃ depart : (j : Fin x.jobs) → Fin (x.ops j) → ℕ,
    (∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      finish x σ ⟨j, k⟩ ≤ depart j k ∧ depart j k + t j k l ≤ σ.start j l) ∧
    ∀ j (k l : Fin (x.ops j)) j' (k' l' : Fin (x.ops j')), l.val = k.val + 1 →
      l'.val = k'.val + 1 → (⟨j, k⟩ : Op x) ≠ ⟨j', k'⟩ →
      depart j k + t j k l + emptyTime e (σ.machines j l) (σ.machines j' k') ≤ depart j' k' ∨
      depart j' k' + t j' k' l' + emptyTime e (σ.machines j' l') (σ.machines j k) ≤ depart j k

/-- A value of the field: a shape of delays, whether a robot carries the
jobs, and whether the robot needs time to travel empty. -/
structure Value where
  shape : Shape
  robot : Bool := false
  emptyMoves : Bool := false

/-- No transportation delays and no robot. -/
def Value.none : Value := ⟨.none, false, false⟩

/-- The data of the field: the delays and the empty moving times. -/
abbrev Data (x : Inst) := Delays x × EmptyMoves x

/-- The delays have the shape, and unless the value has a robot with empty
moves, the empty moving times are `0`. -/
def Value.admits {x : Inst} (v : Value) (d : Data x) : Prop :=
  v.shape.holds d.1 ∧ ((v.robot && v.emptyMoves) = false → ∀ i i', d.2 i i' = 0)

/-- The shape is a special case, both values have a robot or neither has,
and empty moves only if the other value has them. -/
def Value.le (v w : Value) : Bool :=
  Shape.le v.shape w.shape && decide (v.robot = w.robot) && (!v.emptyMoves || w.emptyMoves)

/-- The field of transportation delays. -/
def module : Module kernel where
  Value := Value
  Data _ x := Data x
  admits v _ d := v.admits d
  constraint v x d σ := Delayed x d.1 σ ∧ (v.robot = true → Carried x d.1 d.2 σ)
  le := Value.le
  embed _ _ d := d

axiom sound : module.Sound

end Lax434175.Transportation

concepts.title: Scheduling problems as parameterized problems on words
concepts.description:
A parameterized problem on words consists of the words that encode an
instance, the yes-instances among them, and a parameter read off the word.
Fixed-parameter tractability, fpt-reductions and hardness for a class of such
problems are those of the word RAM.

A coding of a family of scheduling problems says, for every specification,
which words encode which instance, such that a word encodes at most one
instance of a specification and a word that encodes an instance also encodes
it when the instance is read with a field-wise more general specification.

Given a coding, a specification $s$ and a parameter $\kappa$ of its problem,
the decision version of the problem of $s$ becomes a parameterized problem on
words. An instance $x$ with the integral threshold $D$ is encoded by a word
of $x$ followed by two entries, $1$ or $0$ according to whether $D$ is
negative, and $|D|$. The admissible words are these, the yes-instances are
those for which some feasible schedule has cost at most $D$, and the
parameter of the word is $\kappa(x)$.

**Theorem.** Let the fields of the family be sound, let $s$ be field by field
a special case of $t$, and let $\kappa_s$ and $\kappa_t$ be parameters with
$\kappa_t(x') \le g(\kappa_s(x))$ for a computable $g$ and every instance $x$
of $s$ read as an instance $x'$ of $t$. Then the parameterized problem of $s$
and $\kappa_s$ fpt-reduces to that of $t$ and $\kappa_t$; the reduction is
the identity on words. In particular this holds, with the same parameter on
both sides, for every parameter of the kernel instance and for every
invariant parameter of a constraint field. Consequently fixed-parameter
tractability passes from the problem of $t$ to that of $s$, and hardness for
a class from the problem of $s$ to that of $t$.

**Theorem.** Let the fields of the family be sound, let $s$ be field by field

$\kappa_t(x') \le g(\kappa_s(x))$ for a computable $g$ and every instance $x$
of $s$ read as an instance $x'$ of $t$. Then the parameterized problem of $s$
and $\kappa_s$ fpt-reduces to that of $t$ and $\kappa_t$; the reduction is
the identity on words. In particular this holds, with the same parameter on
both sides, for every parameter of the kernel instance and for every
invariant parameter of a constraint field. Consequently fixed-parameter
tractability passes from the problem of $t$ to that of $s$, and hardness for
a class from the problem of $s$ to that of $t$.
-/

namespace Lax434175.WordProblems
open Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules Lax434175.Assembly
open Lax434175.Parameters
open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions
open scoped Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions

/-- A coding of the instances of the problems of a family by words. -/
structure Coding {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) where
  /-- The word encodes the instance. -/
  Encodes : (s : Spec F) → List ℕ → Inst F s → Prop
  /-- A word encodes at most one instance. -/
  unique : ∀ (s : Spec F) (w : List ℕ) (x y : Inst F s), Encodes s w x → Encodes s w y → x = y
  /-- A word of an instance is a word of the instance read with a more
  general specification. -/
  lift : ∀ (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t) (w : List ℕ) (x : Inst F s),
    Encodes s w x → Encodes t w ((lift F hF h).map x)

variable {K : Kernel} {F : Family K}

/-- The word presents the instance together with the threshold: a word of the
instance followed by the sign and the absolute value of the threshold. -/
def EncodesDecision (C : Coding F) (s : Spec F) (w : List ℕ) (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ y, w = y ++ [if D < 0 then 1 else 0, D.natAbs] ∧ C.Encodes s y x

open Classical in
/-- The decision version of the problem of a specification, with a parameter,
as a parameterized problem on words. -/
noncomputable def wordProblem (C : Coding F) (s : Spec F) (κ : Parameter (problem F s)) :
    Lax888481.ParameterizedComplexity.Problem where
  Domain := {w | ∃ (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ), EncodesDecision C s w x D}
  Yes w := ∃ (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ), EncodesDecision C s w x D ∧ (problem F s).Decides x D
  param w := if h : ∃ (x : Inst F s) (D : ℤ), EncodesDecision C s w x D then κ h.choose else 0

axiom fptReduces_of_le (C : Coding F) (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t)
    (κs : Parameter (problem F s)) (κt : Parameter (problem F t)) (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hg : Computable g) (hκ : ∀ x, κt ((lift F hF h).map x) ≤ g (κs x)) :
    wordProblem C s κs ≤ᶠᵖᵗ wordProblem C t κt

axiom fptReduces_of_le_kernel (C : Coding F) (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t)
    (κ : K.Inst → ℕ) :
    wordProblem C s (ofKernel F κ s) ≤ᶠᵖᵗ wordProblem C t (ofKernel F κ t)

axiom fptReduces_of_le_field (C : Coding F) (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t)
    (i : F.ModuleName) (κ : FieldParameter (F.module i)) (hκ : κ.Invariant) :
    wordProblem C s (ofField F i κ s) ≤ᶠᵖᵗ wordProblem C t (ofField F i κ t)

axiom fpt_of_le_kernel (C : Coding F) (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t)
    (κ : K.Inst → ℕ) :
    IsParameterized (wordProblem C s (ofKernel F κ s)) →
      wordProblem C t (ofKernel F κ t) ∈ FPT → wordProblem C s (ofKernel F κ s) ∈ FPT

axiom hard_of_le_kernel (C : Coding F) (hF : F.Sound) {s t : Spec F} (h : s.le t)
    (κ : K.Inst → ℕ) (𝒞 : Set Lax888481.ParameterizedComplexity.Problem) :
    Hard 𝒞 (wordProblem C s (ofKernel F κ s)) → Hard 𝒞 (wordProblem C t (ofKernel F κ t))

end Lax434175.WordProblems

concepts.title: At most k scheduled jobs, and prescribed machine loads
concepts.description:
Two problems built on a problem $s$ of the family with operations, as used for
interval scheduling with eligible machine sets (lax-767944).

A job is *kept* by a schedule if it is on time, for an objective that counts
late jobs, or just in time, for one that counts jobs not just in time; for the
other objectives no job is kept.

**At most $k$ scheduled jobs.** An instance is an instance $x$ of $s$ together
with a number $k$. A schedule is a schedule of $x$ together with a set $S$ of
at most $k$ jobs, the jobs it schedules; it is feasible if the schedule is
feasible for $s$. Its cost is the weight of the jobs that are not in $S$ or not
kept, so that a cost of at most $D$ says that some schedule of at most $k$ jobs
keeps weight at least $W - D$, with $W$ the total weight. This is the weighted
question parameterized by the number $k$ of scheduled jobs: a schedule of at
most $k$ jobs and weight at least a target.

**Prescribed machine loads.** An instance is an instance $x$ of $s$ together
with a number $q_i$ for every machine $i$. A schedule is feasible if it is
feasible for $s$ and every machine $i$ runs exactly $q_i$ jobs, a job running
on a machine if a piece of one of its operations occupies it. The cost is the
cost in $s$; with the threshold $0$ and an objective that counts jobs not just
in time, the question is whether all jobs can be scheduled with these loads
(Das, Opler and Valla).
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: At most k scheduled jobs, and prescribed machine loads
type: definition
---
Two problems built on a problem $s$ of the family with operations, as used for
interval scheduling with eligible machine sets (lax-767944).

A job is *kept* by a schedule if it is on time, for an objective that counts
late jobs, or just in time, for one that counts jobs not just in time; for the
other objectives no job is kept.

**At most $k$ scheduled jobs.** An instance is an instance $x$ of $s$ together
with a number $k$. A schedule is a schedule of $x$ together with a set $S$ of
at most $k$ jobs, the jobs it schedules; it is feasible if the schedule is
feasible for $s$. Its cost is the weight of the jobs that are not in $S$ or not
kept, so that a cost of at most $D$ says that some schedule of at most $k$ jobs
keeps weight at least $W - D$, with $W$ the total weight. This is the weighted
question parameterized by the number $k$ of scheduled jobs: a schedule of at
most $k$ jobs and weight at least a target.

**Prescribed machine loads.** An instance is an instance $x$ of $s$ together
with a number $q_i$ for every machine $i$. A schedule is feasible if it is
feasible for $s$ and every machine $i$ runs exactly $q_i$ jobs, a job running
on a machine if a piece of one of its operations occupies it. The cost is the
cost in $s$; with the threshold $0$ and an objective that counts jobs not just
in time, the question is whether all jobs can be scheduled with these loads
(Das, Opler and Valla).
-/

namespace Lax434175.Wrappers
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

variable (s : Spec OperationsFamily.family)

/-- The weight of a job. -/
def weight (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.weight (K := Operations.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The due date of a job. -/
def due (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s) (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : ℕ :=
  Objectives.dueDate (K := Operations.kernel) s.objective x.objectiveData j

/-- The job is kept: on time for an objective counting late jobs, just in
time for one counting jobs not just in time, and never otherwise. -/
def Kept (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s) (σ : Operations.Sched x.base)
    (j : Fin x.base.jobs) : Prop :=
  match Objectives.kind s.objective with
  | .late => Operations.kernel.completion x.base σ j ≤ (due s x j : NNRat)
  | .notJustInTime => Operations.kernel.completion x.base σ j = (due s x j : NNRat)
  | _ => False

open Classical in
/-- At most `k` scheduled jobs: the instance carries `k`, a schedule names the
at most `k` jobs it schedules, and the cost is the weight of the jobs not
scheduled or not kept. -/
noncomputable def atMostScheduled : Problem where
  Inst := Inst OperationsFamily.family s × ℕ
  Sched x := Operations.Sched x.1.base × Finset (Fin x.1.base.jobs)
  feasible x σ := (problem _ s).feasible x.1 σ.1 ∧ σ.2.card ≤ x.2
  cost x σ := ∑ j, (weight s x.1 j : ℚ) * if j ∈ σ.2 ∧ Kept s x.1 σ.1 j then 0 else 1

/-- The jobs that run on a machine. -/
def jobsOn (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s) (σ : Operations.Sched x.base)
    (i : Fin x.base.machines) : Set (Fin x.base.jobs) :=
  {j | ∃ k, Operations.Occupies σ ⟨j, k⟩ i}

/-- Prescribed machine loads: the instance carries a number of jobs for every
machine, and a feasible schedule runs exactly that many jobs on every machine. -/
def prescribedLoads : Problem where
  Inst := (x : Inst OperationsFamily.family s) × (Fin x.base.machines → ℕ)
  Sched x := Operations.Sched x.1.base
  feasible x σ := (problem _ s).feasible x.1 σ ∧
    ∀ i, Set.ncard (jobsOn s x.1 σ i) = x.2 i
  cost x σ := (problem _ s).cost x.1 σ

end Lax434175.Wrappers

concepts.title: Open questions of The Scheduling Zoo
concepts.description:
The 258 questions the zoo's data leaves open, each as two competing
propositions about a reading of the problem: `yes` and `no`. A question is posed
only where the data shows a gap: an open problem the zoo lists, a problem with
neither hardness nor an algorithm after carrying results along the arrows, an
NP-hard problem neither strongly hard nor pseudo-polynomial, or a parameter in XP
with neither fixed-parameter tractability nor hardness. Both sides of a question
cannot be proved unless P = NP, or W[t] = FPT for the parameterized questions
(`ZooOpen.exclusive_fpt`).

import Lax434175.ZooParallel
