/-!
---
title: Open questions of The Scheduling Zoo
type: theorem
---
The 258 questions the zoo's data leaves open, each as two competing
propositions about a reading of the problem: `yes` and `no`. A question is posed
only where the data shows a gap: an open problem the zoo lists, a problem with
neither hardness nor an algorithm after carrying results along the arrows, an
NP-hard problem neither strongly hard nor pseudo-polynomial, or a parameter in XP
with neither fixed-parameter tractability nor hardness. Both sides of a question
cannot be proved unless P = NP, or W[t] = FPT for the parameterized questions
(`ZooOpen.exclusive_fpt`).
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooOpen
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters
open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions

/-- **Theorem.** Both sides of a parameterized question cannot hold unless every
parameterized problem of W[t] is fixed-parameter tractable. -/
axiom exclusive_fpt {P : Problem} {R : PReading P} {κ : TParameter P} {t : ℕ} :
    IsFPT R κ → WHard R t κ →
      ∀ Q ∈ Lax496464.WH_B4_Hierarchies.W t, IsParameterized Q →
        Q ∈ Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions.FPT

/-- `1||ΣwjTj`, parameter pmax: Is 1||ΣwjTj fixed-parameter tractable for the maximum processing time pmax? It is for agreeable weights and times, and 1|pj=p|ΣwjTj is polynomial.

The yes side. Source: open problem 1 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p133_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p133) (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p133))

/-- `1||ΣwjTj`, parameter pmax: Is 1||ΣwjTj fixed-parameter tractable for the maximum processing time pmax? It is for agreeable weights and times, and 1|pj=p|ΣwjTj is polynomial.

The no side. Source: open problem 1 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p133_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p133) 1 (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p133))

/-- `1|prec|ΣwjCj`, parameter D−LP: Does 1|prec|ΣwjCj have a polynomial kernel in the gap between the optimum and the lower bound of its natural LP relaxation? The problem is a special case of Weighted Vertex Cover, which has one.

The yes side. Source: open problem 2 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p15_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  PolyKernel (R.at ZooParallel.p15) (Ops.gapLP ZooParallel.p15)

/-- `1|prec|ΣwjCj`, parameter D−LP: Does 1|prec|ΣwjCj have a polynomial kernel in the gap between the optimum and the lower bound of its natural LP relaxation? The problem is a special case of Weighted Vertex Cover, which has one.

The no side. Source: open problem 2 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p15_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  ¬ PolyKernel (R.at ZooParallel.p15) (Ops.gapLP ZooParallel.p15)

/-- `1|rj|ΣUj`, parameter pmax: Are 1|rj|ΣUj and 1|rj|ΣwjUj W[1]-hard for the maximum processing time pmax? Not even membership in XP is known.

The yes side. Source: open problem 3 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p252_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p252) (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p252))

/-- `1|rj|ΣUj`, parameter pmax: Are 1|rj|ΣUj and 1|rj|ΣwjUj W[1]-hard for the maximum processing time pmax? Not even membership in XP is known.

The no side. Source: open problem 3 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p252_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p252) 1 (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p252))

/-- `1|rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter pmax: Are 1|rj|ΣUj and 1|rj|ΣwjUj W[1]-hard for the maximum processing time pmax? Not even membership in XP is known.

The yes side. Source: open problem 3 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p237_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p237) (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p237))

/-- `1|rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter pmax: Are 1|rj|ΣUj and 1|rj|ΣwjUj W[1]-hard for the maximum processing time pmax? Not even membership in XP is known.

The no side. Source: open problem 3 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p237_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p237) 1 (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p237))

/-- `1|forbidden-times|Cmax`, parameter τ: Is makespan minimization on a single machine with τ forbidden start and end times fixed-parameter tractable for τ? It is solvable in time n^O(τ), and in polynomial time for constant τ even when the number of jobs of each length is written in binary.

The yes side. Source: open problem 4 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p253_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p253) (lift (Ops.tau ZooParallel.p253))

/-- `1|forbidden-times|Cmax`, parameter τ: Is makespan minimization on a single machine with τ forbidden start and end times fixed-parameter tractable for τ? It is solvable in time n^O(τ), and in polynomial time for constant τ even when the number of jobs of each length is written in binary.

The no side. Source: open problem 4 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p253_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p253) 1 (lift (Ops.tau ZooParallel.p253))

/-- `P|HM|Cmax`, parameter #p: Is P||Cmax with the high-multiplicity encoding fixed-parameter tractable for the number p̄ of distinct processing times? It is polynomial for constant p̄, and a fixed-parameter algorithm needs an output schedule that is not listed machine by machine.

The yes side. Source: open problem 5 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p254_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p254) (lift (Ops.numP ZooParallel.p254))

/-- `P|HM|Cmax`, parameter #p: Is P||Cmax with the high-multiplicity encoding fixed-parameter tractable for the number p̄ of distinct processing times? It is polynomial for constant p̄, and a fixed-parameter algorithm needs an output schedule that is not listed machine by machine.

The no side. Source: open problem 5 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p254_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p254) 1 (lift (Ops.numP ZooParallel.p254))

/-- `P3|prec;pj=1|Cmax`, parameter width: Is P3|prec;pj=1|Cmax fixed-parameter tractable for the width of the partial order? A negative answer settles a question of Garey and Johnson; the slight generalizations are W[2]-hard.

The yes side. Source: open problem 6 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p255_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p255) (lift (Ops.width ZooParallel.p255))

/-- `P3|prec;pj=1|Cmax`, parameter width: Is P3|prec;pj=1|Cmax fixed-parameter tractable for the width of the partial order? A negative answer settles a question of Garey and Johnson; the slight generalizations are W[2]-hard.

The no side. Source: open problem 6 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p255_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p255) 1 (lift (Ops.width ZooParallel.p255))

/-- `P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: Are P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? Their complexity is open when the number of machines is part of the input.

The yes side. Source: open problem 7 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p29_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p29) (lift (Ops.m ZooParallel.p29))

/-- `P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: Are P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? Their complexity is open when the number of machines is part of the input.

The no side. Source: open problem 7 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p29_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p29) 1 (lift (Ops.m ZooParallel.p29))

/-- `P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj`, parameter m: Are P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? Their complexity is open when the number of machines is part of the input.

The yes side. Source: open problem 7 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p238_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p238) (lift (Ops.m ZooParallel.p238))

/-- `P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj`, parameter m: Are P|rj;pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj;pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? Their complexity is open when the number of machines is part of the input.

The no side. Source: open problem 7 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p238_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=

/-- `P|Mj|ΣwjZj`, parameter m: Is just-in-time scheduling on identical machines with machine sets (P|Mj;dj−rj=pj|ΣwjUj) fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? A positive answer would be a first step towards unrelated machines.

The yes side. Source: open problem 8 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p200_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p200) (lift (Ops.m ZooParallel.p200))

/-- `P|Mj|ΣwjZj`, parameter m: Is just-in-time scheduling on identical machines with machine sets (P|Mj;dj−rj=pj|ΣwjUj) fixed-parameter tractable for the number of machines? A positive answer would be a first step towards unrelated machines.

The no side. Source: open problem 8 of Mnich and van Bevern (2018).
-/
def ZooParallel_p200_q0_no (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=

/-- `P|rj;pmtn|ΣCj`, parameter #p: Are the three NP-hard preemptive problems P|pmtn;rj|ΣCj, P|pmtn|ΣUj and P|pmtn|ΣTj fixed-parameter tractable for the number of distinct processing times? With equal processing times they are polynomial.

concepts.title: Open parameters of The Scheduling Zoo
concepts.description:
The 911 pairs of a problem and a parameter that the zoo's data leaves open
and `ZooOpen` does not already ask about, as 1822 questions with a `yes` and a `no` proposition each.
A pair is open when the parameter is defined for the problem and not a
constant on it, the problem is NP-hard and not in P, and no result is
recorded for the parameter, carried along the arrows or implied by a special
case in which the parameter is a constant.

Each pair gets two questions: fixed-parameter tractable or W[1]-hard, and,
where XP is not known, polynomial for every fixed value (XP) or NP-hard for
one (para-NP-hard). Together they separate the three outcomes FPT, W[1]-hard
in XP, and para-NP-hard. Both sides of a question cannot be proved unless
W[1] = FPT or P = NP (`ZooOpen.exclusive_fpt`, `ZooOpenParams.exclusive_xp`).

import Lax434175.ZooParallel
import Lax434175.ZooParallelBatching
import Lax434175.ZooPreemptive
import Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShops
import Lax434175.ZooSerialBatching
import Lax434175.ZooShops
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters
import Lax434930.PolynomialTime
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Open parameters of The Scheduling Zoo
type: theorem
---
The 911 pairs of a problem and a parameter that the zoo's data leaves open
and `ZooOpen` does not already ask about, as 1822 questions with a `yes` and a `no` proposition each.
A pair is open when the parameter is defined for the problem and not a
constant on it, the problem is NP-hard and not in P, and no result is
recorded for the parameter, carried along the arrows or implied by a special
case in which the parameter is a constant.

Each pair gets two questions: fixed-parameter tractable or W[1]-hard, and,
where XP is not known, polynomial for every fixed value (XP) or NP-hard for
one (para-NP-hard). Together they separate the three outcomes FPT, W[1]-hard
in XP, and para-NP-hard. Both sides of a question cannot be proved unless
W[1] = FPT or P = NP (`ZooOpen.exclusive_fpt`, `ZooOpenParams.exclusive_xp`).
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooOpenParams
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters
open Lax496464.WH_A2_FptReductions

/-- **Theorem.** Both sides of an XP question cannot hold unless P = NP: a problem
NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter and polynomial for every fixed value
puts every language of NP in P. -/
axiom exclusive_xp {P : Problem} {R : PReading P} {κ : TParameter P} :
    InPFixed R κ → ParaNPHard R κ →
      Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP ⊆ Lax434930.PolynomialTime.P

/-- `P|rj|Cmax`, parameter pmax: Is P|rj|Cmax fixed-parameter tractable for pmax, or W[1]-hard? Nothing is known for pmax: it is not a constant here, and no special case of the data in which it is a constant is NP-hard.

The yes side. Source: the zoo's data, no result own, inherited or implied (scripts/open_params.py).
-/
def ZooParallel_p1_q0_yes (R : Reading OperationsFamily.family) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at ZooParallel.p1) (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p1))

The no side. Source: the zoo's data, no result own, inherited or implied (scripts/open_params.py).
-/

  WHard (R.at ZooParallel.p1) 1 (lift (Ops.pmax ZooParallel.p1))

/-- `P|rj|Cmax`, parameter pmax: Is P|rj|Cmax polynomial for every fixed value of pmax, or NP-hard for one? Nothing is known for pmax: it is not a constant here, and no special case of the data in which it is a constant is NP-hard.

/-- `P|rj|Cmax`, parameter pmax: Is P|rj|Cmax polynomial for every fixed value of pmax, or NP-hard for one? Nothing is known for pmax: it is not a constant here, and no special case of the data in which it is a constant is NP-hard.

-/

exclusive_xp : ∀ {P : Lax434175.Problems.Problem} {R : Lax434175.Results.PReading P} {κ : Lax434175.Results.TParameter P},
  Lax434175.Results.InPFixed R κ →
    Lax434175.Results.ParaNPHard R κ →
      Set.instLE.le Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP Lax434930.PolynomialTime.P
statements.doc:
**Theorem.** Both sides of an XP question cannot hold unless P = NP: a problem
NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter and polynomial for every fixed value
puts every language of NP in P.

concepts.title: The Scheduling Zoo, non-preemptive problems on parallel machines
concepts.description:
The 256 non-preemptive problems on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 251 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
242 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
9 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 0 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, non-preemptive problems on parallel machines
type: theorem
---
The 256 non-preemptive problems on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 251 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
242 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
9 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 0 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The

special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the

import Lax434175.BatchFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, parallel batching problems
type: theorem
---
The 35 parallel batching problems of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 10 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
10 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one.
Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the second list is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooParallelBatching
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

/-- The family of the problems listed here. -/
abbrev F := BatchFamily.family

/-- `1|pj=p;p-batch;rj|ΣwjCj` -/
def p0 : Spec F :=
  BatchFamily.spec .parallel (processingTimes := .equal) (release := .releaseDates)
    (capacity := .bounded) (objective := .sumWC)

import Lax434175.ZooParallel
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, non-preemptive problems on parallel machines
type: definition
---
The 381 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its non-preemptive problems on parallel machines that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooParallelResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooParallel

/-- `P||Cmax`: has an (1+epsilon)-approximation in time 2^O(1/epsilon^2)log^3(1/epsilon) + O(nlog n).

Klaus Jansen (2010). An EPTAS for scheduling jobs on uniform processors: using an MILP relaxation with a constant number of integral variables. https://doi.org/10.1137/090749451
-/
def p0_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : ℕ, SchemeWithin (R.at p0) (fun ε x => 2 ^ (a * ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ ^ 2) * Nat.log 2 ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ ^ 3 + (Ops.n p0 x) * Nat.log 2 (Ops.n p0 x))

/-- `P||Cmax`: under the exponential time hypothesis (ETH) there is no (1+epsilon)-approximation running in time 2^(1/epsilon)^1-delta +poly(n) for any delta>0.

L. Chen and K. Jansen and G. Zhang (2014). On the optimality of approximation schemes for the classical scheduling problem. https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611973402.50

Note: stated for one program reading ε, which the claim implies.
-/
def p0_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ETH → ∀ δ : ℚ, 0 < δ → ∀ d : ℕ, ¬ SchemeWithin (R.at p0) (fun ε x => 2 ^ ⌈((1 / ε : ℚ) : ℝ) ^ ((1 - δ : ℚ) : ℝ)⌉₊ + ((Ops.n p0 x) + 1) ^ d + inputSize (R.at p0) x)

/-- `P||Cmax`: is strongly NP-hard.

Garey, M.R. and Johnson, D.S. (1978). Strong NP-completeness results: motivation, examples, and implications. https://doi.org/10.1145/322077.322090
-/
def p0_r2 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p0)

/-- `P||Cmax`: has a deterministic O(2^O(1/epsilon log^2 (1/epsilon))) time algorithm.

Jansen, Klaus and Rohwedder, Lars (2022). On integer programming, discrepancy, and convolution. https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.2022.1308

Note: an approximation scheme; the dependence on n, not in the wording, is stated as a polynomial.
-/
def p0_r3 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ∃ a d : ℕ, SchemeWithin (R.at p0) (fun ε x => 2 ^ (a * ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ * Nat.log 2 ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ ^ 2) + ((Ops.n p0 x) + 1) ^ d)

/-- `P||Cmax`: for any delta>0 there is no PTAS in time 2^O((1/epsilon)^1-delta) under the exponential time hypothesis (ETH).

Chen, Lin and Jansen, Klaus and Zhang, Guochuan (2018). On the optimality of exact and approximation algorithms for scheduling problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcss.2018.03.005

Note: stated for one program reading ε, with a polynomial factor in n.
-/
def p0_r4 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ETH → ∀ δ : ℚ, 0 < δ → ∀ a d : ℕ, ¬ SchemeWithin (R.at p0) (fun ε x => 2 ^ (a * ⌈((1 / ε : ℚ) : ℝ) ^ ((1 - δ : ℚ) : ℝ)⌉₊) * ((Ops.n p0 x) + 1) ^ d + inputSize (R.at p0) x)

/-- `P||Cmax`: has a deterministic O(2^O(1/epsilon log(1/epsilon)loglog(1/epsilon))) time algorithm.

Berndt, Sebastian and Deppert, Max A and Jansen, Klaus and Rohwedder, Lars (2022). Load balancing: The long road from theory to practice. https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611977042.9

Note: an approximation scheme; the dependence on n, not in the wording, is stated as a polynomial.
-/
def p0_r5 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ∃ a d : ℕ, SchemeWithin (R.at p0) (fun ε x => 2 ^ (a * ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ * Nat.log 2 ⌈1 / ε⌉₊ * Nat.log 2 (Nat.log 2 ⌈1 / ε⌉₊)) + ((Ops.n p0 x) + 1) ^ d)

/-- `P||Cmax`: has an additive approximation scheme with additive error epsilon pmax in time O(m^O(2^1/epsilon· n^O(1/epsilon· 2^1/epsilon))).

Buchem, Moritz and Rohwedder, Lars and Vredeveld, Tjark and Wiese, Andreas (2021). Additive Approximation Schemes for Load Balancing Problems. None

Note: an additive scheme with error ε p_max; the running time, polynomial for each fixed ε, is not stated.
-/

  IsFPT (R.at p236) (tplus (Ops.pw p236) (lift (Ops.pmax p236)))

-/

  NoApproxBelow (R.at p244) ((7 : ℝ) / 6)

/-- `P|pj=1;prec;c=1|Cmax`: cannot be approximated below ratio 5/4 unless P=NP.

Hoogeveen, JA and Lenstra, Jan Karel and Veltman, Bart (1994). Three, four, five, six, or the complexity of scheduling with communication delays. https://doi.org/10.1016/0167-6377(94)90024-8
-/

Munier, Alix and König, Jean-Claude (1997). A Heuristic for a Scheduling Problem with Communication Delays. http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/opre.45.1.145

/-- `P|prec;c|Cmax`: has a randomized, expected polynomial time O(log c· log m)-approximation.

Davies, Sami and Kulkarni, Janardhan and Rothvoss, Thomas and Tarnawski, Jakub and Zhang, Yihao (2020). Scheduling with Communication Delays via LP Hierarchies and Clustering. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9317899/

concepts.title: Parameters of scheduling problems
concepts.description:
The parameters by which scheduling problems are commonly parameterized are
functions of an instance.

Over every kernel: the number $n$ of jobs and the number of distinct release
dates. On parallel machines and in shops: the number $m$ of machines, the
maximum processing time $p_{\max}$ and the number of distinct processing
times. For every objective value: the number of distinct weights and the
number of distinct due dates, where an unweighted value has the weights $1$
and a value without due dates the due dates $0$.

The first five depend on the kernel instance only. They are therefore
preserved by every embedding induced by a field-wise comparison and by every
reduction in place.

**Theorem.** Reading the data of an objective value with a more general
value changes neither the number of distinct weights nor the number of
distinct due dates.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Image
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Lattice.Fold
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod
import Lax434175.ParallelMachines
import Lax434175.Shops
import Lax434175.Objectives

/-!
---
title: Parameters of scheduling problems
type: theorem
---
The parameters by which scheduling problems are commonly parameterized are
functions of an instance.

Over every kernel: the number $n$ of jobs and the number of distinct release
dates. On parallel machines and in shops: the number $m$ of machines, the
maximum processing time $p_{\max}$ and the number of distinct processing
times. For every objective value: the number of distinct weights and the
number of distinct due dates, where an unweighted value has the weights $1$
and a value without due dates the due dates $0$.

The first five depend on the kernel instance only. They are therefore
preserved by every embedding induced by a field-wise comparison and by every
reduction in place.

**Theorem.** Reading the data of an objective value with a more general
value changes neither the number of distinct weights nor the number of
distinct due dates.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooParameters
open Lax434175.Kernels Lax434175.Modules

/-- The number of distinct values of a function on the jobs. -/
def distinct {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℕ) : ℕ := (Finset.univ.image f).card

/-- The number of jobs. -/
def jobs (K : Kernel) : K.Inst → ℕ := K.jobs

/-- The number of distinct release dates. -/
def releaseDates (K : Kernel) (x : K.Inst) : ℕ := distinct (K.release x)

namespace Parallel

/-- The number of machines. -/
def machines (M : ParallelMachines.Model) : M.kernel.Inst → ℕ := ParallelMachines.machines M

/-- The maximum processing time. -/
def pmax (M : ParallelMachines.Model) (x : M.kernel.Inst) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => Finset.univ.sup fun i => (M.inst x).p j i

/-- The number of distinct processing times. -/
def processingTimes (M : ParallelMachines.Model) (x : M.kernel.Inst) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.image fun q : Fin (M.inst x).jobs × Fin (M.inst x).machines =>
    (M.inst x).p q.1 q.2).card

end Parallel

namespace Shop

/-- The number of machines. -/
def machines : Shops.kernel.Inst → ℕ := Shops.machines

/-- The maximum processing time of an operation. -/
def pmax (x : Shops.Inst) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => Finset.univ.sup fun k => x.p j k

/-- The number of distinct processing times of operations. -/
def processingTimes (x : Shops.Inst) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.image fun o : Shops.Op x => x.p o.1 o.2).card

end Shop

/-- The number of distinct weights. -/
def weights (K : Kernel) (v : Objectives.Value) (x : K.Inst) (d : Objectives.Data K v x) : ℕ :=
  distinct (Objectives.weight v d)

/-- The number of distinct due dates. -/
def dueDates (K : Kernel) (v : Objectives.Value) (x : K.Inst) (d : Objectives.Data K v x) : ℕ :=
  distinct (Objectives.dueDate v d)

axiom weights_embed (K : Kernel) (v w : Objectives.Value) (h : Objectives.le v w = true)
    (x : K.Inst) (d : Objectives.Data K v x) :
    weights K w x (Objectives.embed h x d) = weights K v x d

axiom dueDates_embed (K : Kernel) (v w : Objectives.Value) (h : Objectives.le v w = true)
    (x : K.Inst) (d : Objectives.Data K v x) :
    dueDates K w x (Objectives.embed h x d) = dueDates K v x d

end Lax434175.ZooParameters

statements.signature:
dueDates_embed : ∀ (K : Lax434175.Kernels.Kernel) (v w : Lax434175.Objectives.Value) (h : Eq (Lax434175.Objectives.le v w) Bool.true)
  (x : K.Inst) (d : Lax434175.Objectives.Data K v x),
  Eq (Lax434175.ZooParameters.dueDates K w x (Lax434175.Objectives.embed h x d))
    (Lax434175.ZooParameters.dueDates K v x d)

weights_embed : ∀ (K : Lax434175.Kernels.Kernel) (v w : Lax434175.Objectives.Value) (h : Eq (Lax434175.Objectives.le v w) Bool.true)
  (x : K.Inst) (d : Lax434175.Objectives.Data K v x),
  Eq (Lax434175.ZooParameters.weights K w x (Lax434175.Objectives.embed h x d))
    (Lax434175.ZooParameters.weights K v x d)

concepts.title: The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive problems on parallel machines
concepts.description:
The 76 preemptive problems on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 65 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
60 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 5 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive problems on parallel machines
type: theorem
---
The 76 preemptive problems on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 65 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
60 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 5 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooPreemptive
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

/-- The family of the problems listed here. -/
abbrev F := OperationsFamily.family

import Lax434175.ZooPreemptive
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive problems on parallel machines
type: definition
---
The 95 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its preemptive problems on parallel machines that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooPreemptive

/-- `R|rj;pmtn|ΣwjCj`: has a polynomial time approximation ratio < 1.99971 by LP-rounding.

Sungjin Im and Shi Li (2017). Better Unrelated Machine Scheduling for Weighted Completion Time via Random sets from Non-Uniform Distributions. https://doi.org/10.1109/focs.2016.23
-/
def p0_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ∃ ρ : ℝ, ρ < (1.99971 : ℝ) ∧ Approx (R.at p0) (const ρ)

/-- `R|rj;pmtn|ΣwjCj`: has a 3-approximation algorithm when migration is allowed.

Skutella, Martin (2001). Convex Quadratic and Semidefinite Programming Relaxations in Scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1145/375827.375840

Note: preemption lets a job move between machines, as in the source.
-/
def p0_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  Approx (R.at p0) (const (3 : ℝ))

/-- `R|rj;pmtn|ΣwjCj`, parameter m: has a PTAS.

Afrati, Foto and Bampis, Evripidis and Chekuri, Chandra and Karger, David and Kenyon, Claire and Khanna, Sanjeev and Milis, Ioannis and Queyranne, Maurice and Skutella, Martin and Stein, Clifford and others (1999). Approximation schemes for minimizing average weighted completion time with release dates. https://doi.org/10.1109/sffcs.1999.814574

Note: a PTAS for every fixed value.
-/
def p0_r2 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  PTASFixed (R.at p0) (Ops.m p0)

/-- `1|prec;rj;pmtn|Lmax`: is in P.

Błażewicz, J. (1976). Scheduling dependent tasks with different arrival times to meet deadlines. None
-/
def p1_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p1)

/-- `1|prec;rj;pmtn|Lmax`: is in P.

Baker, K.R. and Lawler, E.L. and Lenstra, J.K. and Rinnooy Kan, A.H.G. (1983). Preemptive scheduling of a single machine to minimize maximum cost subject to release dates and precedence constraints. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.31.2.381
-/
def p1_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p1)

/-- `P|pj=p;pmtn|ΣwjUj`: is NP-hard.

Brucker, P. and Kravchenko, S.A. (1999). Preemption can make parallel machine scheduling problems hard. None
-/
def p2_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NPHard (R.at p2)

/-- `P|pj=p;pmtn|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (2000). Preemptive scheduling of identical machines. None

Note: in P for every fixed value.
-/
def p2_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InPFixed (R.at p2) (lift (Ops.m p2))

/-- `P|pj=1;pmtn;rj|ΣwjTj`: is in P.

  InP (R.at p3)

/-- `1|rj;pmtn|ΣCj`: is in P.

Baker, K.R. (1974). Introduction to Sequencing and Scheduling. None

def p4_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p4)

-/
def p4_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  RandomApprox (R.at p4) (const ((4 : ℝ) / 3))

/-- `1|pmtn;pj=p;rj|ΣwjUj`: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (1999). Polynomial time algorithms for minimizing the weighted number of late jobs on a single machine with equal processing times. https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1099-1425(199911/12)2:6<245::aid-jos28>3.0.co;2-5

  Approx (R.at p65) (const (2 : ℝ))

Afrati, Foto and Bampis, Evripidis and Chekuri, Chandra and Karger, David and Kenyon, Claire and Khanna, Sanjeev and Milis, Ioannis and Queyranne, Maurice and Skutella, Martin and Stein, Clifford and others (1999). def p67_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  Approx (R.at p67) (const (3 : ℝ))

/-- `1|rj;prec;pmtn|ΣFj`: has approximation ratio ge n^frac1(loglog n)^c for some c > 0 under ETH.

Janardhan Kulkarni and Shi Li (2018). Flow-time Optimization for Concurrent Open-Shop and Precedence Constrained Scheduling Models. https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX-RANDOM.2018.16

Note: the claim is for polynomial-time algorithms.
-/
def p68_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ETH → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ Approx (R.at p68) (fun x => ((Ops.n p68 x) : ℝ) ^ (1 / Real.log (Real.log (Ops.n p68 x)) ^ c))

Armbruster, Alexander and Rohwedder, Lars and Wiese, Andreas (2023). A PTAS for Minimizing Weighted Flow Time on a Single Machine. https://doi.org/10.1145/3564246.3585146
-/
def p70_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  PTAS (R.at p70)

/-- `1|online-rj;pmtn|ΣUj`: there is a randomized algorithm which is O(1) competitive against an oblivious adversary.

Kalyanasundaram, Bala and Pruhs, Kirk (1998). Maximizing job completions online. https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-68530-8_20

Note: measured on the kept weight (total weight minus the cost), as the source maximizes it.
-/
def p72_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, RandCompetitiveKept (R.at p72) (Ops.totalW p72) (const C)

/-- `P|online-rj;pmtn|ΣUj`: there is a O(1)-competitive determinstic algorithm.

Moseley, Benjamin and Pruhs, Kirk and Stein, Clifford and Zhou, Rudy (2022). A Competitive Algorithm for Throughput Maximization on Identical Machines. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-06901-7_30

Note: measured on the kept weight (total weight minus the cost), as the source maximizes it.
-/

  ∃ C : ℝ, DetCompetitiveKept (R.at p73) (Ops.totalW p73) (const C)

/-- `P|pmtn|ΣTj`: is NP-hard.

Kravchenko, Svetlana A. and Werner, Frank (2013). Erratum to: Minimizing total tardiness on parallel machines with preemptions. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10951-013-0313-5
-/

  NPHard (R.at p74)

concepts.title: The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive shop problems
concepts.description:
The 24 preemptive shop problems of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 17 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
15 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
2 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one.
Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the second list is a reduction of decision versions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive shop problems
type: theorem
---
The 24 preemptive shop problems of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 17 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
15 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
2 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one.
Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the second list is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShops
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

/-- The family of the problems listed here. -/
abbrev F := OperationsFamily.family

/-- `J|n=k;pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p0 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .constant)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `J|n=k;pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p1 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .constant)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `J2|n=3;pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p2 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 3)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `J2|n=3;pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p3 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 3)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O|pmtn;rj|Lmax` -/
def p4 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (objective := .lmax)

/-- `F2|pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p5 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F2|rj;pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p6 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F3|pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p7 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 3) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F2|pmtn|Lmax` -/
def p8 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .lmax)

/-- `O2|pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p9 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `F2|pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p10 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O2|chains;pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p11 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.chains, .zero⟩)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `O2|chains;pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p12 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.chains, .zero⟩)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O2|pmtn|ΣwjCj` -/
def p13 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumWC)

/-- `F2|chains;pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p14 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .flow)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.chains, .zero⟩)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `J2|pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p15 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O3|pmtn|ΣCj` -/
def p16 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 3) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O2|pmtn|ΣUj` -/
def p17 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumU)

/-- `J2|pmtn|Cmax` -/
def p18 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job)
    (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=k;pmtn|ΣwjUj` -/
def p19 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .constant)
    (release := .releaseDates) (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=k;pmtn|ΣwjTj` -/
def p20 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .constant)
    (release := .releaseDates) (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=2;pmtn|ΣwjUj` -/
def p21 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 2)
    (release := .releaseDates) (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=2;pmtn|ΣwjTj` -/
def p22 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 2)
    (release := .releaseDates) (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `O2|pmtn;rj|ΣCj` -/
def p23 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .pmtn) (shopType := .open) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- The problems with their names in three-field notation. -/
def problems : List (String × Spec F) := [
  ("J|n=k;pmtn|Cmax", p0),
  ("J|n=k;pmtn|ΣCj", p1),
  ("J2|n=3;pmtn|Cmax", p2),
  ("J2|n=3;pmtn|ΣCj", p3),
  ("O|pmtn;rj|Lmax", p4),
  ("F2|pmtn|Cmax", p5),
  ("F2|rj;pmtn|Cmax", p6),
  ("F3|pmtn|Cmax", p7),
  ("F2|pmtn|Lmax", p8),
  ("O2|pmtn|ΣCj", p9),
  ("F2|pmtn|ΣCj", p10),
  ("O2|chains;pmtn|Cmax", p11),
  ("O2|chains;pmtn|ΣCj", p12),
  ("O2|pmtn|ΣwjCj", p13),
  ("F2|chains;pmtn|Cmax", p14),
  ("J2|pmtn|ΣCj", p15),
  ("O3|pmtn|ΣCj", p16),
  ("O2|pmtn|ΣUj", p17),
  ("J2|pmtn|Cmax", p18),
  ("J|prec;rj;n=k;pmtn|ΣwjUj", p19),
  ("J|prec;rj;n=k;pmtn|ΣwjTj", p20),
  ("J|prec;rj;n=2;pmtn|ΣwjUj", p21),
  ("J|prec;rj;n=2;pmtn|ΣwjTj", p22),
  ("O2|pmtn;rj|ΣCj", p23)]

/-- The relations that hold field by field: general problem, special problem. -/
def specialCases : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
  (p20, p1), (p18, p2), (p15, p3), (p6, p5), (p7, p5), (p8, p5), (p14, p5), (p18, p5),
  (p12, p9), (p13, p9), (p16, p9), (p23, p9), (p15, p10), (p19, p21), (p20, p22)]

/-- The relations that need a threshold step: general problem, special problem. -/
def thresholdReductions : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
  (p19, p0), (p20, p0)]

axiom specialCases_hold : ∀ e ∈ specialCases,
    SpecialCase (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

axiom thresholdReductions_hold : ∀ e ∈ thresholdReductions,
    Reducible (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

end Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShops

concepts.title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive shop problems
concepts.description:
The 29 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its preemptive shop problems that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShops
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, preemptive shop problems
type: definition
---
The 29 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its preemptive shop problems that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShopsResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooPreemptiveShops

/-- `J|n=k;pmtn|Cmax`, parameter m: is in Ppseudo.

Brucker, P. and Kravchenko, S.A. and Sotskov, Y.N. (1999). Preemptive job-shop scheduling problems with a fixed number of jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/pl00020906

concepts.title: The Scheduling Zoo, problems with restarts on parallel machines
concepts.description:
The 4 problems with restarts on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 4 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
2 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 2 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, problems with restarts on parallel machines
type: theorem
---
The 4 problems with restarts on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 4 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
2 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
0 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one. The 2 relations of the third list replace completion
time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooRestarts
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

/-- The family of the problems listed here. -/
abbrev F := OperationsFamily.family

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣCj` -/
def p0 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .restarts) (release := .online)
    (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjCj` -/
def p1 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .restarts) (release := .online)
    (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumWC)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣFj` -/
def p2 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .restarts) (release := .online)
    (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumF)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjFj` -/
def p3 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (interruption := .restarts) (release := .online)
    (machineCount := .atMost 1) (objective := .sumWF)

/-- The problems with their names in three-field notation. -/
def problems : List (String × Spec F) := [
  ("1|online-rj;restarts|ΣCj", p0),
  ("1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjCj", p1),
  ("1|online-rj;restarts|ΣFj", p2),
  ("1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjFj", p3)]

/-- The relations that hold field by field: general problem, special problem. -/
def specialCases : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
  (p1, p0), (p3, p2)]

/-- The relations that need a threshold step: general problem, special problem. -/
def thresholdReductions : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
]

axiom specialCases_hold : ∀ e ∈ specialCases,
    SpecialCase (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

axiom thresholdReductions_hold : ∀ e ∈ thresholdReductions,
    Reducible (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

/-- The relations through flow time: general problem, special problem. -/
def flowReductions : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
  (p2, p0), (p3, p1)]

axiom flowReductions_hold : ∀ e ∈ flowReductions,
    Reducible (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

end Lax434175.ZooRestarts

namespace Lax434175.ZooRestartsResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooRestarts

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣCj`: has a deterministic 3/2-competitive algorithm.

Johannes A. La Poutré (2005). Minimizing the total completion time on-line on a single machine,
using restarts. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgor.2004.10.001
-/
def p0_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DetCompetitive (R.at p0) (const ((3 : ℝ) / 2))

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣCj`: deterministic competitive ratio ge1.2108.

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p0_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DetLowerBound (R.at p0) (1.2108 : ℝ)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣCj`: randomized competitive ratio ge1.1068.

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p0_r2 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  RandLowerBound (R.at p0) (1.1068 : ℝ)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjCj`: deterministic competitive ratio ge1.2232.

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p1_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DetLowerBound (R.at p1) (1.2232 : ℝ)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjCj`: randomized competitive ratio ge1.1161.

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p1_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  RandLowerBound (R.at p1) (1.1161 : ℝ)

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣFj`: deterministic competitive ratio Omega(sqrtn).

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p2_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DetLowerBoundFn (R.at p2) (fun x => Real.sqrt ((Ops.n p2 x) : ℝ))

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣFj`: randomized competitive ratio Omega(sqrtn).

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p2_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  RandLowerBoundFn (R.at p2) (fun x => Real.sqrt ((Ops.n p2 x) : ℝ))

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjFj`: deterministic competitive ratio Omega(n).

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7
-/
def p3_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DetLowerBoundFn (R.at p3) (fun x => ((Ops.n p3 x) : ℝ))

/-- `1|online-rj;restarts|ΣwjFj`: randomized competitive ratio Omega(n).

Leah Epstein and
Rob van Stee (2003). Lower bounds for on-line single-machine scheduling. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00488-7

/-- `1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj` -/
def p19 : Spec F :=
  BatchFamily.spec .serial (release := .releaseDates) (capacity := .unbounded)
    (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `1|s-batch(∞)|ΣwjUj` -/
def p20 : Spec F :=
  BatchFamily.spec .serial (capacity := .unbounded) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `1|s-batch(b)|ΣwjUj` -/
def p21 : Spec F :=
  BatchFamily.spec .serial (capacity := .bounded) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `1|s-batch(b);rj|ΣwjUj` -/
def p22 : Spec F :=
  BatchFamily.spec .serial (release := .releaseDates) (capacity := .bounded) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- The problems with their names in three-field notation. -/
def problems : List (String × Spec F) := [
  ("1|prec;pj=p;s-batch|ΣCj", p0),
  ("1|pj=p;s-batch|ΣwjCj", p1),
  ("1|chains;s-batch|ΣCj", p2),
  ("1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣwjCj", p3),
  ("1|s-batch|ΣwjCj", p4),
  ("1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣwjCj", p5),
  ("1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣwjUj", p6),
  ("1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣTj", p7),
  ("1|s-batch|ΣTj", p8),
  ("1|s-batch|ΣUj", p9),
  ("1|s-batch|ΣwjUj", p10),
  ("1|s-batch|ΣCj", p11),
  ("1|pj=p;s-batch|ΣwjUj", p12),
  ("1|prec;s-batch|ΣCj", p13),
  ("1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣUj", p14),
  ("1|s-batch;rj|Lmax", p15),
  ("1|s-batch;rj|ΣCj", p16),
  ("1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣTj", p17),
  ("1|prec;s-batch|Lmax", p18),
  ("1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj", p19),
  ("1|s-batch(∞)|ΣwjUj", p20),
  ("1|s-batch(b)|ΣwjUj", p21),
  ("1|s-batch(b);rj|ΣwjUj", p22)]

/-- The relations that hold field by field: general problem, special problem. -/
def specialCases : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
  (p13, p0), (p4, p1), (p5, p1), (p13, p2), (p10, p9), (p2, p11), (p4, p11), (p8, p11),
  (p16, p11), (p6, p12), (p10, p12), (p22, p19), (p10, p20), (p19, p20), (p21, p20), (p22, p21)]

/-- The relations that need a threshold step: general problem, special problem. -/
def thresholdReductions : List (Spec F × Spec F) := [
]

axiom specialCases_hold : ∀ e ∈ specialCases,
    SpecialCase (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

axiom thresholdReductions_hold : ∀ e ∈ thresholdReductions,
    Reducible (problem F e.2) (problem F e.1)

end Lax434175.ZooSerialBatching

concepts.description:

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.ZooSerialBatching
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, serial batching problems
type: definition
---
The 33 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its serial batching problems that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooSerialBatchingResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooSerialBatching

/-- `1|prec;pj=p;s-batch|ΣCj`: is in P.

Albers, S. and Brucker, P. (1993). The complexity of one-machine batching problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218x(93)90085-3
-/
def p0_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p0)

/-- `1|pj=p;s-batch|ΣwjCj`: is in P.

Albers, S. and Brucker, P. (1993). The complexity of one-machine batching problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218x(93)90085-3
-/
def p1_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p1)

/-- `1|chains;s-batch|ΣCj`: is NP-hard.

Albers, S. and Brucker, P. (1993). The complexity of one-machine batching problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218x(93)90085-3
-/
def p2_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NPHard (R.at p2)

/-- `1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣwjCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Albers, S. and Brucker, P. (1993). The complexity of one-machine batching problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218x(93)90085-3
-/
def p3_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p3)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣwjCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Albers, S. and Brucker, P. (1993). The complexity of one-machine batching problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218x(93)90085-3
-/
def p4_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p4)

/-- `1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣwjCj`: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (2000). Batching identical jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/s001860000088
-/
def p5_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p5)

/-- `1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣwjUj`: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (2000). Batching identical jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/s001860000088
-/
def p6_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p6)

/-- `1|pj=p;s-batch;rj|ΣTj`: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (2000). Batching identical jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/s001860000088
-/
def p7_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p7)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣTj`: is in Ppseudo.

Baptiste, P. and Jouglet, A. (2001). On minimizing total tardiness in a serial batching problem. https://doi.org/10.1051/ro:2001105
-/
def p8_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  PseudoPoly (R.at p8)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣTj`: is NP-hard.

Du, J. and Leung, J.Y.-T. (1990). Minimizing total tardiness on one machine is NP-hard. https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.15.3.483
-/
def p8_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NPHard (R.at p8)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣUj`: is in P.

Brucker, P. and Kovalyov, M.Y. (1996). Single machine batch scheduling to minimize the weighted number of late jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01303431
-/
def p9_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p9)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣwjUj`: is in Ppseudo.

Brucker, P. and Kovalyov, M.Y. (1996). Single machine batch scheduling to minimize the weighted number of late jobs. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01303431
-/
def p10_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  PseudoPoly (R.at p10)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣwjUj`: is NP-hard.

Karp, R.M. (1972). Reducibility among combinatorial problems. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4684-2001-2_9
-/
def p10_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NPHard (R.at p10)

/-- `1|s-batch|ΣCj`: is in P.

Coffman, Jr., E.G. and Yannakakis, M. and Magazine, M.J. and Santos, C. (1990). Batch sizing and job sequencing on a single machine. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf02248589
-/
def p11_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p11)

/-- `1|pj=p;s-batch|ΣwjUj`: is in P.

Hochbaum, D.S. and Landy, D. (1994). Scheduling with batching: minimizing the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://doi.org/10.1016/0167-6377(94)90063-9
-/
def p12_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p12)

/-- `1|prec;s-batch|ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Lawler, E.L. (1978). Sequencing jobs to minimize total weighted completion time subject to precedence constraints. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0167-5060(08)70323-6
-/
def p13_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p13)

/-- `1|prec;s-batch|ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Lenstra, J.K. and Rinnooy Kan, A.H.G. (1978). Complexity of scheduling under precedence constraints. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.26.1.22
-/
def p13_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p13)

/-- `1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣUj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Lenstra, J.K. and Rinnooy Kan, A.H.G. (1980). Complexity results for scheduling chains on a single machine. https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-2217(80)90111-3
-/
def p14_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p14)

/-- `1|s-batch;rj|Lmax`: is strongly NP-hard.

Lenstra, J.K. and Rinnooy Kan, A.H.G. and Brucker, P. (1977). Complexity of machine scheduling problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0167-5060(08)70743-x
-/
def p15_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p15)

/-- `1|s-batch;rj|ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Lenstra, J.K. and Rinnooy Kan, A.H.G. and Brucker, P. (1977). Complexity of machine scheduling problems. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0167-5060(08)70743-x
-/
def p16_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p16)

/-- `1|chains;pj=1;s-batch|ΣTj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Leung, J.Y.-T. and Young, G.H. (1990). Minimizing total tardiness on a single machine with precedence constraints. https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.2.4.346
-/
def p17_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p17)

/-- `1|prec;s-batch|Lmax`: is in P.

Ng, C.T. and Cheng, T.C.E. and Yuan, J.J. (2002). A note on the single machine serial batching scheduling problem to minimize maximum lateness with precedence constraints. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0167-6377(01)00105-5
-/
def p18_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p18)

/-- `1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj`: is NP-hard.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9
-/
def p19_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NPHard (R.at p19)

/-- `1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter #d+#p: is W[1]-hard.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9
-/
def p19_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at p19) 1 (tplus (lift (Batch.numD p19)) (lift (Batch.numP p19)))

/-- `1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter #p+#r: is W[1]-hard.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9
-/
def p19_r2 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  WHard (R.at p19) 1 (tplus (lift (Batch.numP p19)) (lift (Batch.numR p19)))

/-- `1|s-batch(∞);rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter #d+#p+#w: is in P.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9

Note: in P for every fixed value.
-/

  InPFixed (R.at p19) (tplus (tplus (lift (Batch.numD p19)) (lift (Batch.numP p19))) (lift (Batch.numW p19)))

Note: in P for every fixed value.

  InPFixed (R.at p19) (tplus (tplus (lift (Batch.numP p19)) (lift (Batch.numR p19))) (lift (Batch.numW p19)))

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9

  IsFPT (R.at p20) (tplus (lift (Batch.numD p20)) (lift (Batch.numP p20)))

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9
-/
def p20_r3 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at p20) (tplus (lift (Batch.numD p20)) (lift (Batch.numW p20)))

/-- `1|s-batch(b)|ΣwjUj`, parameter #d+#w: is fixed parameter tractable.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9
-/
def p21_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  IsFPT (R.at p21) (tplus (lift (Batch.numD p21)) (lift (Batch.numW p21)))

/-- `1|s-batch(b);rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter #d+#p+#r: is fixed parameter tractable.

Hermelin, Danny and Mnich, Matthias and Omlor, Simon (2024). Serial batching to minimize the weighted number of tardy jobs. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-024-00818-9

The 327 shop problems of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 237 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
221 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more

16 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the

import Lax434175.OperationsFamily

/-!
---
title: The Scheduling Zoo, shop problems
type: theorem
---
The 327 shop problems of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a
specification, and the 237 relations of the zoo among them that are
derived here.

A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The
221 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more
special problem is a special case of the more general one. The
16 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the
decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more
general one.
Each pair lists the more general problem first.

**Theorem.** Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair
of the second list is a reduction of decision versions.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooShops
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Assembly

/-- The family of the problems listed here. -/
abbrev F := OperationsFamily.family

/-- `F2|no-idle;no-wait|Cmax` -/
def p0 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (waiting := .noWait) (idling := .noIdle)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F|no-idle;no-wait|Cmax` -/
def p1 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (waiting := .noWait) (idling := .noIdle)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F2|tj|Cmax` -/
def p2 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (machineSets := .shop .byPosition)
    (transportation := { shape := .job, robot := false }) (machineCount := .atMost 2)
    (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F2|pij=1;tj|Cmax` -/
def p3 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (processingTimes := .unit)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (transportation := { shape := .job, robot := false })
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .makespan)

/-- `F||Cmax` -/
def p4 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (machineSets := .shop .byPosition)
    (objective := .makespan)

/-- `O2||ΣCj` -/
def p5 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (machineSets := .shop .byPosition)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O2|fixj|ΣCj` -/
def p6 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (machineSets := .shop .fix)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O2|Mj|ΣCj` -/
def p7 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (machineSets := .shop .sets)
    (machineCount := .atMost 2) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `F|intree;pij=1|ΣCj` -/
def p8 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (processingTimes := .unit)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.intree, .zero⟩) (objective := .sumC)

/-- `O|pij=1;rj|ΣwjUj` -/
def p9 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (processingTimes := .unit) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `J|fixj;n=2|ΣwjUj` -/
def p10 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 2) (machineSets := .shop .fix)
    (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `J|fixj;n=2|ΣwjTj` -/
def p11 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .atMost 2) (machineSets := .shop .fix)
    (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `F|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjUj` -/
def p12 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (jobCount := .constant) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .sets) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `F|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjTj` -/
def p13 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .flow) (jobCount := .constant) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .sets) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩) (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `O|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjUj` -/
def p14 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (jobCount := .constant) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .sets) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩) (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `O|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjTj` -/
def p15 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (jobCount := .constant) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .sets) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩) (objective := .sumWT)

/-- `O|pij=1;intree|Lmax` -/
def p16 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (processingTimes := .unit)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.intree, .zero⟩) (objective := .lmax)

/-- `O2|pij=1;prec;rj|Lmax` -/
def p17 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .open) (processingTimes := .unit) (release := .releaseDates)
    (machineSets := .shop .byPosition) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩) (machineCount := .atMost 2)
    (objective := .lmax)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=k;no-wait|ΣwjUj` -/
def p18 : Spec F :=
  OperationsFamily.spec (shopType := .job) (jobCount := .constant) (waiting := .noWait)
    (release := .releaseDates) (machineSets := .shop .dedicated) (precedence := ⟨.prec, .zero⟩)
    (objective := .sumWU)

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=k;no-wait|ΣwjTj` -/

concepts.title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, shop problems
concepts.description:
The 360 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its shop problems that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.ZooShops
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, shop problems
type: definition
---
The 360 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its shop problems that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooShopsResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters Lax434175.ZooShops

/-- `F2|no-idle;no-wait|Cmax`: can be solved in time O(n).

Jean-Charles Billaut and Federico Della Croce and Fabio Salassa and Vincent T'kindt (2017). When Shop Scheduling Meets Dominoes, Eulerian and Hamiltonian Paths. None
-/
def p0_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  DecidesWithin (R.at p0) (fun x => (Ops.n p0 x))

/-- `F|no-idle;no-wait|Cmax`: can be solved in polynomial time by a reduction to Eulerian path in directed multi-graphs.

Jean-Charles Billaut and Federico Della Croce and Fabio Salassa and Vincent T'kindt (2017). When Shop Scheduling Meets Dominoes, Eulerian and Hamiltonian Paths. None
-/
def p1_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p1)

/-- `F2|pij=1;tj|Cmax`: is strongly NP-hard.

Yu, W. and Hoogeveen, H. and Lenstra, J.K. (2004). Minimizing makespan in a two-machine flow shop with delays and unit-time operations is NP-hard. https://doi.org/10.1023/b:josh.0000036858.59787.c2
-/
def p3_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p3)

/-- `F2|pij=1;tj|Cmax`: is strongly NP-hard.

Yu, W. (1996). The two-machine flow shop problem with delays and the one-machine total tardiness problem. None
-/
def p3_r2 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p3)

/-- `F||Cmax`: has polynomial time approximation ratio ≥5/4.

Williamson, DP and Hall, LA and Hoogeveen, JA and Hurkens, CAJ and Lenstra, Jan Karel and Sevast'Janov, SV and Shmoys, DB (1997). Short shop schedules. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.45.2.288

Note: read as holding unless P = NP.
-/
def p4_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  NoApproxBelow (R.at p4) ((5 : ℝ) / 4)

/-- `O2||ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Achugbue, J.O. and Chin, F.Y. (1982). Scheduling the open shop to minimize mean flow time. https://doi.org/10.1137/0211058
-/
def p5_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p5)

/-- `O2|fixj|ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Achugbue, J.O. and Chin, F.Y. (1982). Scheduling the open shop to minimize mean flow time. https://doi.org/10.1137/0211058
-/
def p6_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p6)

/-- `O2|Mj|ΣCj`: is strongly NP-hard.

Achugbue, J.O. and Chin, F.Y. (1982). Scheduling the open shop to minimize mean flow time. https://doi.org/10.1137/0211058
-/
def p7_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  StronglyNPHard (R.at p7)

/-- `F|intree;pij=1|ΣCj`, parameter m: is in P.

Averbakh, I. and Berman, O. and Chernykh, I. (2005). The m-machine flowshop problem with unit-time operations and precedence constraints. None

Note: in P for every fixed value.
-/
def p8_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InPFixed (R.at p8) (lift (Ops.m p8))

/-- `O|pij=1;rj|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: is in P.

Baptiste, P. (2003). On minimizing the weighted number of late jobs in unit execution time open-shops. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0377-2217(02)00759-2

Note: in P for every fixed value.
-/
def p9_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InPFixed (R.at p9) (lift (Ops.m p9))

/-- `J|fixj;n=2|ΣwjUj`: is in P.

Brucker, P. (1995). Scheduling algorithms. None
-/
def p10_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p10)

/-- `J|fixj;n=2|ΣwjTj`: is in P.

Brucker, P. (1995). Scheduling algorithms. None
-/
def p11_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p11)

/-- `F|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: is in P.

Brucker, P. (1995). Scheduling algorithms. None

Note: the problem has k jobs for every fixed k, so the result is read for every fixed number of jobs and of m.
-/
def p12_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InPFixed (R.at p12) (tplus (lift (Ops.n p12)) (lift (Ops.m p12)))

/-- `F|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjTj`, parameter m: is in P.

Note: the problem has k jobs for every fixed k, so the result is read for every fixed number of jobs and of m.

/-- `O|Mj;prec;rj;n=k|ΣwjUj`, parameter m: is in P.

Brucker, P. (1995). Scheduling algorithms. None

Note: the problem has k jobs for every fixed k, so the result is read for every fixed number of jobs and of m.

-/

/-- `O|pij=1;intree|Lmax`: is in P.

Brucker, P. and Jurisch, B. and Jurisch, M. (1993). Open shop problems with unit time operations. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01415528
-/
def p16_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p16)

/-- `O2|pij=1;prec;rj|Lmax`: is in P.

Brucker, P. (1995). Scheduling algorithms. None
-/
def p17_r0 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=
  InP (R.at p17)

/-- `O2|pij=1;prec;rj|Lmax`: is in P.

Brucker, P. and Jurisch, B. and Jurisch, M. (1993). Open shop problems with unit time operations. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01415528

def p17_r1 (R : Reading F) : Prop :=

/-- `J|prec;rj;n=k;no-wait|ΣwjUj`: is in P.

Baptiste, P. and Brucker, P. and Knust, S. and Timkovsky, V. (2004). Ten notes on equal-execution-time scheduling. None

concepts.title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, problems outside the families
concepts.description:
The 8 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its problems outside the families that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434175.Rejection
import Lax434175.MachineCovering
import Lax434175.Results
import Lax434175.ResultParameters

/-!
---
title: Results of The Scheduling Zoo, problems outside the families
type: definition
---
The 8 results of The Scheduling Zoo on its problems outside the families that are
stated here, each as a proposition about a reading of the problem
(`Results.PReading`; for a family, `Results.Reading` at the problem's
specification): its words of instances and schedules and what an online
scheduler sees. Each names its source; where the proposition is weaker than
the wording, a note says what is left out.
-/

namespace Lax434175.ZooStandaloneResults
open Lax434175 Lax434175.Problems Lax434175.Results Lax434175.ResultParameters 

/-- `P||Cmin`: has a PTAS running in time O(c_epsilon n log m) where c_epsilon is a constant depending on the desired approximation ratio 1+epsilon.

Gerhard J. Woeginger (1997). A polynomial-time approximation scheme for maximizing the minimum machine completion time. http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167637796000557

Note: a maximization problem: value at least 1 - ε times the optimum.
-/
def cover_r0 (R : PReading MachineCovering.problem) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℚ → ℕ, SchemeMaxWithin R (fun ε x => f ε * (Cover.n x) * Nat.log 2 (Cover.m x))

/-- `1|Σ_j∈reject ej≤B|ΣCj`: is NP-hard.

Danny Hermelin and Michael Pinedo and Dvir Shabtay and Nimrod Talmon (2019). On the parameterized tractability of single machine scheduling with rejection. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2018.07.038
-/
def reject_r0 (R : PReading Rejection.problem) : Prop :=
  NPHard R

/-- `1|Σ_j∈reject ej≤B|ΣCj`: is in Ppseudo.

Danny Hermelin and Michael Pinedo and Dvir Shabtay and Nimrod Talmon (2019). On the parameterized tractability of single machine scheduling with rejection. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2018.07.038
-/
def reject_r1 (R : PReading Rejection.problem) : Prop :=
  PseudoPoly R

/-- `1|Σ_j∈reject ej≤B|ΣCj`, parameter #accept: is W[1]-hard.

Danny Hermelin and Michael Pinedo and Dvir Shabtay and Nimrod Talmon (2019). On the parameterized tractability of single machine scheduling with rejection. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2018.07.038
-/
def reject_r2 (R : PReading Rejection.problem) : Prop :=

/-- `1|Σ_j∈reject ej≤B|ΣCj`, parameter #p: is fixed parameter tractable.

Danny Hermelin and Michael Pinedo and Dvir Shabtay and Nimrod Talmon (2019). On the parameterized tractability of single machine scheduling with rejection. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2018.07.038
-/
def reject_r3 (R : PReading Rejection.problem) : Prop :=
  IsFPT R (lift (Reject.numP))

-/
def reject_r6 (R : PReading Rejection.problem) : Prop :=
  IsFPT R (lift (Reject.emax))
